author: gribbs
body:
## Summary

`procure login` printed the OAuth **client_id and client_secret in plaintext** to stderr on a failed token request. Procurify echoes the request body back inside its 401 error response, and `fetchToken` embedded that raw body into the `OAuthError` message/`.body`, which `handleError` then prints.

## Changes

- Add `sanitizeResponseText()` in `lib/oauth.js` that redacts `client_id`, `client_secret`, and token/password/assertion fields before any response body is surfaced in an error. JSON bodies are parsed and masked structurally; non-JSON falls back to regex redaction.
- Masking preserves the last 4 chars (e.g. `***ibAN`) so output stays diagnosable and still lines up with Procurify's own "client_id ending in ibAN" hint.
- Applied to both the non-2xx and unparseable-body error paths.
- Add a regression test asserting the full client id and secret never appear in `err.message` or `err.body`.

Before vs after (same failing login):

\`\`\`
before: "client_id":"nIeayneGllGyilEeFkKhBzvgFZIwibAN","client_secret":"<plaintext>"
after:  "client_id":"***ibAN","client_secret":"***Yldv"
\`\`\`

Note: the `--debug` log line was already masked; this closes the remaining leak in the error body.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx jest` — 136 tests pass (incl. new redaction test)
- [x] `npx eslint lib/oauth.js test/oauth.test.js` — clean
- [x] Manual: `procure login --profile sandbox` no longer prints plaintext credentials

author: jsboige
body:
## Summary
Fix 6 error cells in Framework_Composite_EMATrend/quantbook_composite_research.ipynb caused by MultiIndex Symbol lookup failure.

## Root Cause
`qb.history(qb.securities.keys(), ...)` returns a DataFrame with Symbol objects as MultiIndex level 0. When the code does `history.loc[qb.symbol(ticker)]`, the PandasMapper fails to match the Symbol object, throwing `KeyError: No key found for either mapped or original key`.

## Fix
1. **Cell 1**: Import `datetime` before `AlgorithmImports` try/except for local execution
2. **Cell 5**: Per-ticker `qb.history(ticker, ...)` instead of batch `qb.history(keys)` — avoids MultiIndex entirely
3. **Cell 7/9**: Use `data[ticker]` dict instead of `history.loc[symbol]`
4. Local fallback via yfinance when QuantBook unavailable

## Validation
- Papermill: 9/9 code cells OK, 0 errors, 8.6s
- yfinance loaded 15/15 tickers (2516 bars each, 2015-2025)
- Results: Pearson correlation 0.604 (moderate), EMA30/Trend70 recommended
- No forbidden patterns, all execution_count set

## Scope
- 1 notebook: `Framework_Composite_EMATrend/quantbook_composite_research.ipynb`
- 4 cells source changed (cells 1, 5, 7, 9)
- 464 insertions, 210 deletions

Part of #1916 Phase 4. Follows PR #1991 (BTC-EMA-Cross).

author: stephhubka
body:
## Summary

Second round of spec updates following the API gap analysis. Reconciles the **Case details** spec with settled decisions and applies cross-page UI refinements. (Builds on #5, now merged.)

## Case details spec
- **Assignee — individuals only:** Picker assigns to an individual agent via type-ahead search only; commits immediately and emits assigned/reassigned events. Documents that queue assignment is out of scope for v1 — cases enter a queue only via auto-routing rules at creation, with manual queue-move flagged post-v1. The system-events "Case assigned to {queue name}" row is now explicitly auto-routing-only, never picker-triggered.
- **Status enum mapping:** New note mapping rep-facing labels to `CaseDetails.status` (New→NEW, Needs response→OPEN, Awaiting customer→PENDING, On hold→net-new/KAYAK-4922, Resolved→CLOSED, Permanently closed→PERMANENTLY_CLOSED). On hold must not collapse into PENDING. Adopted pending River's confirmation that nothing consumes OPEN/PENDING conflictingly.
- **On hold behavior (KAYAK-4922):** SLA clock pauses on entry and resumes on exit, preserving accumulated elapsed time (not reset), with rationale; pending River's confirmation the SLA engine supports pause/resume. On hold reportable as distinct from Awaiting customer/PENDING.
- **Restricted access:** Note that the read-only banner depends on a load-time write-access signal (net-new, ticketed, tied to Settings/Teams/Queues), degrading to error-on-write as a fallback.

## UI / visual
- Sidebar: orange "Updated" badges for Conversation window and Case details (new `.nav-chip--updated` class).
- Added a commented-out Figma functional-prototype callout to the Case details intro (mirrors Conversation window).
- Removed the inter-section divider line and tightened spacing between intro and first content section on both pages (the line came from the `.section.active + .section.active` rule; matched the Anatomy override).
- Header date bumped to June 1, 2026.

## Reviewer notes
- Two items are explicitly captured as pending River's confirmation (not open design questions): the OPEN/PENDING enum mapping and the On hold SLA pause/resume semantics.
- The Figma prototype callouts on both pages are committed but commented out until the prototype link is ready.

author: aakarkale
body:
## What

Reworks the "Get started" steps and adds an optional multiple-choice health questionnaire that feeds the AI recommendations. Also includes a small mobile-nav fix.

### 1. Reordered + merged "Get started" steps (`EmptyDashboard`)
1. **Upload lab reports** — now first; it's the core of the dashboard.
2. **Connect your health data or upload metrics** — the two old steps merged into one card with **both** CTAs ("Set up sync" → `/settings`, "Upload metrics" → `/upload`), so the user picks the path and lands on the right page.
3. **Health questionnaire** *(Optional)* — links to the new flow.

### 2. Optional MCQ health questionnaire
- **`lib/questionnaire.ts`** — 11 questions, all multiple-choice (single- or multi-select): activity level, diet, sleep duration, sleep quality, stress, smoking, alcohol, caffeine, diagnosed conditions, family history, medications. Single source of truth shared by the form, server action, and AI summary.
- **`components/questionnaire/QuestionnaireForm.tsx`** — one question at a time with a progress bar. Single-select **auto-advances**, multi-select has Next, "None" is exclusive — so the whole thing takes well under a minute. Back/Skip supported.
- **`/questionnaire`** page + **`saveQuestionnaire`** server action. Answers stored as JSONB on `profiles.health_questionnaire`. Demo account is view-only.
- Linked from the user menu.

### 3. Sharper AI recommendations
- `generateRecommendations()` now folds the lifestyle profile into the prompt, and the system prompt instructs Claude to tailor advice to the user's diet/sleep/stress/habits/conditions/family-history/medications (and not suggest what they already do).
- Demo profile seeded with sample answers so the demo shows the richer output.

### 4. Mobile nav scrollbar fix
- Added a reusable `.no-scrollbar` utility (WebKit + Firefox + Edge) and applied it to the nav's `overflow-x` strip, so swiping the nav on mobile no longer shows a white scrollbar. Still scrollable via touch/trackpad.

## Migration
- **Migration `0006_health_questionnaire.sql`** — adds `health_questionnaire jsonb` to `profiles`. ✅ **Applied to the production DB** (column confirmed present). No RLS change needed (existing `auth.uid() = id` policies cover it).

`typecheck`, `lint`, `build` all clean. Preview deploy linked by the Vercel bot below.

author: govinda777
body:
This PR introduces a significant architectural shift by transitioning the mandala generation from a rigid Cartesian / Bézier model to a mathematical engine based on Polar Coordinates (Polar Rose equation). 

The new approach allows the canvas to draw continuous, organic waves, providing options for both fluid (sine) and sharp (absolute sine) geometry. It eliminates the need for hardcoded collision checks and Cartesian bounds algorithms, resulting in a cleaner, more performant codebase that paves the way for deterministic "hash-based" generation in the future.

author: dawit-0
body:
## The problem

Otto already has 6 tabs, multiple tables, saved queries, and query history — but zero fast way to navigate any of it. As a database grows you end up clicking: tab → table list → scroll → click, or hunting through History to find that query you wrote yesterday. Every extra click is friction that gets in the way of exploring data.

## The feature: Command Palette

Press **⌘K** (Mac) or **Ctrl+K** (Windows/Linux) anywhere in the app and an instant search palette opens. Type a few letters and jump straight to what you need.

[command palette concept](https://i.imgur.com/placeholder.png)

### What you can find

| Group | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Navigate** | Overview, Schema, Data, Query Editor, Visualize, Ask Otto |
| **Tables** | Any table in the connected database, with column/row counts |
| **Saved Queries** | All saved queries, searchable by name, description, or SQL |
| **Recent** | Last 5 successful unique queries from history |

### How it works

- **Fuzzy search** — type `usr` to match `users`, `cust` to match `customers`
- **Character highlighting** — matched characters light up in accent color so you can see why a result matched
- **Full keyboard navigation** — ↑↓ to move, Enter to select, Escape to close
- **Instant load** — saved queries and history are fetched in the background when the palette opens
- **Smart deduplication** — recent queries deduplicate identical SQL so the list stays clean

### Selecting an item

- A **view** → switches to that tab
- A **table** → switches to the Data tab with that table open
- A **saved query** or **recent query** → switches to the Query editor with that SQL loaded

### Discoverability

A subtle **search button** with a ⌘K badge is added to the right side of the header toolbar so new users can discover the feature without relying on knowing the keyboard shortcut.

## Implementation

**New file:** `frontend/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx`
- Portal-rendered above all content (no z-index conflicts)
- Smooth fade + scale animation on open
- Fetches saved queries and history via the existing API client
- Click outside or Escape to close

**Modified:** `frontend/src/App.tsx`
- Global `keydown` listener for ⌘K / Ctrl+K (only when a database is connected)
- `handleCommandNavigate` callback that routes to the correct view + loads SQL/table
- Search button in the header

**Modified:** `frontend/src/styles/globals.css`
- All palette styles using existing CSS variables (dark theme, accent color)
- No new design tokens introduced

## Test plan

- [ ] Press ⌘K with a database connected → palette opens
- [ ] Press ⌘K with no database → nothing happens
- [ ] Type partial table name → table appears with column/row count
- [ ] Select a table → Data view opens with that table
- [ ] Type partial saved query name → shows in Saved Queries group
- [ ] Select saved query → Query editor loads with that SQL
- [ ] Select a recent query → Query editor loads with that SQL
- [ ] Click a navigation item → switches to that view
- [ ] Arrow keys navigate the list, Enter selects, Escape closes
- [ ] Click outside the palette → closes
- [ ] Click the ⌘K header button → palette opens

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [go.k6.io/k6/v2](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6) | `v2.0.0-rc1` → `v2.0.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/go/go.k6.io%2fk6%2fv2/v2.0.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/go/go.k6.io%2fk6%2fv2/v2.0.0-rc1/v2.0.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>grafana/k6 (go.k6.io/k6/v2)</summary>

### [`v2.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/releases/tag/v2.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/compare/v2.0.0-rc1...v2.0.0)

k6 `v2.0.0` is here 🎉!

k6 v2.0.0 is the final release of the v2 major version, completing the cleanup of deprecated APIs, old commands, and obsolete configuration options that was started with v2.0.0-rc1. If you were already running the release candidate, this release includes a handful of additional changes on top — they are marked with ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** throughout these notes.

Here's a glimpse of what's changed in this release:

- The Go module path has changed to `go.k6.io/k6/v2` — all extensions must update their import paths to be compatible with v2.
- Removal of all long-deprecated CLI commands and flags: `k6 login`, `k6 pause`, `k6 resume`, `k6 scale`, `k6 status`, `--no-summary`, `--upload-only`, and more.
- The `externally-controlled` executor has been removed — scripts using `executor: externally-controlled` will no longer run.
- Cloud run non-threshold aborts (aborted by user, system, timeout, etc.) now return exit code `97` instead of `0`.
- `options.ext.loadimpact` is no longer supported — use `options.cloud`.
- `k6/experimental/redis` module has been removed.
- The `k6 cloud script.js` positional form has been fully removed — use `k6 cloud run script.js`.
- A stack is now required for all `k6 cloud` commands — the previous fallback to the first available stack has been removed.
- The web-vitals library has been updated to v5.1.0, removing the deprecated FID metric.
- ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** easyjson has been dropped in favor of stdlib `encoding/json` — extension authors relying on easyjson-generated methods on k6 types must update.
- ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** The k6 HTTP API server no longer starts by default — pass `--address` to enable it.
- ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** New `k6 cloud project list` command to list Grafana Cloud k6 projects.
- ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** Cloud secrets are now automatically available in `k6 cloud run --local-execution`; use `--no-cloud-secrets` to opt out.

#### Breaking changes

These are changes that require you to update your scripts, CI/CD pipelines, or configuration files before upgrading.

##### Go module path changed to `go.k6.io/k6/v2` [#​5777](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5777)

Following the [Go module versioning conventions](https://go.dev/ref/mod#major-version-suffixes), the k6 module path has changed from `go.k6.io/k6` to `go.k6.io/k6/v2`.

Any extension or external package that imports `go.k6.io/k6` must update all import paths to `go.k6.io/k6/v2`. For the vast majority of extensions this is the only change needed — a mechanical find-and-replace across the codebase:

```
go.k6.io/k6/ → go.k6.io/k6/v2/
```

For example:

```go
// Before
import "go.k6.io/k6/js/modules"

// After
import "go.k6.io/k6/v2/js/modules"
```

##### Removed CLI commands [#​5653](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5653)

The following commands for controlling a running test have been removed. They have not been functional for most use cases since the REST API they relied on was limited to specific execution modes:

- `k6 pause`
- `k6 resume`
- `k6 scale`
- `k6 status`

**Migration:** There is no replacement. These commands relied on the `externally-controlled` executor, which has also been removed in v2.0.0 (see below).

##### Removed `externally-controlled` executor [#​5846](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5846)

The `externally-controlled` executor has been removed. It was legacy code from an older k6 Cloud architecture that allowed external systems to scale VUs and pause/resume a running test via the k6 REST API — the capability that `k6 pause`, `k6 resume`, `k6 scale`, and `k6 status` relied on.

**Migration:** There is no replacement. Any test script with `executor: externally-controlled` will fail to start. Migrate to a different executor based on the desired load profile (e.g., `ramping-vus`, `constant-vus`, `constant-arrival-rate`).

##### Removed `k6 login` command [#​5134](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5134)

The top-level `k6 login` command and its subcommands (`k6 login cloud`, `k6 login influxdb`) have been removed.

**Migration:**

- Replace `k6 login cloud` → `k6 cloud login`
- InfluxDB authentication is no longer configurable via a login command. Use environment variables such as `K6_INFLUXDB_*` to configure the InfluxDB output directly.

##### Removed `k6 cloud script.js` positional form [#​5624](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5624), [#​5912](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5912) *(completed in v2.0.0)*

The old positional-argument form `k6 cloud script.js` has been fully removed. In v2.0.0-rc1 it was changed to show help instead of running; in v2.0.0 the deprecated command handler itself has been removed entirely. The `run` subcommand has been the recommended path since `k6 cloud run` was introduced.

**Migration:** Replace `k6 cloud script.js` with `k6 cloud run script.js`.

##### Removed `--upload-only` flag [#​5844](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5844)

The `--upload-only` flag on the `k6 cloud` command has been removed.

**Migration:** Use `k6 cloud upload script.js` to upload a test without running it.

##### Removed `--no-summary` flag [#​5729](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5729)

The `--no-summary` flag has been removed.

**Migration:** Replace `--no-summary` with `--summary-mode=disabled`.

##### Removed `--summary-mode=legacy` [#​5730](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5730)

The `legacy` value for `--summary-mode` has been removed.

**Migration:** There is no direct equivalent — the new summary format is different from the legacy one. // Before

      name: "My Test",

};

## Summary

Implements Phase 1 of the dual-target (web + Tauri desktop) architecture by introducing a `DataService` abstraction layer that decouples frontend components from direct API calls.

## What Changed

**New files:**
- `lib/services/types.ts` — DataService interface with 5 core methods
- `lib/services/webDataService.ts` — Fetch-based implementation for web
- `lib/services/tauriDataService.ts` — Placeholder for Phase 3 (Tauri)

## Summary
A self-hostable Python web app that scans crypto for **alt / micro-cap pump potential** and **perp / whale activity**, behind a login. Public-data analytics / screener — not financial advice. Lives in `scanner/`, fully separate from the Pine indicator.

## What it does
- **Pump radar (DexScreener):** crawls search terms + boosted tokens, normalises each pair (volume, liquidity, price change, buy/sell counts, age), and ranks by a transparent **pump score** (volume acceleration vs its own 24h average, 1h buy pressure, momentum, turnover).
- **Rug/trap risk score:** flags low liquidity, thin liquidity vs market cap, very new pairs, sell-dominated flow, and already-pumped (+300% 24h) → LOW/MED/HIGH badge. Pump and risk are shown side by side on purpose.
- **Perp heat (Hyperliquid):** market-wide OI / funding / 24h change / day volume, no auth.
- **Whale tracking (Hyperliquid):** open positions for wallets you list in `HL_WHALE_ADDRESSES`.

## App
- FastAPI + Jinja templates, session login (creds from `.env`), background async scan loop (`SCAN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`), dashboard with three tables, JSON API (`/api/scan`, `/api/rescan`), `/healthz`.
- Config via `.env` (see `.env.example`): credentials, scan interval, chains, min liquidity, max pair age, whale addresses.

## Verified live (this environment, OPEN_INTERNET)
- Real scan cycle: **24 tokens scored, 230 Hyperliquid markets**, no errors. Risk heuristics behaved correctly (e.g. a +206% token tagged MED with "very new / already +300% (late)").
- All modules `py_compile` clean.

## Run
```
cd scanner && python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env   # set ADMIN_PASSWORD + SESSION_SECRET
python run.py          # http://localhost:8000
```

## Known limitations / next steps
- Single-user auth, in-memory store (no DB persistence yet) — Phase A MVP.
- I could not fully boot uvicorn inside this sandbox to click through the UI; the **scan/scoring/data layer is verified live**, the HTTP routing is standard FastAPI and compiles, but please smoke-test `python run.py` locally.
- Rug-detection is heuristic from market data only (no honeypot/LP-lock/mint-authority on-chain checks yet) — that's the recommended Phase B hardening before trusting micro-cap calls.

author: rosa-regional-platform-ci
body:
## Security Audit — aws-nuke-cf

**Date:** 2026-06-01  
**Auditor:** Automated security-audit-agent  
**Method:** Full static analysis of CloudFormation template, Containerfile, Makefile, shell buildspec scripts  
**Action required:** Triage each finding. This PR does not contain fixes — it communicates security issues for owner review.

> **Context:** This repository deploys aws-nuke as a scheduled CloudFormation stack to perform automated AWS account cleanup. The security stakes are extremely high: the CodeBuild execution role has AdministratorAccess, and a successful exploit could result in mass deletion of production AWS resources or permanent account compromise. This audit focuses on attack paths that could cause unintended resource deletion, privilege escalation, or bypass of the protection guardrails.

---

## CRITICAL Findings

### CRIT-1 — CodeBuild Role Has AdministratorAccess — Protection Relies Solely on Deny Statements

**File:** `template.yaml` line 139 (ManagedPolicyArns section)  
**Risk:** Any gap in the deny policy grants unrestricted access to the AWS account

```yaml
ManagedPolicyArns:
  - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess
```

The execution role is granted `AdministratorAccess` — the broadest possible AWS permission set. The protection model relies entirely on explicit deny statements in the `DenyDangerousActions` policy to prevent misuse. This is **inverted least-privilege**: the role can do everything by default, and safety depends on the completeness of the deny list.

**Why this is dangerous:** Deny statements must exhaustively cover every dangerous action, present and future. AWS adds new API actions regularly. Any newly added IAM action that should be denied but isn't (because it didn't exist when the deny list was written) is immediately available to the CodeBuild role. Historical examples include `sts:AssumeRoot`, `iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole`, and various organization-level actions added after initial deployment.

**Attack vector:**
1. A new AWS IAM action (e.g., `organizations:DeleteOrganization`) is added by AWS and not in the deny list.
2. A malicious or misconfigured aws-nuke config targets this action.
3. The CodeBuild role executes it, causing irreversible account-level damage.

**Mitigation:** Replace `AdministratorAccess` with an explicit allow list of only the IAM actions that aws-nuke actually requires to enumerate and delete resources. While this list is long, it is finite and auditable. Use AWS Access Analyzer with policy generation to derive the minimum required permissions from CloudTrail.

---

### CRIT-2 — Missing `iam:PassRole` Denial Enables Privilege Escalation Out of aws-nuke Context

**File:** `template.yaml` lines 193–208 (DenyDangerousActions)  
**Risk:** Attacker with CodeBuild shell access can escape the aws-nuke sandbox and run arbitrary code with AdministratorAccess

The deny policy blocks `iam:Create*`, `iam:Put*`, `iam:Attach*`, and `iam:Upload*` — but critically does **not** deny `iam:PassRole`. With `iam:PassRole` available:

**Attack vector (step by step):**
1. Attacker gains code execution inside the CodeBuild environment (e.g., via a compromised aws-nuke config that embeds a shell command, a malicious nuke binary in the container image, or a dependency vulnerability).
2. Attacker creates an AWS Lambda function using `lambda:CreateFunction` (not denied) and passes the CodeBuild role to it using `iam:PassRole`.
3. Attacker invokes the Lambda with arbitrary code payload.
4. Lambda executes as the CodeBuild role (AdministratorAccess) — **outside the aws-nuke process** and therefore outside aws-nuke's own protection filters.
5. Attacker now has unrestricted AdministratorAccess with no deny constraints.

**Mitigation:** Add the following to the deny policy:
```yaml
- Sid: DenyPrivilegeEscalation
  Effect: Deny
  Action:
    - iam:PassRole
    - lambda:CreateFunction
    - lambda:UpdateFunctionCode
    - glue:CreateJob
    - ec2:RunInstances   # prevents launching new compute that inherits the role
  Resource: "*"
  Condition:
    StringNotEquals:
      iam:PassedToService: codebuild.amazonaws.com
```

---

### CRIT-3 — TOCTOU Race Condition: Config Validated Then Modified Before Execution

**File:** `template.yaml` lines 315–325 (validation), 378–394 (sed/awk modification), 406 (execution)  
**Risk:** Validated config can be replaced or corrupted between validation and aws-nuke invocation

The buildspec follows this pattern:
1. **Line 321:** Validate that the config contains the target account ID (`grep -q "$ACCOUNT" /tmp/user-config.yml`).
2. **Lines 379–393:** Modify the config using `sed -i` and `awk` to inject protection filters.
3. **Line 406:** Execute `aws-nuke run --config /tmp/nuke-config.yml`.

Between steps 1 and 3, the config file is modified in place in `/tmp`. If a second process (possible in CodeBuild's Docker-based execution environment with writable `/tmp`) can replace the file during this window, the protection guardrails are bypassed.

Additionally, `sed -i` (step 2) edits the file in place without an atomic rename. If the sed command fails midway (disk full, process kill signal, OOM), the config file is left in a corrupt or partially modified state, and step 3 executes against a malformed config that may silently omit protection rules.

**Attack vector (S3 path):** If `CONFIG_URL` points to an S3 object, an attacker with `s3:PutObject` on the config bucket modifies the object between the CodeBuild `grep` validation (which reads the first downloaded copy) and execution. The `sed`/`awk` protection injection runs against the already-downloaded copy, so this particular race requires the download to happen twice — but if the buildspec is modified or if caching is involved, this window exists.

**Mitigation:**
- Compute a SHA256 hash of the config immediately after download and validate the hash before execution.
- Write the modified config to a new file (not in-place) and execute from that file.
- Use `set -o noclobber` to prevent file overwrites.

---

### CRIT-4 — Unsafe Config Download via `curl` Without Integrity Verification

**File:** `template.yaml` line 317  
**Risk:** MITM attack on HTTPS config download delivers malicious nuke config

```bash
curl -fsSL "$CONFIG_URL" -o /tmp/user-config.yml
```

The `-f` flag only causes curl to fail on HTTP 4xx/5xx responses — it does not provide any integrity verification. HTTPS protects against passive eavesdropping but not against a certificate-validating MITM (e.g., a corporate proxy with a trusted intercepting certificate, a compromised CA, or DNS hijacking targeting the config host).

A malicious config delivered here could:
- Remove protection filters → delete production resources
- Add accounts to target that shouldn't be nuked
- Override preset configurations

**Mitigation:**
- Require a SHA256 checksum parameter alongside `ConfigSourceUrl`. Verify it immediately after download:
  ```bash
  echo "${CONFIG_SHA256}  /tmp/user-config.yml" | sha256sum -c -
  ```
- Alternatively, require configs to be GPG-signed and verify the signature before use.
- Strongly prefer S3-hosted configs (which are authenticated via IAM) over HTTP URLs.

---

### CRIT-5 — CodeBuild Trust Policy Missing `aws:SourceAccount` Condition (Confused Deputy)

**File:** `template.yaml` lines 128–137  
**Risk:** Cross-account confused deputy attack — another account's CodeBuild project could assume this role

```yaml
AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
  Statement:
    - Effect: Allow
      Principal:
        Service: codebuild.amazonaws.com
      Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Condition:
        ArnLike:
          aws:SourceArn: !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:codebuild:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:project/${NamePrefix}-job
```

The trust policy uses `ArnLike` with `aws:SourceArn` but is missing `aws:SourceAccount`. AWS's own documentation for confused deputy prevention requires **both** conditions. `ArnLike` on a Source ARN may be bypassable

author: moviu
body:
## Summary
This PR improves animation performance and accessibility by introducing tier-dependent breathing scale curves and comprehensive support for the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query. The changes allow weaker devices to use simpler animation keyframes while respecting user accessibility preferences across the entire application.

## Key Changes

- **Tier-dependent breathing curves**: Added `breathe` property to `TierConfig` with two variants:
  - `BREATHE_RICH`: 9-point curve for high/medium tiers (full pulsing detail)
  - `BREATHE_LITE`: 3-point curve for low/off tiers (cheaper interpolation, same feel)
  - Reduces per-frame interpolation work on constrained devices

- **Improved device capability detection**: Enhanced `getInitialTier()` to check:
  - Data saver mode (`navigator.connection.saveData`)
  - Network speed (2G detection)
  - Hardware concurrency (CPU cores)
  - Device memory (RAM)
  - Starts low-end devices at 'low' tier instead of 'high' to prevent initial jank

- **Degradation path refinement**: Changed `low` tier to degrade to `off` (static) instead of staying at `low`, allowing genuinely struggling devices to fall back to fully static glows rather than stutter indefinitely

- **Reduced motion support**:
  - Wrapped app in `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">` to respect OS preference for Framer Motion
  - Added `prefersReducedMotion` check to disable auto-palette cycling
  - Palette changes snap instead of cross-fading when reduced motion is requested
  - Added CSS media query to disable CSS animations (status dot pulse, auto swatch spin) and collapse transitions to near-instant

- **GPU memory optimization**: Moved `will-change: transform, opacity` from base `.aurora-glow` to `.aurora-glow.is-animated` class, so static glows don't unnecessarily pin GPU memory

- **Improved comments**: Updated documentation to clarify the degradation strategy and device-specific constraints (iOS Safari GPU memory cap)

## Implementation Details

The breathing curves are now applied per-tier rather than hardcoded, allowing the animation to maintain visual consistency while reducing computational cost on lower tiers. The device detection logic runs once at startup to avoid unnecessary motion on devices that can't sustain it, complementing the runtime FPS monitor's fine-tuning.

## Summary
This PR implements critical fixes for role-based access control, adds missing project management endpoints, and establishes the RAG pipeline infrastructure with document processing and embedding services.

## Key Changes

### Backend - Role & Permission Fixes
- **Admin Guard & Extractors**: Updated `admin.guard.ts` and `extractors.rs` to include `"owner"` role alongside `"admin"` for `workspace:manage` permission
- **Tests**: Added unit tests in `extractors_tests` to verify owner/admin receive workspace:manage while member/viewer do not

### Backend - Project Endpoints
- **New Routes**: Added `GET /api/v1/projects/:id/chats` and `GET /api/v1/projects/:id/members` to projects.rs
  - `/chats` returns array of chats with message_count, is_pinned, last_message_at
  - `/members` returns array of project members with user_id, name, email, role
- **Document Endpoint Enhancement**: Modified `GET /api/v1/projects/:id/documents` to return `ProjectDocumentView` with `linked_at` timestamp and `chunk_count` field
- **Integration Tests**: Added comprehensive tests in `projects_test.rs` for chats list, members list, and instructions roundtrip

### Frontend - Project Workspace Component
- **Document Upload**: Added file input with upload state management (uploading signal, uploadError signal)
- **Instructions Form**: Implemented inline form for creating project instructions with trigger_mode selection
- **Data Binding Fixes**: Updated component to consume array responses directly (not wrapped objects) from backend endpoints
- **Spec Tests**: Added `project-workspace.component.spec.ts` with tests for newChat(), loadProjectData(), and saveInstruction()

### Frontend - Services & Layout
- **ProjectsService**: New service with projects signal and reload() method for workspace project list
- **AppShellComponent**: Integrated ProjectsService to populate sidebar projects on init
- **AppShellComponent Tests**: Added spec file with tests for component creation and project list loading

### Frontend - Auth & Guards
- **Admin Guard**: Updated to include `"owner"` in ADMIN_ROLES constant
- **Guard Tests**: Added test case verifying owner role grants admin access

### RAG Pipeline Infrastructure
- **Docker Compose**: Added `embedding` service (HuggingFace-based) and `document-processor` service (Rust worker)
  - Embedding service: 2GB memory limit, health check on /health endpoint
  - Document-processor: Polls database for pending documents, processes via embedding, indexes to Qdrant
  - Both services depend on postgres and qdrant health checks
- **Smoke Test Script**: Created `scripts/smoke-rag.sh` for end-to-end RAG validation
  - Tests registration → login → project creation → document upload → processing status polling
  - Validates chunk_count > 0 after processing completes
- **E2E RAG Job**: Added gated CI job (`e2e-rag-pipeline`) triggered by workflow_dispatch or `rag-e2e` label
  - Runs migrations, builds API and document-processor, validates smoke-rag.sh flow
  - Separate from main PR gate to avoid blocking on embedding availability

### CI/CD Updates
- **Workflow Name**: Updated to "CI - Fase 6 (Fixes + RAG Worker)"
- **Branch Triggers**: Added `claude/gifted-newton-BmT9l` to push branches
- **New Checks**: Added Fix1 (adminGuard owner role), Fix2 (projects routes), Fix3 (ProjectsService exists)
- **Smoke Tests**: Added Fix1 (GET /admin/health with owner token) and Fix2 (project flow: create, list chats/members)

### Environment Configuration
- **`.env.example`**: Added worker configuration variables (WORKER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS, WORKER_CONCURRENCY, MAX_RETRIES)

## Notable Implementation Details
- Owner role now has full workspace management permissions equivalent to admin
- Project endpoints return pure JSON arrays (not wrapped objects) for consistency
- Document processing is async via background worker with status polling
- RAG pipeline is gated in CI

author: teknium1
body:
## Summary
File/content searches that hit their time budget on a huge tree now return the partial results collected so far flagged as truncated, instead of failing hard or leaking the backend's timeout marker into the result.

Ported in spirit from [nearai/ironclaw#4211](https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/pull/4211), which changed IronClaw's glob walk so that exceeding its visited-entry budget returns partial results with `truncated: true` + a `limit_reason`, rather than erroring out with a `Resource` failure.

## What it solves
Before this, when `rg`/`grep`/`find` exceeded the 60s search subprocess timeout, the terminal backend returned exit code 124 with the partial stdout collected so far **plus** a trailing `[Command timed out after 60s]` marker. The search code didn't recognize 124 (it only guarded `rg` exit 2), so that marker got parsed as a phantom file/match line and the result carried no signal that it was incomplete. The model would see garbage or an empty-looking result and often retry the same doomed query.

## Architectural adaptation
IronClaw counts visited filesystem entries (`MAX_VISITED_ENTRIES`) as its budget; hermes-agent's equivalent budget is the per-search subprocess wall-clock timeout. Same contract — *degrade, don't fail* — different mechanism. The terminal backend (`tools/environments/base.py`) already preserves partial output on timeout (exit 124 + marker), so the fix is purely in the search layer: detect 124, strip the marker, keep the partial output, and flag it.

## Changes
- `tools/file_operations.py`:
  - `SearchResult` gains a `limit_reason` field, surfaced in `to_dict()`.
  - New `_search_hit_budget()` / `_strip_timeout_marker()` helpers on `ShellFileOperations`.
  - Wired into all four backends: `_search_files` (find fallback), `_search_files_rg`, `_search_with_rg`, `_search_with_grep`. A budget timeout sets `truncated=True` + `limit_reason="search_timeout"` and suppresses the now-pointless fallback retries (BSD-find / unsorted-rg). Genuine `rg`/`grep` errors (exit 2, no output) still hard-fail.
- `tests/tools/test_search_budget_truncation.py`: 14 new tests covering the helpers and all four backends (files, content, files_only, count modes), the no-retry behavior, and that the marker never leaks into results.

## Validation
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Search times out on huge tree | exit 124 unrecognized; `[Command timed out…]` parsed as a phantom file/match; no truncation signal | partial results kept; marker stripped; `truncated=True`, `limit_reason="search_timeout"` |
| Genuine `rg`/`grep` error (exit 2, no output) | hard error | hard error (unchanged) |
| Normal search | unchanged | unchanged |

- 14 new unit tests pass; 121 existing search/file-op tests pass.
- E2E verified against a real `LocalEnvironment`: a real subprocess timeout produces exit 124 + the marker, and the full `search(target="content")` path returns `error=None, truncated=True, limit_reason="search_timeout"` with a clean `to_dict()`.

Source PR: https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/pull/4211

body:
PPV events display only mechanical label-value metadata with no narrative content. This adds a provider plugin architecture that assembles standings, H2H history, and team form from multiple sources, then uses an LLM to generate a 2-sentence EPG description grounded exclusively in fetched facts.

## Context enrichment architecture (`services/ppv/context/`)

- **`base.py`** — `ContextDataProvider` ABC with `DataType` enum, `TeamContext`/`EventContext` dataclasses, and `settings_fields()` / `get_setting()` / `set_setting()` for per-provider credential management
- **`registry.py`** — priority-ordered provider dispatch with `coverage_report()` gap matrix
- **`cache.py`** — thread-safe TTL cache (standings 6h, H2H 24h, form 2h, notes 30min)
- **`assembler.py`** — iterates providers per data type with fallthrough on `None`
- **`prompt_builder.py`** — `=== FACTS ===` injection block; hallucination guard rejects any number in output absent from the facts block
- **`llm_client.py`** — OpenAI/Anthropic at temperature=0; falls back to mechanical description on validation failure

## Initial providers

| Provider | Priority | Coverage | Data types |
|---|---|---|---|
| ESPN | 10 | NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, MLS, Boxing, MMA | standings, H2H, form, notes |
| football-data.org | 15 | PL, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, CL, WC | standings |
| sportsipy | 50 | NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, NCAAF, NCAAB, MiLB | H2H, form |
| TheSportsDB | 90 | broad fallback | standings, H2H |

## Per-provider settings (`models/provider_settings.py`)

Provider credentials are stored in a dedicated `provider_settings` table (not global `Settings`), so adding a new plugin requires no DB migration or global config change. Each provider declares its own fields for UI rendering:

```python
class FootballDataProvider(ContextDataProvider):
    def settings_fields(self):
        return [{"key": "api_key", "label": "API Key", "type": "password", "required": True}]
    
    def get_standings(self, sport, league, teams):
        key = self.get_setting("api_key")  # reads from provider_settings table
        ...
```

LLM settings (enabled flag, provider, API key, model, base URL) live under a `LLMEnrichmentSettings` virtual provider — same storage and UI pattern, not registered in the provider registry.

## API surface

- `GET /api/ppv-enrichment/provider-settings` — all providers with field declarations and current values (passwords masked)
- `PUT /api/ppv-enrichment/provider-settings/<provider>/<key>` — save a value, validated against declared fields
- `GET /api/ppv-enrichment/coverage` — sport × data-type gap matrix

## Integration

Opt-in via `ProviderSettings.get("llm_enrichment", "enabled")` (off by default). Runs in the existing background detail-fetch thread after `_update_event_from_api`; sets `data_completeness = "enriched"`. `services/ppv/epg.py` uses `event.description` when set, falls back to label-value format.

送付履歴詳細の手動状態更新後も、元の一覧 filter 文脈へ戻れるようにします。

## 対応 Issue

Closes #1458

## 変更内容

- 詳細画面の `送付済みにする` / `送付失敗として記録` button に、既存の `safe_return_to_path` で検証済みの `return_to` を渡すようにしました。
- `DocumentDeliveryLogsController#update` の成功 redirect で、`return_to` が渡された場合は安全な戻り先を詳細 URL に引き継ぐようにしました。
- `return_to` がない既存の直接 update は従来どおり詳細 URL へ redirect します。
- request spec に、filtered list 由来の `q` / `status` / `delivery_type` を手動状態更新後も保持するケースと、不正な `return_to` が通常一覧へ fallback するケースを追加しました。

## 受け入れ条件との対応

- `status=draft` などの filtered list から詳細へ入り、手動状態更新後も詳細画面の戻り先が元の filtered list を指す
  - `return_to` hidden param と update 後 redirect の request spec で固定しました。
- `q` / `delivery_type` を含む戻り先も壊していない
  - `q: "DLV1"`, `status: :draft`, `delivery_type: :portal_link` を含む代表ケースを追加しました。
- 不正な `return_to` で open redirect や任意 path redirect にならない
  - `//example.com` が `document_delivery_logs_path` へ fallback する spec を追加しました。
- 送付済み / 失敗記録そのものの既存 behavior を変えていない
  - `status`, `sent_at`, `error_message` の更新 expectation を追加し、既存 spec も維持しています。
- request spec で filtered list から detail / update 後の戻り先を代表ケースとして固定できる
  - `spec/requests/document_delivery_logs_spec.rb` に追加しました。

## 変更範囲

- `app/controllers/document_delivery_logs_controller.rb`
- `app/views/document_delivery_logs/show.html.slim`
- `spec/requests/document_delivery_logs_spec.rb`

## 実施した確認

- GitHub compare: `main...feature/1458-delivery-log-return-to-update`
  - `ahead_by: 3`
  - `behind_by: 0`
  - changed files: 3
- ローカル test / lint は未実行です。この環境では GitHub HTTPS remote が `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` になるため、PR 作成後の GitHub Actions で確認します。

## リスク

- risk: low
- 既存の `safe_return_to_path` 境界を使い、戻り先保持だけに閉じています。DB schema、認可、visible scope、delivery type、送信 workflow、mailer 実送信、paging / export / bulk action は変更していません。

- 送付履歴一覧の redesign、bulk action、状態 enum 変更はしていません。

author: roeap
body:
## Summary

Replaces the pgcrypto secret-at-rest path (a single static AES key defaulting to the literal `"dummy"`) with Rust-side **envelope encryption**, and adds a **TTL cache** for credential vending. This code is unreleased, so the legacy path is removed outright — no dual-read, migration shim, or backwards compatibility.

### Envelope encryption (`crates/common/src/services/encryption.rs`)
- `KeyProvider` trait wraps/unwraps per-secret data keys (DEKs); the signature is async so external key stores (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, GCP KMS) can plug in later without changing callers.
- `LocalKeyProvider` holds an **active KEK plus retired KEKs**, enabling rotation.
- `EnvelopeEncryptor` seals each value under a fresh AES-256-GCM DEK (RustCrypto), wraps the DEK under the active KEK, and stores a **self-describing, versioned blob** (`version | kek_id | nonce | wrapped_dek | ciphertext`). The secret name is bound as AEAD associated data; key buffers are zeroized.
- `rewrap` re-keys a DEK under the active KEK **without touching the value ciphertext** (cheap rotation).

### Wiring
- **Simplified `SecretManager`** from 5 methods to 3 (`put_secret`/`get_secret`/`delete_secret`): dropped the never-called version-by-uuid method and the always-discarded `Uuid`; collapsed create/update into an idempotent upsert.
- **Postgres and in-memory stores** both seal/open via the encryptor, so the DB never sees plaintext and dev/test matches prod. Migration drops the pgcrypto extension and adds a `unique` constraint on `secrets.name`.
- **Lazy KEK rotation on read:** `get_secret` re-wraps a secret under the active KEK (best-effort write-back) when it was sealed under a retired one. The embedded `kek_id` already drives correct decrypt-by-write-time-version.
- **CLI `encryption` config** (backend-agnostic): active + retired KEKs, 32-byte base64 material, built at startup. Missing/invalid keys fail fast — no dummy fallback.

### Credential-vending cache (`crates/server/src/services/credential_vending.rs`)
- Caches vended temporary credentials by `(credential material, url, operation)` until shortly before expiry, avoiding a cloud round-trip (Azure AAD/Storage, AWS STS) on every request. Hashing the credential content invalidates the entry on rotation. (TTL cache, not strict single-flight — concurrent cold misses may each vend once.)

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test` on common/server/cli/postgres — encryption round-trip, AAD/tamper rejection, rewrap, multi-KEK, lazy-rewrap-on-read, store round-trips asserting ciphertext-not-plaintext, vending cache hit/expiry, config build/reject
- [x] `just integration` recorded suite — 18/18 journeys pass (incl. credential + temporary-credential flows)
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace` clean (no new warnings); `cargo fmt` applied
- [x] Regenerated offline `.sqlx` query cache for the changed secret queries
- [x] No generated files touched — the `SecretManager` simplification needed no codegen regeneration

## Follow-ups
- #152 Azure Key Vault `KeyProvider`
- #153 AWS KMS `KeyProvider`
- #154 GCP Cloud KMS `KeyProvider`
- #155 Background KEK rotation sweep (+ optional indexed `kek_id` column)
- #156 Route recipient/provider tokens through `SecretManager`

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

body:
### Motivation

- Consolidate UI/UX and gameplay for mobile by moving from a long stacked layout to a compact tabbed layout and a larger tactical map. 
- Introduce a clear per-floor cost rule for `magicBook` usage so attempts are predictable and saveable. 
- Provide optional automatic AI GM narration that only describes already-computed local results without changing game state. 
- Bump saved state schema to a new version to persist the new `magicBookAttempt` field and related behavior.

### Description

- Expanded fixed map to 11x11: changed `MAP_SIZE` to `11` and replaced the layout with a fixed 11x11 `layout` (start at `{ x: 5, y: 9 }`, enemy at `{ x: 5, y: 1 }`) in `src/map/fixedMap.ts`, and updated map rendering to use `--map-size` CSS variable. 
- Player/enemy initial and floor-reset positions updated to `player.position = { x: 5, y: 9 }` and `enemy.position = { x: 5, y: 1 }` in `src/state/gameState.ts` and `src/game/floor.ts`, and `enterNextFloor()` now initializes `magicBookAttempt` for the new floor. 
- Added `magicBookAttempt` to `GameState` and implemented per-floor magic book attempt cost logic in `src/game/inventory.ts`: first attempt on a floor is free, subsequent attempts on the same floor cost `1` coin, attempts are blocked when coins are insufficient, failure keeps the book, success removes the book and adds the spell. 
- Save schema bumped to `saveVersion = 13`, `SAVE_KEY = 'manrpg-pwa-ai:save:v13'`, legacy keys include v12, and `magicBookAttempt` validation added to `src/storage/save.ts`. 
- Implemented AI automatic GM narration: `applyStateWithAutoNarration()` in `src/ui/render.ts` calls `callLLM('narrate', payload)` after applying local state when `AI` is enabled; AI responses are appended as logs only and do not modify HP/MP/positions/stats/rewards. Prompt constraints were tightened in `src/ai/prompt.ts`. 
- UI rework: created a tab bar and per-tab renderers in `src/ui/render.ts` with tabs `battle | sheet | maintenance | trial | ai | log`; battle tab focuses on map, controls, queue, skills/spells and a compact enemy sheet; maintenance tab aggregates shop, equipment, inventory and shows magicBook attempt state; trial tab is a placeholder. 
- Styling updates in `src/styles.css` to support the tab bar, responsive `battle-layout`, and CSS variable map grid sizing; reduced panel paddings and tightened layout for mobile. 
- AI settings copy updated to label the feature `AI 자동 GM 서술 사용` and explain that AI will not change rules or numeric state in `src/ui/aiSettings.ts`. 
- Tests added/updated: `src/map/fixedMap.test.ts`, `src/game/floor.test.ts`, `src/game/inventory.test.ts` (magicBook attempt cost tests), `src/ui/render.test.ts` (tab UI + auto narration), and multiple existing tests updated to expect `saveVersion 13`. 
- Documentation updated: `README.md`, `docs/TESTING.md`, `docs/TODO.md`, `docs/rules-extracted.md` to reflect 11x11 map, magicBook rules, AI auto narration, tab UI, and `saveVersion 13`.

### Testing

- Ran `npm install` (completed). 
- Unit tests: ran `npm run test` (Vitest) and all tests passed: `21 files, 95 tests passed` after adding/fixing tests for the new behaviors. 
- Worker TypeScript check: ran `npm run worker:check` (tsc --noEmit against worker tsconfig) and it passed. 
- Production build: ran `npm run build` (tsc && vite build) and site built successfully (`dist` artifacts produced). 

If you want, I can split this large PR into smaller focused PRs (map, magicBook rules, AI narration, UI) for easier review.

author: acehack
body:
## What

`install.ps1` now enables Windows long paths, so any machine that runs the installer stops worrying about the 260-char MAX_PATH limit on Zeta's long persona-archive filenames (the B-0947 "Filename too long" class). Aaron-requested 2026-05-31.

## Two layers (matching install.ps1's existing conditional-on-admin pattern)

| Layer | Admin? | What | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 — `git config --global core.longpaths true`** | **No** | Git prepends the Windows extended-length path prefix + bypasses MAX_PATH **itself** (no registry, no reboot) | **Fixes the actual problem** — git creating Zeta's long files. Always-set, best-effort (`Invoke-ToolSoft`, never bricks install). |
| **2 — `HKLM\…\FileSystem\LongPathsEnabled = 1`** | Yes | OS-wide DWORD (Win10 1607+; all longPathAware apps) | Broader bonus; **needs a restart**. Admin-gated + graceful (set only when `Test-IsAdmin`, else print how-to). Never forces elevation. |

Runs as a new step 2b (after the manifest step installs git, before mise). Mirrors the existing scoop `-RunAsAdmin` / choco-only-when-elevated / graceful-skip discipline.

This is the **dev-machine + post-install-git-ops** prong. ### Motivation

- Ensure the startup script works on systems where `python3` exists but `python` is missing, and to make the script able to install Python 3 automatically when feasible.
- Avoid mixing different Python executables by selecting a single, validated interpreter for all runtime and pip invocations.
- Improve robustness of dependency installation and privilege escalation when system packages need to be installed.

### Description

- Added `detect_python` to prefer `python3`/`python` and set `PYTHON_BIN` to the chosen interpreter, and added `install_python` and `run_as_root` helpers to attempt installing `python3`/`pip` via common package managers with `sudo` if needed.
- Replaced all direct `python` calls with `"$PYTHON_BIN"` so `pip`, `flask`, and embedded Python one-liners use the detected interpreter consistently.
- Updated the prereq step to install `PyYAML` using the detected interpreter and adjusted the config parsing `eval` invocation to call the chosen Python binary.
- Left existing behavior intact for environment export, DB initialization, admin creation, and starting the Flask server while logging the server PID and output to `flask-server.log` in the script directory.

### Testing

- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: darriey
body:
## Why the acquire workflow was red

The first live bootstrap runs created the `db-snapshot` release and fetched data successfully — but the **job still showed red**. Cause: the `Fail if degraded` step exits 1 whenever *any* tier connector is degraded. In a real tier some connector almost always is (dead host, awaiting data, or capped to stations without recent obs), so **every run would be red** — which trains people to ignore the workflow.

Example: the realtime bootstrap fetched **9/10 connectors** and saved a 7.9 MB snapshot, but went red because 3 connectors were flagged degraded.

## Change
Removes the fail-on-degraded gate. A run that acquired and saved the snapshot is a **success**. Degraded connectors are still surfaced via:
- the **alert issue** (opened/commented automatically), and
- the uploaded **health artifact** (`health.txt` / `health.json`).

The job still fails naturally if `fetch` or the snapshot upload errors (real pipeline failures).

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>grafana/k6 (go.k6.io/k6/v2)</summary>

### [`v2.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/releases/tag/v2.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/compare/v2.0.0-rc1...v2.0.0)

k6 `v2.0.0` is here 🎉!

k6 v2.0.0 is the final release of the v2 major version, completing the cleanup of deprecated APIs, old commands, and obsolete configuration options that was started with v2.0.0-rc1. If you were already running the release candidate, this release includes a handful of additional changes on top — they are marked with ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** throughout these notes.

Here's a glimpse of what's changed in this release:

- The Go module path has changed to `go.k6.io/k6/v2` — all extensions must update their import paths to be compatible with v2.
- Removal of all long-deprecated CLI commands and flags: `k6 login`, `k6 pause`, `k6 resume`, `k6 scale`, `k6 status`, `--no-summary`, `--upload-only`, and more.
- The `externally-controlled` executor has been removed — scripts using `executor: externally-controlled` will no longer run.
- Cloud run non-threshold aborts (aborted by user, system, timeout, etc.) now return exit code `97` instead of `0`.
- `options.ext.loadimpact` is no longer supported — use `options.cloud`.
- `k6/experimental/redis` module has been removed.
- The `k6 cloud script.js` positional form has been fully removed — use `k6 cloud run script.js`.
- A stack is now required for all `k6 cloud` commands — the previous fallback to the first available stack has been removed.
- The web-vitals library has been updated to v5.1.0, removing the deprecated FID metric.
- ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** easyjson has been dropped in favor of stdlib `encoding/json` — extension authors relying on easyjson-generated methods on k6 types must update.
- ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** The k6 HTTP API server no longer starts by default — pass `--address` to enable it.
- ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** New `k6 cloud project list` command to list Grafana Cloud k6 projects.
- ***(new since v2.0.0-rc1)*** Cloud secrets are now automatically available in `k6 cloud run --local-execution`; use `--no-cloud-secrets` to opt out.

#### Breaking changes

These are changes that require you to update your scripts, CI/CD pipelines, or configuration files before upgrading.

##### Go module path changed to `go.k6.io/k6/v2` [#​5777](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5777)

Following the [Go module versioning conventions](https://go.dev/ref/mod#major-version-suffixes), the k6 module path has changed from `go.k6.io/k6` to `go.k6.io/k6/v2`.

Any extension or external package that imports `go.k6.io/k6` must update all import paths to `go.k6.io/k6/v2`. For the vast majority of extensions this is the only change needed — a mechanical find-and-replace across the codebase:

```
go.k6.io/k6/ → go.k6.io/k6/v2/
```

For example:

```go
// Before
import "go.k6.io/k6/js/modules"

// After
import "go.k6.io/k6/v2/js/modules"
```

##### Removed CLI commands [#​5653](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5653)

The following commands for controlling a running test have been removed. They have not been functional for most use cases since the REST API they relied on was limited to specific execution modes:

- `k6 pause`
- `k6 resume`
- `k6 scale`
- `k6 status`

**Migration:** There is no replacement. These commands relied on the `externally-controlled` executor, which has also been removed in v2.0.0 (see below).

##### Removed `externally-controlled` executor [#​5846](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5846)

The `externally-controlled` executor has been removed. It was legacy code from an older k6 Cloud architecture that allowed external systems to scale VUs and pause/resume a running test via the k6 REST API — the capability that `k6 pause`, `k6 resume`, `k6 scale`, and `k6 status` relied on.

**Migration:** There is no replacement. Any test script with `executor: externally-controlled` will fail to start. Migrate to a different executor based on the desired load profile (e.g., `ramping-vus`, `constant-vus`, `constant-arrival-rate`).

##### Removed `k6 login` command [#​5134](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5134)

The top-level `k6 login` command and its subcommands (`k6 login cloud`, `k6 login influxdb`) have been removed.

**Migration:**

- Replace `k6 login cloud` → `k6 cloud login`
- InfluxDB authentication is no longer configurable via a login command. Use environment variables such as `K6_INFLUXDB_*` to configure the InfluxDB output directly.

##### Removed `k6 cloud script.js` positional form [#​5624](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5624), [#​5912](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5912) *(completed in v2.0.0)*

The old positional-argument form `k6 cloud script.js` has been fully removed. In v2.0.0-rc1 it was changed to show help instead of running; in v2.0.0 the deprecated command handler itself has been removed entirely. The `run` subcommand has been the recommended path since `k6 cloud run` was introduced.

**Migration:** Replace `k6 cloud script.js` with `k6 cloud run script.js`.

##### Removed `--upload-only` flag [#​5844](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5844)

The `--upload-only` flag on the `k6 cloud` command has been removed.

**Migration:** Use `k6 cloud upload script.js` to upload a test without running it.

##### Removed `--no-summary` flag [#​5729](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5729)

The `--no-summary` flag has been removed.

**Migration:** Replace `--no-summary` with `--summary-mode=disabled`.

##### Removed `--summary-mode=legacy` [#​5730](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5730)

The `legacy` value for `--summary-mode` has been removed.

**Migration:** There is no direct equivalent — the new summary format is different from the legacy one. Review the available [summary modes](https://grafana.com/docs/k6/latest/results-output/end-of-test/#summary-modes) and choose the one that best fits your needs: `compact` (the default) or `full` for more detailed output.

##### Removed `options.ext.loadimpact` support [#​5774](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5774)

The `options.ext.loadimpact` configuration block in test scripts is no longer supported.

**Migration:** Move all cloud-related configuration from `options.ext.loadimpact` to `options.cloud`:

```javascript
// Before
export const options = {
  ext: {
    loadimpact: {
      projectID: 12345,
      name: "My Test",
    },
  },
};

// After
export const options = {
  cloud: {
    projectID: 12345,
    name: "My Test",
  },
};
```

##### Removed `k6/experimental/redis` module [#​5485](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/k6/issues/5485)

The `k6/experimental/redis` module has been removed from the k6 core binary. It was shipped as an experiment and has not been promoted to stable.

**Migration:** Change your import from `k6/experimental/redis` to `k6/x/redis`. With [auto-extension-resolution](https://grafana.com/docs/k6/latest/using-k6/auto-extension-resolution/), k6 will automatically provision the [xk6-redis](https://redirect.github.com/grafana/xk6-redis) extension when it sees the `k6/x/redis` import.

author: chanyavrc
body:
## Summary

Per the project direction that `vm.rs` should dispatch only dunder (`__xxx__`) protocol slots and hold no concrete builtin-method bodies, move the generator method surface out of `vm.rs`.

`vm.rs`'s `call_generator_method` hardcoded the **non-dunder** generator methods `send` / `throw` / `close` (mixed in with the `__iter__` / `__next__` arms), plus their implementation helpers. That coupled the Python-level method surface to the VM's low-level resume machinery.

This moves `call_generator_method` and its helpers (`generator_close` / `generator_throw` / `generator_send`) into a new `include!`'d `runtime/generators.rs`. `vm.rs` keeps only the resume machinery (`resume_generator*`, `GeneratorFrame`, `yield_from_advance`).

After this change, **no non-dunder method-dispatch string literals remain in `vm.rs`** (the residual `"const"` / `"name"` / `"*_iterator"` strings are `pool_get!` / `type()`-label strings, not method names).

## Notes

- Pure organisational split: all items stay `impl Interpreter` in the same module (via `include!`), so visibility and behaviour are identical.
- `vm.rs` −366 lines (pure deletion); `runtime.rs` +1 `include!`.
- `generators.rs` uses plain `//` file-header comments (not `//!`): an `include!`'d file is pasted mid-module, where inner doc-comments are illegal (`E0753`).

## Verification

- `cargo build --release` — clean
- `cargo test --release --bin pyrust` — 402 passed
- `cargo test --release --test parity_compare` — passed
- generator `send` / `throw` / `close` / `__iter__` / `__next__` and the bad-attribute `AttributeError` **differential-tested byte-identical to python3.12**

author: sleetish
body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** The `ConversionService.BuildOutputPath` method passed user-provided file names directly into `Path.Combine` without sanitization. An attacker could enter a filename containing directory traversal characters (e.g., `..\..\`) or absolute paths, allowing them to escape the intended output directory and write output files to arbitrary locations on the file system.
🎯 **Impact:** Arbitrary file write. Depending on the privileges the GUI application runs under, this could lead to the modification or overwriting of sensitive local files, resulting in data loss, application corruption, or execution of malicious code.
🔧 **Fix:** Sanitized the `fileName` parameter before passing it to `Path.Combine`. 
    - Replaced all cross-platform slash variants (`/` and `\`) with `Path.DirectorySeparatorChar`.
    - Used `Path.GetFileName()` to strictly extract the file name portion.
    - Provided a safe default fallback string ("output") to handle cases where the sanitized string was entirely empty (e.g., if the user submitted `..`).
✅ **Verification:** 
    - The `dotnet test` suite was run and confirmed no regressions were introduced to the build process.
    - Path traversal sequences like `..\..\file.vsdx` are now safely resolved to `file.vsdx` in the intended output directory.

## Root cause (surfaced by #14's set +e)

The v1.0.2 release's smoke step failed with `exit=127 'sh: 1: rendobar-mcp: not found'` on all 5 retries. `npx -y @rendobar/mcp@VERSION -- --version` fails under **npm 11**: npx resolves the *bin name* (`rendobar-mcp`) instead of the package and can't find it on PATH. Reproduced locally on npm 11.12.1 — Form C (install + node the bin) is the only reliable one.

This blocked *Create GitHub Release* + *MCP registry* on every release; `set -e` masked it until #14.

## Fix

Replace npx with a deterministic smoke: install `@rendobar/mcp@VERSION` into a throwaway dir, run `dist/bin.js --version` directly with `node`. No bin-shim / PATH / npx-version dependency; still proves the published artifact installs and runs. Metadata-based propagation wait kept before install.

## Recovery context
- npm 1.0.2 live; GitHub Release v1.0.2 created manually.
- After merge: dispatch `release.yml tag=v1.0.2` to backfill the MCP registry (publish is idempotent), then close #13.

## Motivation

The close-the-loop phase — the small, satisfying debris the retros named. Three cleanups, and the premise-audit (now a habit) found the scope was a touch larger than the PLAN stated.

## Solution

### D3 — align `loom --help`
`formatHelp` padded namespace names with `padEnd(8)`, but `revise-plan` (11) and `parse-plan` (10) overflow 8, so their descriptions started past the column the shorter verbs aligned to. The width is now **derived** from the longest namespace name, so the descriptions line up and a future longer verb can't silently re-break it (the same derive-don't-duplicate move as Phase 2). A test pins the same-column property.

### D2 — refresh `INSIGHTS.md`
A dated "Remediation outcomes" section folds the 8-phase results back into the diagnosis: each original cluster (#1–6) mapped to what actually shipped — including #1's honest landing (the cap framing unsupported, only the 529 retry shipped) — plus the newly-mined findings (chiefly **plan premises go stale across projects** — three deliverables found already-shipped — and the `derive-panel` positional-arg footgun). The original #1–6 diagnosis is left intact.

### D1 — fill the ADR Consequences (0002–0006)
The PLAN named ADR-0002 and ADR-0005; a grep found **five** ADRs still carrying `TODO: operator to fill before commit`. The exit criterion is "no ADR carries a TODO," so all five are filled — and remarkably, **this remediation's own work is their realized consequences**: P1 realized 0006's `loom doctor` skew-check corollary, P5 realized 0004/0005, P6 realized 0002/0003. ADR-0004's Consequences records a real **divergence**: the decided per-tier verbs (`sync-shared docs`/`lib`) were never built; Phase 5 shipped `--only`/`--exclude-lib` *flags* instead → marked "superseded in practice," recommending a formal superseding ADR.

> **These five Consequences are agent-drafted for your review.** You confirmed (via a structured prompt) to commit the drafts and revise on this PR — the 0004 "superseded in practice" framing in particular is an architectural call worth your pass.

author: paulnonatomic
body:
## Summary
Brings the analyzers in line with ServiceKit V2 and adds a test project.

### SK006 — `[Service]` on an abstract class (new rule, Warning)
`[Service]` is declared `Inherited = false` and abstract classes are never instantiated, so `[Service]` on an abstract base registers nothing — `ServiceKitBehaviour` reads the attribute from the concrete instance's own type. This is a common V1→V2 migration trap (the old generic `ServiceKitBehaviour<T>` base propagated its type via inheritance; the attribute does not). The code fix removes the ineffective attribute.

### SK004 / SK010 — detect the V2 `Inject()` entry point
Both rules previously keyed only on the now-obsolete `InjectServicesAsync(...)` to find the start of an injection chain, so they silently stopped covering the V2 preferred `Inject(target)` entry point. They now treat `Inject` and `InjectServicesAsync` as equivalent chain starters. README examples updated to `Inject(this)`.

### Test project (new)
`Tests/ServiceKit.Analyzers.Tests.csproj` — Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Testing + MSTest (net6.0). Covers SK006 (analyzer + code fix), SK004 and SK010 `Inject()` detection, and `InjectServicesAsync` regression cases. **11 tests, all passing** (`dotnet test`).

## Notes
- The README still does not document SK003/SK005 (pre-existing gap, not addressed here).
- SK001/SK002/SK003 (attribute-based) and SK005 (base-`Awake` check, matches the base type by name) were reviewed and are already V2-compatible.

body:
## Summary

Adds `RasCmdr.preprocess_geometry_linux()` — a native-Linux wrapper around the bundled
`RasGeomPreprocess` binary — closing the CLB-885 gap where the two-phase Linux workflow still
needed Windows for geometry preprocessing.

It runs `RasGeomPreprocess` headlessly to (re)generate the geometry preprocessor tables
(1D XSEC property tables + 2D cell/face HTab property tables) **in place** inside an existing
`{project}.p{plan}.tmp.hdf`, mirroring `compute_plan_linux`:

- LD_LIBRARY_PATH auto-detect (`libs/`, `libs/mkl/`, `libs/rhel_8/`)
- `dos2unix` of project text files
- geometry-number resolution from the plan file (fails fast if the plan can't be resolved)
- output validation via new `_validate_geom_preprocess()` — scans the solver log for error
  markers and the `Finished Processing Geometry` banner, and confirms `/Geometry/GeomPreprocess`
  is populated in the HDF (so an exit-0-but-failed run is not reported as success — same
  philosophy as `_validate_linux_solve` from #171).

## Scope / honest limitation

`RasGeomPreprocess` operates **in place** on a `.tmp.hdf` that already contains the raw
`/Geometry` group. It does **not** build the initial `.tmp.hdf` / `.b##` / `.x##` skeleton from
raw `.prj`/`.g##`/`.u##` text — that assembly remains the Windows Phase-1 step. This wrapper
covers the geometry-HTab (re)preprocessing step, which is what enables a fully-Linux
**geometry-only** preprocess → solve loop without round-tripping to Windows. Documented in the
method docstring.

## Verification (HEC-RAS 6.6 Linux, CLB07)

End-to-end on real binaries:
1. Strip `/Geometry/GeomPreprocess` (8 datasets) from a Muncie `.tmp.hdf`
2. `preprocess_geometry_linux("04", ras_exe_dir="/opt/hecras/6.6")` → `success=True`; all 8
   GeomPreprocess datasets regenerated (IBC_CON, XSEC Properties, Property Tables, Skyline, …)
3. `compute_plan_linux("04", …)` on the Linux-regenerated geometry → `success=True`,
   valid `/Results/Unsteady`

Tests: `tests/test_geom_preprocess_linux.py` (6 tests) — validator pass/fail paths and the
missing-binary guard. Full Linux suite green: `test_geom_preprocess_linux.py` + the #171
`test_linux_robustness.py` → **14 passed**.

## Base

Branched on `fix/linux-robustness` (#171) since it reuses that PR's validation philosophy.

## Summary

Closes **#16**. Promotes `google-ads` from a stub to a working
**opt-in** live adapter behind the new `[google-ads]` extra — without
adding any runtime dependency to the base install.

## How it works

With a complete credential block passed via `--config` and the extra
installed, the adapter calls
[`KeywordPlanIdeaService.GenerateKeywordIdeas`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/keyword-planning/generate-keyword-ideas)
and emits `KeywordMetric` rows (`query`, `avg_monthly_searches`,
`competition`, bid micros in `raw`).

```bash
pip install "site-context-pipeline[google-ads]"
site-context-pipeline import-keywords \
    --client demo --provider google-ads \
    --config clients/demo/config/google_ads.json --write
```

## Safety (per docs/providers.md rules)

- **No runtime dep in base install.** The `google-ads` SDK is imported
  lazily inside `_load_client`, never at module load.
- **No credentials in repo / artifacts / logs.** Creds come from the
  config block; `customer_id` is masked in result metadata; no secret
  is ever serialised.
- **Graceful degradation, never a stack trace:**
  - no / empty config → `not_configured` (`ok=false`, exit 1)
  - extra not installed → `missing_dependency` (`ok=false`, exit 1)
  - malformed config → `ProviderConfigurationError` naming the keys
- **No network in tests.** The two seams (`_load_client`,
  `_generate_ideas`) are stubbed with fakes; all mapping/validation is
  pure-function unit tested.

## Tests

`tests/test_google_ads_adapter.py` — 32 tests covering:

- not_configured / missing_dependency / malformed-config paths
- live happy path via stubbed seams (idea → metric mapping, blank-text
  drop, competition enum translation, customer_id redaction, JSON
  serialisability)
- pure helpers (`validate_config`, `_coerce_seeds`, `_redact`,
  `_competition_label`, `map_idea_to_metric`)

Test count 228 → **260**.

## Docs & metadata

- `[google-ads]` extra added to `pyproject.toml`.
- `mypy` override for `google.ads.*`.
- Registry flags `google-ads` live with an opt-in description;
  `list-providers` reflects it.
- `docs/provider-reference.md`, `docs/providers.md`, README provider
  table, ROADMAP (0.4 item marked landed), CHANGELOG all updated.

## Verification

- `ruff check .` — clean
- `mypy --strict` — 0 issues across 22 source files
- `pytest -q` — **260 passed**
- `mkdocs build --strict` — clean
- Base install still has zero runtime dependencies.
- No files outside `oss/site-context-pipeline/` modified.

Closes #16.

body:
## Summary

Exposes Zig's clang-frontend C/C++ compiler as first-class Dagger functions on the `zig` module:

- **`Cc`** — `zig cc <files...> [-target ..] -o <outputName> [args...]`
- **`Cxx`** — `zig c++ ...` (C++ counterpart)

`zig cc`/`zig c++` bundle libc and headers for every supported target, so cross-compilation needs no sysroot setup — useful for compiling C/C++ directly and as `CC` for foreign toolchains (e.g. Go CGO cross-builds). Both reuse the existing checksum-verified base container.

### Details
- `files` is required; an empty slice is rejected with a clear error before any exec.
- `outputName` (CLI `--output-name`) is renamed from `output` to avoid colliding with the Dagger CLI's top-level `--output`/`-o`, per the `go` module's `Ci.WithBuild` precedent. Defaults to `a.out`.
- Both functions carry `+cache="session"` and share an unexported `compileC` helper.
- Adds `fixtures/c/hello.c` + `fixtures/cpp/hello.cpp` and 4 tests wired into `tests/All` under `+check`.

## Test plan

- [x] Each test passes individually: `cc-compiles-hello-c`, `cc-cross-windows-produces-exe`, `cc-rejects-empty-files`, `cxx-compiles-hello-cpp`.
- [x] `dagger -m daggerverse/zig/tests call all` green.
- [x] `gofmt` + `go vet ./...` clean in both modules.

Closes #95

## Summary

**Fourth pass crate** now has its `tests/upstream/` layout — and the first one targeting the **emitter** rather than a transform pass. Asserts on output strings instead of AST shape.

- Pinned to `google/closure-compiler@5bb35ec1245dc1d3557481e5f8b4db344bcd1e6b`. Apache-2.0 attribution complete.
- **12 ported test methods: 6 pass today, 6 are `#[ignore]`-ed citing gap-021 through gap-027.** (gap-024 is a DOCUMENTED divergence, not a missing feature.)

## Passing today (6)

| Test | Assertion |
|------|-----------|
| `test_binary_addition_with_parens_is_current_behaviour` | `2 + 3` → `(2 + 3);` |
| `test_string_concat_with_parens_is_current_behaviour` | `\"a\" + \"b\"` → `(\"a\" + \"b\");` |
| `test_unary_not_emits_without_space` | `!x` → `!x;` |
| `test_boolean_literal_at_statement_position` | `true;` / `false;` |
| `test_integer_literals_at_statement_position` | `0;`, `42;`, `1;` |
| `test_string_literal_at_statement_position` | `\"hello\";`, `\"a\";` |

The two `_is_current_behaviour` tests deliberately pin our paren-wrapping divergence from upstream — they serve as regression markers so when **gap-024** is closed and the wrapping comes off, both assertions can flip together to upstream's exact bytes.

## Ignored (6) + 1 divergence

| Test / Gap | What it'd need |
|------------|---------------|
| `test_big_int` / **gap-021** | `BigIntLiteral` AST variant (Phase 1.x) |
| `test_trailing_comma_*` / **gap-022** | Array/object trailing-comma policy in AST + emitter |

| (no test) / **gap-024** | DOCUMENTED — `ExpressionStatement` paren-wrapping diverges; closes when ambiguity-aware emitter lands |
| `test_number_formatting_shortest_form` / **gap-025** | Pick-shortest numeric formatter (exponential vs decimal) |
| `test_string_quote_choice_minimises_escapes` / **gap-026** | Quote-choice optimisation |
| `test_operator_precedence_inserts_inner_parens` / **gap-027** | Precedence-aware paren insertion |

`CodePrinterTest` has 263 `@Test` methods covering Phase 2+ AST node variants (BigInt, optional chaining, template literals, classes, spread, async/await, regex) plus formatting policies (quote choice, exponential-form numerics, precedence-aware parens) we haven't implemented yet. body: The audit chain hashes `timestamp` (in HASHED_FIELDS) at microsecond precision, but Mongo stores datetimes at millisecond precision -> the verify-time recompute drifts from the stored hash whenever the timestamp had sub-ms microseconds, intermittently failing `test_proposal_audit_chain` on shared-mongo CI (seen red on main @260464e). Fix: truncate datetimes to ms in `_json_default` so write-time and verify-time bytes are identical. Verified locally: a us-precision write row and its ms-truncated read-back now hash equal. via improvement-initiative

author: xergioalex
body:
## Summary

The auto-release job [failed](https://github.com/DailybotHQ/deepworkplan-skill/actions/runs/26731715588/job/78776896421) on the last merge to `main` (exit code 127).

**Root cause:** the *Update CHANGELOG.md* step built the commit list with
`COMMITS="${{ steps.version.outputs.commits }}"`. GitHub Actions expands
`${{ }}` into the script **source** before bash runs it, so a commit
message containing a literal double quote —

> `docs(skill): use the official Dailybot "Powered by" section in the README`

— terminated the bash string early, and the leftover text `by section in
the README` was executed as a command (`No such file or directory`,
exit 127). It's also a textbook GitHub Actions script-injection vector.

## Fix

Pass `NEW_VERSION`, `NEW_TAG`, and `COMMITS` through `env:` instead of
inlining them with `${{ }}`. Bash now receives them as real environment
variables that are never re-parsed as script source, so quotes,
backticks, and `$()` in any commit message are inert. Applied the same
hardening to the *Bump version* and *Commit, tag, push* steps for
consistency.

## Validation

- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/auto-release.yml'))"` → OK
- No behavior change to the version-bump logic; once merged, auto-release re-runs over the same backlog and should cut the pending release cleanly.

author: jjin18
body:
## Symptom
Site loads, event picker works, but **goes blank (white screen) right after you pick an event.**

## What this is
A white screen after an interaction = a **render-time JavaScript exception** with nothing to catch it. `InPersonApp.jsx` had **no error boundary** (the desktop `App.jsx` does), so any throw blanks the entire app silently — and on a phone there's no console to see what threw.

## This PR
Wraps the in-person app in an **error boundary** that renders the **actual error message + a Reload button** instead of a blank page.

Two wins:
1. **No more dead-end white screen** — you get a readable error and can reload.
2. **It surfaces the real error** (on-screen and in console), so we can finally see *what's* throwing after event-pick and fix the root cause. Right now it's invisible.

## I need one thing from you after this deploys
Pick an event again. Instead of blank, you'll now see **"Something broke on this screen"** with an error message under it. **Tell me that message** (or screenshot it) and I'll push the actual fix immediately — it'll point straight at the culprit (likely the QR camera init or a bad cached event object).

Build passes. Opened ready-to-merge (not draft) since the site's unusable.

> Quick alternative to try first, in case it's a stale cached bundle: hard-refresh / clear the site data on your phone, since the earlier broken deploys may have cached a bad build.
