author: cheapfuck
body:
## Problem

Re-evaluating a project a user had already passed can take coalition points away from them.

Real example from a student on our campus:

| When         | Mark | Points awarded | Reason                                     |
| ------------ | ---: | -------------: | ------------------------------------------ |
| 131 days ago |  98% |           +866 | Validated `42_Collaborative_resume` …      |
|  20 days ago | 100% |            −86 | Validated `42_Collaborative_resume` (retry) |

The student validated the same project again at a *higher* mark and lost 86 points. Same pattern is visible on several other projects on that account (Cybersecurity – Vaccine - Web 102 % → −140, arachnida - Web 120 % → −166).

## Root cause

[`handleFixedPointScore`](https://github.com/codam-coding-college/coalition-system/blob/master/src/handlers/points.ts) is meant to be a **top-up** mechanism on retries: it sums all prior score rows for the same `(user_id, fixed_type_id, type_intra_id)` triple and awards `pointDifference = newPoints − sumOfPrior` so the user's total over all rows ends up at `newPoints`.

That works fine as long as the formula and its inputs (`fixedPointType.point_amount`, `project.difficulty`) are stable. But:

- `point_amount` is editable by admins from the admin panel (`src/routes/admin/points.ts`)
- `project.difficulty` is synced from Intra and can change over time

When either drops between the original validation and a retry, the recomputed `newPoints` is **lower** than the historical row, so `pointDifference` becomes a large negative number — and the existing guard only suppresses *tiny* negatives:

```ts
if (pointDifference > -10 && pointDifference < 1) { return null; }
```

So a `−86` slips through and gets written as a real `CodamCoalitionScore` row with the reason “Validated X with N%”. The user loses points for re-evaluating a project they had already passed, which is the opposite of the intent.

No date / season multiplier exists in the project-score path (traced from `projects_users.ts:100` → `handleFixedPointScore` → `createScore` → DB; `syncIntraScore` only mirrors). The only time-sensitive multiplier in the repo is the evaluation-points sale in `scale_teams.ts`, which does not touch project validations.

## Fix

Suppress *any* `pointDifference <= 0` instead of just the small-negative band. The original intent ("hand out the difference when a retry earned more") is preserved exactly for positive diffs. A `console.warn` is emitted when a large negative is suppressed, so admins can spot scoring-config drift in the logs without it silently affecting students.

```ts
const pointDifference = Math.floor(points) - existingScores._sum.amount;
if (pointDifference < 1) {
  if (pointDifference < -10) console.warn(/* drift warning with details */);
  else                       console.log(/* small noise, as before */);
  return null;
}
```

No DB migration or backfill is included — only the runtime decision changes from this point on. Existing negative score rows that have already been written are untouched and would need a separate admin-driven cleanup if desired.

## Notes / things to confirm

- The fix is intentionally minimal and applies symmetrically to all `handleFixedPointScore` callers (projects, exams, pools), since the "never take points away on a retry" property is desirable across the board. If exams should behave differently, happy to scope it down.
- The `Math.floor(Math.floor(...))` double-floor on the old line was removed (it was a no-op).
- If you want, I can follow up with a small admin script that lists all `CodamCoalitionScore` rows with `amount < 0` whose `fixed_type_id` is `project` or `exam`, so the existing damage can be reviewed and optionally reverted.

## How I verified

- Traced the full point-write pipeline (`projects_users.ts` → `points.ts` → `intrascores.ts`) to confirm no date multiplier exists for project scores.
- Searched `prisma/` for schema fields and recent migrations to make sure no implicit transformation happens on insert.
- Reviewed `git log` on the affected files since 2026-01-01; the only formula change in that window was `a597e87` (exam-mark scaling), which does not affect the example project above.
- TypeScript compile clean (`get_errors` reports no diagnostics on the edited file).

author: iwahbe
body:
## Divergence

`cidrhost` was hand-rolled as a forward-only byte addition over the network
address, diverging from OpenTofu (which delegates to `cidr.HostBig`) in two ways:

- **Negative host numbers.** OpenTofu counts a negative `hostnum` back from the
  end of the prefix's address range, so `cidrhost("10.0.0.0/24", -1)` is the
  last host `10.0.0.255`. The hand-rolled version fell through the `hostnum > 0`
  loop guard and returned the network address `10.0.0.0` unchanged.
- **Out-of-range host numbers.** A `hostnum` larger than the available host bits
  silently carried into the network portion of the address (e.g.
  `cidrhost("10.0.0.0/24", 256)` → `10.0.1.0`). OpenTofu rejects it with
  `prefix of 24 does not accommodate a host numbered 256`.

Probed against `tofu` 1.12.0 to confirm both behaviors.

## Fix

Delegate to `cidr.HostBig` (already imported), matching OpenTofu's
implementation exactly.

## Proof

- `tests/tfcompat/l1_cidrhost` — fails on master (pulumi returns `10.0.0.0` for
  the negative offsets), passes after the fix.
- `pkg/hcl/eval/functions_test.go` — added success cases for `-1`/`-2` and an
  error-path case `TestCidrHostOutOfRange` asserting the OpenTofu error message.

```
PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH" go test ./pkg/hcl/eval/ -run 'TestIPFunctions|TestCidrHostOutOfRange' -count=1
PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH" go test ./tests/tfcompat/ -run TestL1CidrHost -count=1
```

Both pass.

body:
Completes the v1.0.0 global-install migration's project teardown, which shipped incomplete — verified by walking all 5 prod projects post-upgrade. First of two sequential PRs (the steering-response UI fix follows once this merges).

## What was wrong

The migration stripped per-symbiont configs but left several classes of Myco artifact behind in brownfield projects:

- **`.myco/buffer/` + `.myco/logs/`** orphaned — the purge omitted them while the slimmed `.myco/.gitignore` dropped their ignore rules, so stale files surfaced as untracked git adds.
- **Legacy launcher stubs** `.agents/myco-run.cjs` / `myco-cli.cjs` never removed — `uninstall()` preserves the project-shared launchers by design, and nothing called `removeProjectLaunchers` after the strip loop.
- **Retired-symbiont `.gemini/settings.json`** — Gemini has no manifest (superseded by Antigravity), so the manifest-driven strip skipped it.
- **Orphaned OpenCode `.opencode/package.json`** — only removed when empty; the SDK-dep file survived its now-deleted plugin.

## Changes

- `buffer`/`logs` → `PURGABLE_VAULT_ARTIFACTS` as **archive** (swept into the gitignored `.archive-*/`, not deleted); re-add them + `machine_id` to the managed `.myco/.gitignore` as a defensive net (incl. the upgrade-window `machine_id` race the one-shot purge can't win).
- Migration now calls `removeProjectLaunchers()`, `cleanRetiredSymbiontConfigs()` (Gemini), and `removeManagedPluginPackage()` (pristine-only — contributor-edited `package.json` preserved).
- Remove the dead project-local-override delegation from the global launcher (`global-launcher.cjs`) — project-local launchers don't exist in the global model.
- First test coverage for `migrateProjectToGlobalInstall`; updated launcher tests.
- Skill-doc cleanup (`cli-surface-architecture` removal + two skill edits).

## Verification

- `npm test` green; `tsc --noEmit` clean; UI build clean.
- Already-migrated trees on the dev machine cleaned manually (these orphans are git-tracked; git history is their archive).

author: hyxiaoge
body:
## 背景

单点登出 SLO 的最后一块。此前 P3 主线打通了「一次登录、处处可达」（login once in fusion → navigate to audio with no re-login）；本 PR 补上对称的登出侧：「一处登出、处处登出」。

auth-service `/auth/logout`（PR-1）+ auth-client-web `logout({global:true})`（PR-2，#1）+ audio-ui（PR-3）均已上线 dev，fusion-ui 是收尾。

## 改动

- **`revokeSsoSession()` → `sdkLogout({ global: true })`**：登出由「仅撤销本应用 refresh token」升级为全局单点登出。SDK 本地清理后，以顶层表单 POST 到 `${authUrl}/auth/logout` 销毁共享 IdP 会话。
  - 为什么必须顶层表单 POST：IdP 会话 cookie 是 `SameSite=Lax` + HttpOnly + host-only（prod 下 `__Host-` 前缀禁 Domain），跨站 `fetch(credentials:'include')` 带不上；`/auth/logout` 仅收 POST，`location.assign` 只能 GET → 唯一通路是隐藏自动提交的 `<form method=POST>`。
  - 不做全局登出的后果：IdP 会话仍在，下次加载会被静默 SSO 探测立刻重新登入，登出形同虚设。
- **依赖升级**：`auth-client-web` `#2686968 → #e415304`（含 global logout 能力；旧版 `logout()` 类型无 `global`，不升会编译失败）。
- **回调页无需改动**（与 audio 的差异点）：登出后 auth-service 302 裸回跳 fusion 的 `/auth/callback`（无 `?code=`），SDK 返回 `{ status:'no_callback' }` 而非抛错；fusion 的 `completeLogin` 本就把任意非 `authenticated` 结果软回首页，故裸回跳天然软落地、不报错。补 `no_callback` 软落地回归用例固化此行为。
- `logoutWithSso` 编排不变（`markSsoProbed` 先行 + best-effort 撤销 + 清本地 Redux/存储）。

## 测试

- TDD：`authService.test.ts` 先红（断言 `logout` 带 `{ global: true }`）→ 实现转绿。
- 全量 `vitest` 268 通过；`npm run build` 通过（`/auth/callback` 路由正常编译）。

author: rafael-chavez
body:
I have addressed the performance issues and email system deficiencies you reported.

### Performance Optimizations (INP Improvement):
- **Localized Form State:** The `OnboardingForm` now manages its own input state (`clientName`, `accountNumber`, etc.) locally. This prevents the entire dashboard from re-rendering on every keystroke, which was a major contributor to high Interaction to Next Paint (INP) latency.
- **Optimized Calendar Lookups:** I extracted the calendar grid into a new `CalendarGrid` component and implemented an O(1) lookup for onboardings using a `Map` indexed by date. This eliminates expensive filtering logic during calendar renders.
- **Data Synchronization:** `AdminDashboard` now passes its `onboardings` data directly to the app, reducing redundant API calls and state updates.

### Email Notification System Enhancements:
- **Detailed Diagnostics:** The backend now captures and returns raw SMTP responses, including message IDs and information on rejected recipients.
- **SMTP Verification:** Added a new "Check SMTP" button in the Email Log viewer. This allows you to verify the server's connection to the mail provider independently of sending an actual notification.
- **Improved Logging:** The Email Notification Log now displays detailed delivery status for each attempted email, helping you diagnose exactly why a message might not have reached its destination even if the system reported it as "sent".

These changes collectively ensure a more responsive dashboard experience and provide the transparency needed to maintain a reliable email notification system.

Adds the finding **detail view** — a shareable, RLS-gated permalink (`/feed/[id]`) where a founder reads the Analyst's full reasoning and the supporting regulatory sources, so they can justify a decision to an auditor or counsel.

Linear: https://linear.app/entear/issue/ENT-64/founder-opens-finding-detail-with-full-regulatory-context

## What changed

- **`finding_supporting_chunks(p_finding_id)` RPC** builds the "supporting chunks" by joining the finding's obligation citation (`citation_celex` + article/recital) to the existing corpus (`regulatory_articles` → `regulatory_article_paragraphs`, `regulatory_recitals`) — each chunk has quoted text + a EUR-Lex deep link, reusing the `analyst_citation_label`/`analyst_citation_url` builders. - Integration (`tests/integration/finding-supporting-chunks.test.ts`): corpus-backed article + ordered paragraphs, the no-corpus fallback, and cross-tenant isolation.

Full suite green (514 passed), lint clean (0 errors), build passes. `/feed/[id]` registered.

Built with three parallel, non-colliding subagents (chunks RPC, data layer, UI component) against a fixed contract, then integrated the route + feed wiring.

body:
## Summary

Four critical bugs fixed in v0.1.12.

## Bugs Fixed

### 1. Symbol memory leak in `SpeechStream` (Bug 4)
- **File**: `inner_speech/helpers/speech_stream.rb`
- **Problem**: IDs were created as interpolated Symbols (`:"\utt_#{@counter}"`) — Ruby Symbols are never garbage collected, causing unbounded memory growth on long-running instances
- **Fix**: Changed to plain String IDs (`"utt_#{@counter}"`)

### 2. Symbol creation from user-controlled input in `Utterance` (Bug 4 cont.)
- **File**: `inner_speech/helpers/utterance.rb`
- **Problem**: `resolve_mode` and `resolve_voice` called `to_sym` on arbitrary input before validating — any unrecognized value would intern a new Symbol permanently
- **Fix**: Validate against string representation first, return the existing Symbol from the constant array — no new symbols created for invalid input

### 3. Same Symbol-from-input fix in `InnerVoice#switch_voice`
- **File**: `inner_speech/helpers/inner_voice.rb`
- **Problem**: `switch_voice` called `voice.to_sym` before checking against `VOICE_TYPES`
- **Fix**: Extracted `resolve_voice` helper using the same string-comparison pattern; avoids Symbol creation for invalid inputs

### 4. Nil dereference guards — `CognitiveGrammar` and `ConceptualBlending` runners
- **Files**: `grammar/runners/cognitive_grammar.rb`, `conceptual_blending/runners/conceptual_blending.rb`
- **Problem**: `create_grammar_construction`, `create_grammar_construal`, and `create_blend` called `.to_h` on values that the engine returns as `nil` for invalid input types
- **Fix**: Added nil guard clauses returning structured error hashes before calling `.to_h`

## Test Changes
- Updated `inner_speech_spec.rb`: `utterance_id` assertion changed from `be_a(Symbol)` to `be_a(String)`

## Verification
- `bundle exec rspec`: **746 examples, 0 failures**
- `bundle exec rubocop`: **0 offenses**

author: raulg0mez
body:
## Problema

Al pedir un **plan de pagos / parcialidades**, el agente saltaba directo a preguntar el método de cobro (tarjeta guardada vs link) **sin antes especificar cómo quedaba el plan**. El usuario tenía que preguntar manualmente *"¿cómo queda el plan?"* para verlo.

Ejemplo real reportado:

1. Usuario: *"Haz un plan a Raúl: ahorita $30,000, en 2 meses $20,000, al mes siguiente $20,000."*
2. Agente: *(pide elegir cuál Raúl)* → usuario elige.
3. Agente: *"Raúl Gómez ya tiene tarjeta guardada. Para el primer cobro de $30,000... ¿la cobro con su tarjeta guardada o mando link?"* ← **pregunta el método sin mostrar el plan**
4. Usuario tiene que preguntar: *"¿Pero cómo quedará el plan?"* para recién ver el desglose.

## Causa raíz

En `create_installment_payment_flow` (`backend/src/services/aiAgentService.js`), el orden de los gates ponía la pregunta de método/tarjeta guardada **antes** del resumen de confirmación del plan:

```
1. datos faltantes (montos/fechas/método)
2. preferencia de tarjeta guardada   ← se disparaba aquí, antes de mostrar el plan
3. shouldAskStoredCardChoice
4. canal de envío
5. validación de plan completo
6. resumen + confirmación del plan    ← el desglose recién aparecía aquí
```

## Solución

Se añade un gate de **vista previa del plan** que se dispara **antes** de cualquier pregunta de método/tarjeta, cuando el plan tiene 2+ cobros, el schedule está completo y aún no se confirmó:

- Devuelve `planPreviewConfirmationRequired` con el desglose (`schedule`: #, fecha exacta, monto) + total.
- Su `confirmationPrompt` instruye al modelo a mostrar la tabla del plan y pedir confirmarlo, **sin** preguntar todavía por método de pago, tarjeta ni canal de envío.
- Sólo cuando el usuario confirma el plan (`hasExplicitPaymentExecutionConfirmation`), el gate se omite y el flujo continúa con la pregunta del método de tarjeta como antes.

Además, si el **único** dato faltante es el *método del primer pago*, ya no bloquea la vista previa: el método se resuelve después de confirmar el plan. Los datos que sí cambian el plan (montos, fechas, número de cobros) siguen siendo obligatorios antes de mostrarlo, igual que la validación anti-`scheduleIncomplete`.

Se refuerza también el `PAYMENT_WORKFLOW_PROMPT` para que prompt y herramienta sean consistentes sobre el orden: **plan primero, método después**.

## Flujo resultante

| Paso | Antes | Ahora |
|---|---|---|
| Tras elegir contacto | "¿Tarjeta guardada o link?" | **Tabla del plan (fechas/montos/total) + "¿Así te late el plan?"** |
| Tras confirmar el plan | (ya ejecutaba/seguía) | "¿Tarjeta guardada o link?" |
| Tras elegir método | — | Resumen final + ejecución |

## Notas

- Cambio acotado a `create_installment_payment_flow` (flujo de creación de parcialidades), que es el caso reportado. No toca el flujo de modificación de schedules existentes ni el cobro único.
- El output completo de la herramienta (incluido `confirmationPrompt`) llega al modelo vía `safeStringify`, así que la instrucción de "mostrar plan, no pedir método aún" se respeta.
- `node --check` pasa sobre el archivo modificado.

author: yurisa2
body:
## Summary

Fix for the indefinite-poll failure mode (FM-7) on `copilot-review-gate.yml`. Two changes, bounded to this single YAML file per AC4 of #4.

### 1. Pre-poll classifier (new AC1)

`detectUnrecoverableSignal()` runs before the polling loop and checks two signals that mean a Copilot review can never arrive for the current commit:

- **Signal A — Bot unresolvable.** GraphQL probe: `user(login: "copilot-pull-request-reviewer")` + `repository.assignableUsers(query: "copilot-pull-request-reviewer", first: 5)`. If both return empty, the bot can't be added as a reviewer in this caller repo. Exit `conclusion: neutral`.
- **Signal B — Request-side failed.** Most recent `request-copilot-review.yml` workflow run on the PR's HEAD SHA concluded `failure` or `cancelled`. If the request side never succeeded, Copilot was never asked. Exit `conclusion: neutral`.

Both probes are non-fatal — if the GraphQL/REST call itself errors, the classifier logs a warning and falls through to the polling loop rather than blowing up the gate.

### 2. Hard-timeout tightened, exit conclusion changed (new AC2)

- `maxWaitSeconds`: `20 * 60` → `10 * 60`
- Timeout exit: `conclusion: failure` + `core.setFailed` → `conclusion: neutral` + `core.warning`

Rationale: the gate can't distinguish "Copilot is rate-limited" from "Copilot is slow", so blocking merge on no-review-arrived isn't justified. Operator can re-request review and re-run if a real verdict is wanted.

## What's deliberately NOT touched

- **FM-6 self-error path stays SUCCESS-with-annotation.** PR #5 (merged 2026-05-30) chose `success` for that signal to distinguish "Copilot reviewed but errored" from "no verdict at all". The original AC1 of #4 listed self-error-on-HEAD as a third signal, but folding it into this classifier would change FM-6's exit conclusion. Left alone.
- **No service-repo sweep.** Per AC4 of #4, scope locked to this repo's canonical workflow. If service repos carry drifted local copies of `copilot-review-gate.yml`, that's a separate sweep ticket.

## Acceptance criteria mapping

- **AC1** (unrecoverable detection) — Signals A + B implemented; Signal C intentionally deferred as documented above.
- **AC2** (hard timeout, neutral exit) — done.
- **AC3** (honest summary on every exit) — every `finalizeCheck` call now carries a named-signal or timeout summary.
- **AC4** (scope locked to this repo) — single-file change, no service-repo edits.
- **AC5** (verification on no-op PR in petrosa-data-manager) — post-merge step: open a trivial test PR there and link the check-run URL back to #4 before closing.

## Refs

- `Refs: PetroSa2/petrosa-shared-workflows#4` (FM-7)
- `Related: PetroSa2/petrosa_k8s#767` (FM-6, separate exit path; left untouched here)

author: rickcrawford
body:
Sub-ticket 2 of the Logging v2 epic. Switches the canonical request-id generator to UUIDv7 so the leading 48 bits encode a Unix-millisecond timestamp and ids generated milliseconds apart sort in time order. A ClickHouse / SIEM JOIN on request_id stays partition-friendly and the same generator backs every persisted artefact (audit log, access log, callback envelope) so cross-surface correlation no longer requires two columns.

## Changes
- `identity.rs::new_request_id()` switches from `Uuid::new_v4` to `Uuid::now_v7`. Wire shape (32 lowercase hex without hyphens) preserved; the version nibble at hex index 12 is now `7` instead of `4`.
- `server/access_log.rs` fallback id (when `ctx.request_id` is empty) routes through `identity::new_request_id` instead of an ad-hoc `Uuid::new_v4`.
- `Cargo.toml` uuid dep gains the `v7` feature.

## Tests
- `new_request_id_is_uuidv7_monotonic_and_versioned` asserts the monotonicity property and the version nibble.
- `new_request_id_is_32_hex_chars` still passes (shape preserved).

## Docs
`docs/observability.md` correlation triple section names UUIDv7 explicitly and calls out the time-ordered ClickHouse partitioning property.

## Follow-up
`RequestEvent.request_id: Ulid` migration is scoped under the schema-v2 ticket (WOR-1041); today's wire request_id everywhere goes through `identity::new_request_id` so the cross-surface JOIN already works.

## Verification
- fmt / clippy / test / build / doc: all clean (zero `test result: FAILED`).

author: en-ver
body:
## Summary
- add a synthetic regression test for LinkedIn HTML-to-Markdown conversion
- verify headings/strong blocks followed by `<ul>` render with a blank line before the first list item
- keep coverage offline with no network requests

## Why
LinkedIn descriptions can contain a heading or strong block followed by a `<ul>` list. Older converter output could produce Markdown like:

```md
**Heading:**
* item
```

Many Markdown renderers treat that as literal `*` text rather than a list. Current upstream dependency behavior produces:

```md
**Heading:**

* item
```

This test protects that behavior and helps prevent regressions in job description formatting for consumers using Markdown descriptions.

Upstream `speedyapply/JobSpy` already merged the `markdownify` bump in PR #290 (merge commit `84ed670df3b370bf3203aadbe3947bdaf4734439`), so this PR adds regression coverage to guard that behavior.

## Test details
- synthetic/offline fixture only
- no live scraping
- no network requests

## v2.0.0 — "Apprentice" 🎓

The **Apprentice** milestone: all seven tracks (Linux · Network · Crypto · Web · Forensics · OSINT · Cloud) are now playable **level0 → level1 → level2 — 21 levels in total**.

Like v1.0.0 "Foundation" before it, this release is the *coronation* of work already shipped (the level2 sweep landed across v1.23.0–v1.30.0), not a new-gameplay drop. It's a polish + consistency pass so every level meets the same bar.

### Added
- **In-game `hint` coverage on every level.** All 21 levels now carry a three-step escalating `hint` ladder (gentle nudge → specific direction → near-answer that names the breadcrumb's location). Previously only the Linux track and the most recent level2s had hints; the other 14 levels relied solely on their welcome.md "HOW TO PLAY" recipe. The multi-step levels (UNION SQLi, the wayback archive chain, the alg:none JWT) get the most careful ladders.

### Changed
- **Cloud track framework references refreshed to CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0** (current release) on `level0@cloud` + `level1@cloud`, bringing them in line with `level2@cloud`. S3 controls renumber to §3.1.x and IAM access-key rotation to §2.12 — each annotated with the note that AWS Security Hub's managed CIS standard still implements **v5.0.0**, so its console findings show the older §2.1.x / §1.x numbering.
- **Documentation accuracy pass** across README + CONTRIBUTING: level/walkthrough counts → 21, walkthrough section-count wording clarified, stylesheet cache-bust comment corrected.

### Tests
- 351/351 local playtest green (was 350). New `cloud.spec.cjs` assertion confirms the backfilled `hint` ladder surfaces on a representative level rather than the "no hints" fallback.

---

**Motivation:** a pre-2.0 audit of all 21 levels for difficulty-appropriateness found no level intrinsically too hard for its Routine tier — but 14 of them were missing the in-game `hint` safety net a stuck player expects. This release closes that gap before crowning the milestone.

author: provos
body:
## Problem

Leaf subcommand parsers used `parseArgs({ strict: false })`, so an unknown option was silently swallowed instead of rejected. The motivating case:

```
ironcurtain daemon --web-ui --no-signal --capture-blah
```

ran fine — `--capture-blah` (a typo for `--capture-traces`) was dropped on the floor, so the daemon started **with trace capture off** while the operator believed it was on. Silent failure in exactly the wrong direction.

## Change

Add a shared `parseArgsStrict(config, commandName)` helper in `cli-help.ts` that forces `strict: true` and, on a parse error, prints the message plus a `Run \`<command> --help\` for usage.` hint and exits 1. Route every **leaf** parser through it:

- `start`, `daemon`, `mux`, `observe`, `refresh-lists`, `persona create`

`compile-policy` keeps its pure, unit-tested parser, so it uses bare `strict: true` (throws) with a friendly try/catch in `main()`. It also gains `allowPositionals: true` because it parses `process.argv.slice(2)`, which contains the `compile-policy` token — strict mode defaults `allowPositionals` to `false`, which would otherwise reject it.

**Routers stay lenient by design** (top-level `cli.ts`, the `persona` dispatcher, and `auth`'s scope extractor) since they forward unrecognized flags to deeper parsers. `doctor`, `annotate-tools`, and the `workflow` leaves were already strict.

## Behavior note

A known **string** option given without a value (e.g. a dangling `--web-port`) now also errors under strict mode. That's correct, but it's a slightly stricter contract than before.

## Tests

Rewrote the two `compile-policy-cli` cases that asserted lenient behavior to assert rejection, and added a positional-tolerance test for the `process.argv.slice(2)` invocation form.

- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `prettier`: clean
- 200 tests pass (compile-policy / mux / doctor / persona / dynamic-lists)
- `madge --circular`: no cycles
- Manual smoke: unknown flags on `daemon` / `mux` / `compile-policy` exit 1 with a clear message; `--help` still exits 0

author: badoot
body:
## [1.0.6] - 2026-06-01

### Overview

v1.0.6 introduces full Windows support with native filesystem and service parity, significant improvements to gateway network identity detection, and the foundational PKI architecture for gateway-to-gateway federation. This release also standardizes `g8e.local` as the canonical internal mesh hostname and adds native support for MCP-over-HTTP.

### Added

*   **Native Windows Support** - Complete Windows implementation including native filesystem listing (`fs_list_windows.go`), process management, and service control. Added a one-line enrollment flow for Windows operators and specialized handling for Windows network identity (NetBIOS/AD FQDN).
*   **Gateway Peer Identity** - Introduced a new `gateway-peer` intermediate CA and SPIFFE URI SAN binding (`spiffe://g8e.local/gateway/<id>`) to support secure gateway-to-gateway federation.
*   **Canonical Mesh Addressing** - Standardized `g8e.local` as the internal hostname for operator-to-operator communication, supported by a new local translation layer and documentation.
*   **MCP-over-HTTP** - Added support for Model Context Protocol over HTTP on port 8442, including a new `mcp.Config` schema for environment-based TLS configuration.
*   **Network Identity Handoff** - Implemented a structured network identity detection system with cross-process handoff via `--network-identity-file`, allowing parent processes to pre-detect and pass network context to operators.

### Changed

*   **Build Pipeline** - Updated `Makefile` to support compressed builds (~15-17MB) for Linux/Windows and standard builds (~35-38MB). Refined build output for improved developer experience.
*   **Field Path Security** - Optimized `field_parser` to use a constant-backed schema registry, moving away from filesystem-dependent validation for tool call field paths.
*   **Architecture Documentation** - Updated the README and Getting Started guides to reflect current binary sizes, Windows QuickStart commands, and the 5-layer verification sequence.

### Fixed

*   **JSON Robustness** - Gateway controllers now strictly validate and reject malformed JSON bodies during operator binding and configuration updates.
*   **Cross-Platform Nlink** - Fixed `nlink` handling in filesystem listings by implementing architecture-specific casting (uint16/uint32 to uint64) to ensure consistency across Linux, Unix, and Windows.
*   **Gateway Startup** - Resolved race conditions in gateway service initialization specifically affecting Windows environments.

author: itsoso
body:
## 问题
首页天气卡顶部显示 **"California · 北京市"** —— 省/州与城市来自不同位置、互相矛盾。

## 根因
`POST /profile/me/gps-location` 写 `detected_city/region/country` 用了**三个独立 `if`**:
```python
if city:    profile.detected_city = city
if region:  profile.detected_region = region   # ← 新 fix 没 region 时, 旧值残留
if country: profile.detected_country = country
```
用户先在旧金山 → 存了 `region='California'`。之后回到北京,新 GPS 反查只出了 `city='北京'` 没出 `region`(qweather 偶发,或客户端 hint 只带 city)→ 只覆盖 city,**保留了旧的 California** → 省市错配。

## 修复
`city/region/country` 是同一次反查的结果,改为**整组原子写入**:
- 拿到新 `city` → `region/country` 一起覆盖,没反查到的显式置 `None`,不残留旧值
- 没 city 但有 region/country(罕见)→ 同样整组更新,清掉旧 city
- 三者全空 → 只更新 lat/lon,保留旧文字标签(environment.py 优先读坐标,不受影响)

## 验证
- 新增回归 `test_gps_location_new_fix_overwrites_stale_region`(复现该 bug:加州→北京,断言 region 不残留)
- `test_gps_location.py` **15/15 绿**(本地 venv,含坐标透传/英文 hint 丢弃/软失败等既有用例)

author: chrisfmlyc
body:
## Summary

Previously `/spades:setup` short-circuited on re-runs with a meta-question (*"what do you want to change?"*) and "Keep current" defaults on every per-step question. Humans drifted through reconfigurations without re-engaging with the choices; the config grew stale.

This PR flips the UX: **same questions every time, regardless of state.** Current values are surfaced as *context* above each question — never as bias. Before any writes, Step 2.5 presents a diff and requires explicit confirmation. When the human switches backend, Step 2.6 offers AI-assisted migration of existing artefacts.

`apt-get reconfigure` energy. Re-prompt every choice, surface the diff, commit only on confirmation, help with the migration.

## What changes

**1. Step 0.7 — Existing config probe (new).** Captures `current_backend`, `current_scm`, `current_project`, `current_linear_team`, `current_linear_project`, `current_github_remote` from `.spades/config`. These flow into later questions as context lines, not routing inputs.

**2. Steps 1, 1.5, 2 — re-ask every time.** "Keep current" recommended-option language removed throughout. Each question prints a *"Currently configured: X — pick whatever you actually want now"* context line on re-runs. Fresh installs see no context line.

**3. Step 2.5 — Diff & Confirm (new).** Three diff states:
- **No-change re-run** → *"Nothing changed — refresh scaffolding?"* with Yes / Cancel.
- **Some changes** → field-level diff block (`backend: local → linear`, `scm: local-git (unchanged)`, etc.) with Apply / Cancel.
- **First-run** → skipped (nothing to diff against).

**4. Step 2.6 — Backend-switch migration (AI-assisted, new).** Fires only when backend actually changed. Walks the existing artefacts and mirrors them:
- **`local → linear`** — for each local Project / Scope / Plan: search Linear via the MCP for a matching artefact; **link if matched, create if not**; write the new Linear ID back into the local file's frontmatter; append a `Migrated to Linear (backend switch). Linear: <id>.` audit-trail entry. Status mapped SPADES → Linear (`draft` → "Approval", `delivering` → "In Progress", `shipped` → "Done", etc.). Surfaces inline progress.
- **`linear → local`** — reverse: pulls bound Linear Project's Issues + sub-Issues down to local files with `linear_issue_id` preserved.
- **Skip migration** — writes the new config but leaves old artefacts untouched.
- **Cancel the backend switch** — backs out.
- **Error handling** — MCP unreachable → graceful abort; already-linked items keep their `linear_*_id` so re-runs can resume. Duplicate-title disambiguation via `AskUserQuestion`. Rate-limit / network errors surfaced verbatim with retry / skip-this-item / abort.
- **Learnings stay local-only by design** — they're internal commentary, not tracker artefacts.

**5. Step 9 summary** — shows actual transitions (`backend: local → linear`) and a `Migrated: N projects, M scopes, K plans → Linear` line when migration ran.

**6. Re-Run Behaviour section deleted.** The meta-question is gone; its logic is absorbed into Step 0.7 + Step 2.5 + Step 2.6.

## What's deliberately unchanged

- Step 0 (repo plugin probe) and Step 0.5 (git repo check) — pre-flight gates, untouched.
- Step 3 (write config) — already idempotent.
- Steps 4–8 — unchanged.
- AGENTS.md marker block re-stamping in place — same behaviour.
- No new MCP surface area — migration uses Linear MCP operations already documented in `docs/EXTENDING-BACKENDS.md`.

## Files

- `plugins/spades/skills/setup/SKILL.md` — only skill file touched (intro rewrite + new Steps 0.7, 2.5, 2.6 + Steps 1/1.5/2 rewrites + Step 9 transition display + Re-Run section deletion).
- `plugins/spades/CHANGELOG.md` — 2.12.0 entry.

## Versions

- Plugin 2.11.0 → **2.12.0**, marketplace **2.12.0**, `.spades/version` **2.12.0**.
- Skill bump: `setup` 2.7.1 → 2.8.0. No other skill bodies touched.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash plugins/spades/scripts/lint/run-all.sh` — all 5 checks pass.
- [ ] Walk: pre-existing `backend: local` repo. Switch to Linear with Walk-and-mirror; verify Linear populated, local files carry `linear_*_id`, Step 9 summary shows migration counts.
- [ ] Walk: re-pick same backend/SCM/project (no-change re-run) → "refresh scaffolding?" prompt.
- [ ] Walk: fresh install (no `.spades/config`) → no context lines, no diff step.
- [ ] Walk: Cancel on Step 2.5 → no writes happened.
- [ ] Walk: simulate Linear MCP failure mid-migration → graceful abort; re-run picks up partial state.

body:
## The bug
On a finished Gaelic game's summary, the **"By half"** breakdown (below the share card) showed each half's **points total** (e.g. `6 - 4`) instead of the goals-points score (e.g. `1-03 - 0-02`). The share card hero was already correct — only the per-period rows summed raw points.

## Fix (`src/screens/GameSummary.tsx`)
Re-imported `formatGaelicScore` and branched the per-period score: for split-score sports (Gaelic) each half now shows `formatGaelicScore(thatHalf'sEvents, team)` → goals-points; single-score sports still show the integer total. The render was already format-agnostic (`{ps.home}`/`{ps.away}`), so no markup change. Goals/points are derived per half from that half's events.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 111/111; `npm run build` + `npm run lint` clean
- [ ] **On-device:** finish a Gaelic game with goals + points across both halves → confirm the "By half" rows read like `1-03 - 0-02`, and a single-score sport (rugby/soccer/basketball) still shows integers.

## Note
This was the last spot showing a Gaelic points-total instead of goals-points in the result views. (The live play-by-play still shows a running points tally per event — that's a per-event running total, not a half/score line; happy to convert that to goals-points too if you'd like, but it's a separate thing.)

author: abhakeemshah
body:
## Summary
Fixes the production **503 Service Unavailable** on Hostinger (managed Node.js Web App / LiteSpeed). The platform assigns the app a port via `$PORT` and proxies traffic to it; the Next.js preset's auto-start was not binding that port on this Next 16 app, so LiteSpeed couldn't reach the backend → site-wide 503.

This adds a minimal custom server entry file so the app explicitly listens on Hostinger's port:

```js
const port = parseInt(process.env.PORT || '3000', 10);
next({ dev: false }).prepare().then(() => createServer(handle).listen(port, '0.0.0.0'))
```

Deploy config (set in hPanel → Settings and redeploy):
- Framework preset: **Other**
- Build command: `npm run build`
- Entry file: `server.js`
- No `PORT` env var (let the platform inject it)

No app logic, design, or data changed. Verified locally with a non-default port (`PORT=5099 node server.js`): `/`, `/login`, `/categories` → 200; anon `/api/ledger-state` → 401 and `/api/catalog-state` → 200 (PR #6 security fixes intact).

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/fb246f6346f74f649f3e8bba4a2500c2

body:
## Description

A failed Clang CUDA compilation now raises an exception immediately instead of silently continuing and causing a downstream module-load exception that doesn't indicate the root cause. Closes #1325.

## Checklist

- [x] I am familiar with the [Contributing Guidelines](https://nvidia.github.io/warp/stable/user_guide/contribution_guide.html).
- [x] New or existing tests cover these changes.
- [x] The documentation is up to date with these changes.

## Test plan

Added `test_invalid_native_func_compile_error` in `warp/tests/cuda/test_clang_cuda.py`.

Ran:

```bash
uv run warp/tests/cuda/test_clang_cuda.py -k invalid_native_func_compile_error
```

Result: test collected and skipped locally because no suitable CUDA device was available.

## Bug fix

**Repro from #1325:**

```python
import sys
import warp as wp

mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "nvrtc"
wp.config.llvm_cuda = (mode == "clang")

@wp.func_native("""
    INVALID SOURCE;
""")
def bad_func(x: float) -> float: ...

@wp.kernel
def test_kernel(a: wp.array(dtype=float)):
    i = wp.tid()
    a[i] = bad_func(1.0)

a = wp.zeros(10, dtype=float, device="cuda:0")
wp.launch(test_kernel, dim=10, inputs=[a], device="cuda:0")
```

**NVRTC (uv run repro.py nvrtc):**

```
Exception: CUDA kernel build failed with error code 6
```

**Clang CUDA (uv run repro.py clang):**

```
Exception: Failed to load CUDA module '__main__'
```

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Clang CUDA compilation failures are now reported immediately at compile time instead of appearing later as downstream errors.
  * Improved error handling ensures CUDA kernel compilation failures are consistently detected across all compilation paths.

* **Tests**
  * Added a test that verifies invalid native/CUDA compilation errors are raised as expected.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated changelog with the above fix.

author: trinexislabs
body:
## Summary
Adds everything needed to dockerize and deploy ABMSignal to DigitalOcean, plus the mobile-responsiveness pass.

### Deployment assets
- **`Dockerfile`** — multi-stage; one image reused for **web / worker / migrate** (runs `prisma generate`; keeps full deps since the worker runs TS via `tsx` and migrations need the Prisma CLI).
- **`docker-compose.yml`** — `caddy + web + worker + redis + migrate`, with health-gated boot order (`redis` → `migrate` → `web`/`worker`).
- **`Caddyfile`** — reverse proxy + automatic HTTPS, with an SSE flush block for the live-progress endpoints.
- **`.dockerignore`**, **`.env.production.example`** (secret-free template; un-ignored in `.gitignore`).
- **`docs/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md`** + **`.html`** — full step-by-step DigitalOcean runbook (provisioning, TLS, backups, scaling, troubleshooting, env reference).

body:
PR2b step 3a (plan: `docs/multi-growth/PLAN_point1.md`). Sliding-TTL, size-capped in-memory store keyed by `sessionId` that holds in-flight consensus `LoopState` across stateless MCP tool calls — so a Claude-driven multi-round loop survives call-to-call **without** `sessions.persist` (which governs only the durable audit record). Ephemeral by design: a restart drops it and the driver restarts the loop. Consumed by the server `consensus-step` tool next.

## `core/loop-store.js`
- `makeLoopStore({ttlMs=30min, maxEntries=100, now=Date.now})` → `{put,get,delete,sweep,size}`. Injectable clock.
- **Sliding TTL** (get refreshes; lazy drop on get + eager `sweep()`).
- **True-LRU eviction via a monotonic seq counter** — not `touchedAt` — so `Date.now()` ms-granularity ties can't evict a recently-used entry, and a pathological injected clock can't stall eviction.

## Review
`/ask-all` Code Reviewer (5 models, 4 APPROVE). Folded the one REQUEST CHANGES + 2 converging recs: **monotonic-seq LRU** (was timestamp tie-break — deepseek's blocker) + `makeLoopStore(null)` guard. Dismissed deep-copy-on-get (contract: `LoopState` replaced wholesale each step).

## Tests
10 cases incl. **LS10** frozen-clock true-LRU (proves the seq fix). **Full suite 411/411 green, typecheck clean.**

author: brandonrc
body:
## Summary

UI artifact downloads and migration progress streaming are broken because the web client binds download tickets to a `resource_path` the backend cannot match.

The backend binds a download ticket to an exact request path and, at consume time, compares `bound_path == request.uri().path()` by byte equality (`backend/src/api/middleware/auth.rs`). The minter is responsible for sending the exact absolute path the later request will carry. Two call sites sent the wrong value:

| Call site | Sent (wrong) | Now binds |
|-----------|--------------|-----------|
| `artifactsApi.createDownloadTicket` | `` `${repoKey}/${artifactPath}` `` | `` `/api/v1/repositories/${repoKey}/download/${artifactPath}` `` |
| `migrationApi.createStreamTicket` | `` `migration/${jobId}` `` | `` `/api/v1/migrations/${jobId}/stream` `` |

Each was wrong twice: not absolute (the `resource_path must start with '/'` rejection @flopma hit), and not the full request path, so even an absolute form would have been consumed against a mismatching path and silently burned.

No backend change is needed; the backend validator and consumer middleware behave as designed.

Fixes #453

## Test Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] E2E Playwright tests added/updated
- [x] Manually tested locally
- [x] No regressions in existing tests

Added regression tests asserting the exact `resource_path` passed to the SDK for both call sites (`src/lib/api/__tests__/artifacts.test.ts`, `src/lib/api/__tests__/migration.test.ts`). Ran the affected suites locally: 73 passed. ESLint clean on changed files.

## UI Changes
- [x] N/A - no UI changes

This is a client-side request-payload fix in the API layer. No rendered UI changed, though it restores the download and migration-stream flows the UI depends on.

Adds new resw keys across all 5 locales (en-us, fr-fr, nl-nl, zh-cn, zh-tw). Each new key is registered in LocalizationValidationTests so the key-parity, format-placeholder, and mojibake-detector tests pass.

---

### Master merge update (commit `8fe52196`)

Merged in master to resolve drift with PR #558 / #597 / #686 that landed since this PR opened. Eleven conflicts resolved:
- 6 XAML files (AgentEventsPage, ConnectionPage, CronPage, SandboxPage, SessionsPage, HubWindow): took master versions, which already cover the x:Uid wiring
- CronPage.xaml.cs: master + re-applied 2 hunks unique to this PR (JobCompletedInfoBar, ShowDisconnected)
- 5 Resources.resw files: reset to master and re-injected the 80 unique keys via text injection to preserve XML entities (`"`)
- LocalizationValidationTests.cs: pruned 17 obsolete and 7 over-deferred entries from `InvariantOrDeferredResourceKeys`

### Localization regression caught during merge review

Adversarial dual-model review (Claude Opus + GPT Codex) flagged a real regression: AgentEventsPage and SkillsPage runtime code overrides XAML defaults with `LocalizationHelper.GetString` / `Format` calls. The 7 corresponding keys had been seeded English-only across all locales, so fr/nl/zh users would have seen English status badges and skill counters at runtime despite translated XAML defaults.

Fixed by translating those 7 keys in fr-fr, nl-nl, zh-cn, zh-tw using the existing translated XAML defaults as the canonical source (28 strings total):

| Key | fr-fr | nl-nl | zh-cn | zh-tw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AgentEventsPage_Status_Live | En direct | Actueel | 实时 | 即時 |
| AgentEventsPage_Status_Offline | Hors ligne | Niet verbonden | 离线 | 離線 |
| SkillsPage_EnabledHeaderFormat | Activées ({0}) | Ingeschakeld ({0}) | 已启用 ({0}) | 已啟用 ({0}) |
| SkillsPage_DisabledHeaderFormat | Désactivées ({0}) | Uitgeschakeld ({0}) | 已禁用 ({0}) | 已停用 ({0}) |
| SkillsPage_CountFormat | ({0}/{1} activées) | ({0}/{1} ingeschakeld) | ({0}/{1} 已启用) | ({0}/{1} 已啟用) |
| SkillsPage_BadgeEnabled | Activée | Ingeschakeld | 已启用 | 已啟用 |
| SkillsPage_BadgeDisabled | Désactivée | Uitgeschakeld | 已禁用 | 已停用 |

`nl-nl AgentEventsPage_Status_Offline` uses "Niet verbonden" instead of the loanword "Offline" because the runtime check is `Status == Connected` (a connection state, not user presence) and the all-or-none parity test rejects byte-identical matches. Also stripped a stray UTF-8 BOM from `nl-nl/Resources.resw` so all 5 locales share the same encoding.

- `OpenClaw.Shared.Tests`: 2045 passed / 29 skipped
- `OpenClaw.Tray.Tests`: 936 passed / 0 failed
- Key parity: 1885 entries per locale across all 5 locales

body:
## What

Routes `ci.yml` pull_request jobs to a self-hosted runner on the owner's laptop (labels `self-hosted, linux, x64, leo-laptop`) via a per-job dynamic `runs-on` expression. Push to `main`/`staging`, `workflow_call`, fork PRs, and draft PRs stay on `ubuntu-latest`.

Private-repo PR CI now consumes **zero** GitHub-hosted Actions minutes.

## Changes

- `ci.yml`: workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`; `pull_request` types restricted to `opened/synchronize/reopened/ready_for_review`; dynamic `runs-on` on all 9 jobs with fork guard (`head.repo.full_name == github.repository`) + draft guard. Concurrency unchanged.
- New `e2e-local.self-hosted.yml`: `workflow_dispatch`-only E2E gate on the laptop (`branch` + `scope` inputs, sanitized ref), mirrors `e2e-pr.yml` services.
- New `docs/guides/self-hosted-runner.md` + README link.
- Spec `SPEC-179` formalized (approved).

## Why

GitHub Free private-repo quota (2000 min/mo) exhausts fast (~41 `ci.yml` runs/day). Self-hosted minutes are free/unlimited on private repos.

## Live test

author: kodflow
body:
No point burning a Kaggle GPU session and not publishing the vectors. Flip the `publish` input default false→true; `false` stays available for a throwaway shakedown.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

**What**  
The default value of the `publish` workflow input in the Kaggle embed campaign has been changed from `false` to `true` in `.github/workflows/corpus-embed-kaggle.yml`.

**Why**  
Running a Kaggle GPU session to vectorize data without publishing the resulting vectors is wasteful; publishing should be the default behavior. The `false` option remains available for temporary or throwaway runs.

**How**  
Updated the `inputs.publish` default from `"false"` to `"true"`, which enables the `publish-vec` job (ORAS push of vectorized sub-bases to GHCR `3gpp-vec:latest`) by default when the workflow is invoked via `workflow_dispatch`.

**Risk**  
This is a breaking change in workflow behavior. Existing `workflow_dispatch` invocations that do not explicitly set the `publish` parameter will now publish vectors to GHCR by default instead of skipping publication. Users who relied on the previous opt-in behavior must explicitly set `publish: false` in their workflow calls to preserve the old behavior and avoid unintended artifact pushes.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: prashanthkrishnan91
body:
## Summary

Adds `etf_provider_decision_matrix_v1.py` — backend-only, pure, no-IO single source of truth for ETF holdings provider readiness. Stops the SEC NPORT / AV / FMP patch loop by encoding runtime evidence from Stages 9F/9K/9L/9M as immutable per-provider classifications.

**Roadmap stage:** Stage 9N — ETF provider foundation  
**Build queue item:** ETF fund data provider plan (Stage 9F1)

## Severity
- Level: 2
- Reason: Provider foundation — eliminates token-wasting provider patch loop; encodes evidence-based classifications that block future incorrect retries of known-failed paths.

## Root cause / task reason

Three repeated patch loops confirmed by runtime evidence:
1. **SEC NPORT VTI/SCHD/VXUS** (Stage 9M): CIKs are confirmed wrong entities — 0 NPORT-P filings found for all three. Without a decision matrix encoding this, future sessions would re-investigate the same dead end.
2. **Alpha Vantage** (Stage 9F.3c): as-of date absent in every observed response. Without encoding this, future sessions would attempt to build a canonical AV adapter.
3. **FMP free key** (Stage 9F.4): HTTP 402 returned — paywalled. Without encoding this, future sessions would retry FMP.

## Files changed
- `v2/backend/app/services/intelligence/research_workers/etf_provider_decision_matrix_v1.py` (new) — 8 provider paths classified, S-grade canonical gate, ETF class next paths, JSON diagnostic output, two-field semantic documentation
- `v2/backend/tests/test_stage9n_etf_provider_decision_matrix.py` (new) — 71 fixture tests
- `docs/ai/HANDOFF.md` — updated with Stage 9N outcome and next manual actions
- `docs/ai/USAGE_LEDGER.md` — Stage 9N ledger row added (PR #447)

## Validation
- Commands/checks run: `pytest tests/test_stage9n_etf_provider_decision_matrix.py` → 71 passed. `pytest tests/test_stage9f3c_av_supplemental_classifier.py tests/test_stage9k_etf_provider_wiring.py tests/test_stage9k_diagnostic.py tests/test_stage9l_nport_filing_fix.py tests/test_stage9m_nport_resolver_verification.py` → 192 passed (regression). `python3 scripts/workflow/ai_pr_readiness_check.py` → PASS WITH WARNINGS (advisory only).
- Test tier used + why sufficient: **Tier 1 — pure fixture tests, no IO**. Module is pure (no network, no DB, no LLM). All assertions are on deterministic dict outputs. No infrastructure mocking needed.

### Runtime validation (only when relevant)
- No new runtime calls added. Module is pure/static — no provider calls at import or call time.
- Runtime evidence used as input: Stage 9M runtime results (`POST /api/v1/diagnostics/finance-intel/etf-nport-live-check` VTI/SCHD/VXUS) are encoded as string constants in `runtime_evidence` fields. The stop reason for SEC NPORT VTI/SCHD/VXUS references CIKs 0000764180, 0001477379, 0001004244 and the Stage 9M diagnostic result.
- Failure seam: `sec_nport_vti_schd_vxus.classification == "manual_research_required"` — tests N1–N4 prove this is immutable.

## Product behavior changed
- Yes/No: No
- User-visible impact: None. Backend-only module. No snapshot, no UI, no decision policy change.

## SQL / env / providers / UI
- Supabase SQL required (Yes/No + manual action): No
- Env vars required (Yes/No + manual action): No
- New providers or new LLM calls (Yes/No + details): No — pure static module, no provider calls
- UI changed (Yes/No + details): No

## Risks / limitations

**`canonical_ready` vs `safe_for_decision` — two-field semantic (explicitly documented in module):**
- `canonical_ready=True` means the provider **path** meets all S-grade data criteria (identity + holdings + weights + date + authority + entitlement). It is a property of the classification, not of any live artifact.
- `safe_for_decision=False` is preserved on **every** record in this module. This module is diagnostic/helper-only and does not activate decision policy or write artifacts. An actual holdings artifact must pass the Stage 9K holdings-ready gate before `safe_for_decision` can become True at the artifact level.
- Example: `sec_nport_spy_qqq` has `canonical_ready=True` (SEC NPORT path for SPY/QQQ meets all S-grade criteria) but `safe_for_decision=False` (no live artifact evaluated here; this module only classifies provider paths).
- This semantic is explicitly documented in the module docstring and preserved unchanged.

Other risks:
- All issuer-official paths remain `manual_research_required` until a live CSV fetch confirms URL stability, identity, weights, and as-of date.
- The S-grade canonical gate (`check_canonical_gate`) mirrors Stage 9K exactly and is not loosened.

## AI usage note

**Usage note:** Medium; source: unavailable; main drivers: anchor reads (HANDOFF + 6 source files), module design, 71 fixture tests, doc updates; justified: yes; next efficiency improvement: encode runtime evidence as structured constants at the time of discovery, not in a follow-up stage.

The 3 warnings (file count, line count, mixed areas) are advisory and reflect the accumulated branch diff from all prior stages on this branch, not Stage 9N's 4-file / ~1100-line change. No hard failures.
- Usage ledger row: committed — `docs/ai/USAGE_LEDGER.md` Stage 9N row with PR #447

author: shirganon
body:
## Description

On a guide page, clicking a link in the table of contents scrolled the target heading to the very top of the viewport, where the sticky site header overlaps it — so the section heading you jumped to was hidden behind the navbar (reported in #12977, split off from #12976).

This adds `scroll-margin-top: 6rem` to the headings rendered inside the guide `.prose` content (via a scoped `:global()` selector), so in-page anchor jumps land just below the sticky header. The `6rem` (~96px) offset matches the `~100px` threshold already used in this component to highlight the active heading in the TOC.

Closes: #12977

## AI Disclosure

- [x] I used AI to... draft this fix with Claude Code. I reviewed and understand the change (a standard `scroll-margin-top` anchor-offset for the `{@html}`-rendered guide headings).
- [ ] I did not use AI

## 🎯 PRs Should Target Issues

Targets existing issue #12977 (labelled `bug` / `todo`).

## Testing and Formatting Your Code

⚠️ **Honest note on verification:** this is a CSS-only change to the `_website` SvelteKit app. I was not able to run the website locally in my environment (no `pnpm`, and no browser for visual confirmation), so I could not visually verify the rendered result. The change is a minimal, well-understood `scroll-margin-top` offset on the guide headings, scoped to the guides route. I'd appreciate a maintainer/preview-deploy confirming the visual result.

- Added a `"website": patch` changeset.
- Scope kept to the guides page where the issue was reported; the same approach could be applied site-wide if desired (the original report notes it affects anchor links generally).

- Desktop (lg+): keeps full toolbar with all actions visible inline
- Mobile (<lg): clean command bar with only Valid badge + Reset + More button

- Keyboard shortcuts button hidden on mobile since shortcuts don't apply

- Code area now scrolls both vertically and horizontally
- Long queries no longer overflow the box
- Switched from ScrollArea to native overflow-auto for reliable behavior
- `whiteSpace: pre` with `minWidth: max-content` ensures lines don't wrap

- Table wrapper now uses `position: absolute + overflow: auto` 
- Both horizontal and vertical scrolling work correctly
- Column headers stay sticky at the top while scrolling vertically

- All Radix dropdowns (History, Presets, Select) now have correct background
- Added global CSS targeting `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]` and `[role="menu"]`

- Products expanded from 8 to 20 records  
- Orders expanded from 8 to 20 records
- Wider range of values (age 16–55, purchases 0–88, prices 8–1200)

author: extratoast
body:
## Problem

Frankfurt (8 cores) was reporting `Insufficient cpu` and leaving **stalwart `Pending`** (taking down stalwart + its 4 mail-port checks on the status page), yet `kubectl top` shows the node ~95% idle: auth-api **57m**, assistant-api **51m**, postgres **29m**, rabbitmq **19m**, knowledge-api **78m**. ~7000m of the 8000m budget was **reserved** by inflated requests, not used. That reservation is also what produced the earlier reschedule deadlock.

## Change

Requests sized to measured steady-state + headroom; limits kept or raised so cold start still bursts on the idle node:

| service | request | limit |
|---|---|---|
| auth-api (×2) | 1000m→**400m** | 1000m→**2000m** |
| assistant-api | 1000m→**400m** | 1000m→**2000m** |
| stalwart | 1000m→**300m** | 2000m |
| postgres | 750m→**300m** | 1500m |
| knowledge-api | 500m→**250m** | 1000m |
| n8n | 500m→**250m** | 1000m |
| rabbitmq | 400m→**200m** | 800m |
| valkey | 250m→**150m** | 500m |

Frees ~3.75 cores of reservation (Frankfurt → ~3300m/8000m) so stalwart and everything else schedule with margin. The cold-start CPU need is transient and the node has abundant real CPU, so the raised JVM limits give a *faster* cold-start burst than the old `request==limit==1000m`; CFS only throttles toward the request under genuine contention, which steady-state usage makes moot.

## Validation

- `kubectl kustomize` builds clean for apps-stateless, apps-data, apps-mail, apps-knowledge.

author: aeubanks
body:
For compile time/memory reasons, dag-maps-huge-region is the number of memory instructions at which we create a barrier and reset maps. Previously we'd get to dag-maps-huge-region number of instructions, then add a barrier in the middle of the current set of instructions, and continue processing the second half of remaining instructions.

With this change, now we simply add a barrier every time we reach dag-maps-huge-region number of memory instructions, and blow away all previous instructions.

So now instead of waiting until we get to 1000 memory operations before creating a barrier for 500 of them, we do it at 500 and do it for all 500.

With this change, -dag-maps-huge-region=500 still has addChainDependencies() taking up over half of the codegen pipeline in some cases I looked at, but it's much better than the previous 90%.

author: julian-galluzzo
body:
## What

Adds the ability to rename a project. A project's name is just its folder name on disk, so this does a **real folder rename** — `~/ShipStudio/old-name` → `~/ShipStudio/new-name` — keeping the app, Finder, and VS Code/Cursor all in sync.

Everything risky lives *inside* the project directory and rides along with the move untouched: git remotes (`.git/config`), the Vercel link (`.vercel/project.json`), and all `.shipstudio/project.json` metadata/publish records. Only the stores that key a project by its **absolute path** need rekeying, which this handles.

## Backend

- New `rename_project(old_path, new_name)` command:
  - Rejects external projects and paths outside `~/ShipStudio` (mirrors `delete_project`)
  - Validates the new name (no separators, no `.`/`..`, no leading dot, non-empty, length cap)
  - **Blocks the rename while the project is open in a window or has an active session** — so we never move a directory out from under live PTYs / reserved ports. Suspended pinned sessions are fine and get rekeyed.
- Rekey helpers: `pins::rename_pinned_path` (pin order + resume sessions), `folders::rename_project_path` (folder membership), `state::rename_session_path` (suspended in-memory sessions). Registered in `lib.rs`.

## Frontend

- `renameProject` wrapper in `lib/project.ts`
- "Rename project" item (`EditIcon`) in the card `···` menu, hidden for external projects
- Threaded `ProjectCard → ProjectGridView → ProjectList`
- `ModalFrame` + `Button` rename modal reusing the existing `form-group` pattern (no new CSS)

## Scope (v1)

- **ShipStudio projects only.** External projects keep "Remove from list" (no rename) — easy follow-up by updating `external-projects.json`.
- Not added to the Cmd+K palette — it's a per-row list action, which CLAUDE.md keeps out of the palette (same as per-row delete).

## Testing

- Rust: name-validation + pins-rekey unit tests
- Frontend: `pnpm typecheck` clean, full suite (427) green
- `cargo fmt` + full backend build clean
- Manually verified end-to-end in the running app: rename works, folder renamed on disk, settings preserved

author: lloydmak99
body:
## Problem

`store_chat_signature_from_provider` runs in the completion **hot path** (before `[DONE]`) and fetches the per-chat verification signature from the inference backend. The backend signs in a background task that finalizes *after* the final stream chunk and only then caches the signature — so cloud-api's immediate fetch frequently loses a race and gets `HTTP 404 ("Chat id not found or expired")`.

The error is logged and swallowed, so **the completion still returns fine** — but the chat's signature is never stored, and the response becomes **permanently unverifiable** (the verify path reads only cloud-api's repository and never re-fetches from the provider; after the backend's 1200s cache TTL the signature is gone there too).

Datadog triage: this 404 is **~95%** of the chronic `Failed to store chat signature` errors (`host:cpu02-cloud-api-prod`), running at dozens–hundreds/hr with org-concentrated bursts (a 3,550 burst at 14:00 UTC on 2026-06-01). The affected streams completed normally — **zero** disconnect warnings — confirming a timing/affinity miss rather than aborted streams.

## Fix

`get_signature` previously made a single pass (rotation-SNI → bucket → general LB) and gave up on a 404. This wraps that pass in a **bounded retry**: when *every reachable backend* returns 404 (the signing-race signature), back off briefly and re-fetch — up to 3 attempts with `[100ms, 250ms]` backoff.

- A non-404 status or a transport error (e.g. a **TLS SPKI / attestation mismatch**) stays **definitive** and is never retried.
- Total added hot-path latency is capped at **350ms**, well under the caller's 5s `FINALIZE_TIMEOUT`.
- Successful first attempts are unaffected (zero added latency).
- The backoff schedule lives in a module const with a pure helper, unit-tested for boundedness/termination (a faithful HTTP-level test isn't practical here — the signature clients use TLS-SPKI pinning, so there's no existing mock harness for `get_signature`).

## Testing

- `cargo test -p inference_providers --lib` — 180 passed (incl. new `signature_fetch_backoff_is_bounded_and_terminates`)
- `cargo test -p services --lib attestation` — 20 passed
- `cargo clippy -p inference_providers` — clean

## Scope

Addresses the dominant 404 cause in nearai/infra#160. Does **not** address the separate GLM-5.1 attested-fingerprint drift (the TLS SPKI mismatches) — that's an ops/discovery concern tracked in the same issue.

- **Accepted:** otel empty-data terminality is a deliberate, tested convention.
- **Deferred to 0.4.0:** otel concurrent same-tool span keying (needs a per-call id).

author: arolariu
body:
This pull request updates the local development workflow to fully deprecate Docker Desktop in favor of Rancher Desktop and Podman Desktop as the supported container engines. It revises documentation, VS Code launch profiles, Compose files, and troubleshooting steps to ensure developers use Rancher or Podman for all Aspire and selfhost scenarios. The changes also improve environment variable handling for sensitive data and remove Docker-specific configuration from Compose files.

**Container Engine Migration and Documentation Updates:**

* All references to Docker Desktop are removed or marked as deprecated in `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `infra/Local/readme.md`. Instructions now require developers to use Rancher Desktop (Moby/dockerd mode) or Podman Desktop, including explicit CLI examples for each (`npm run dev -- --engine rancher` or `--engine podman`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a54ff182c7e8acf56acfd6e4b9c3ff41e2c41a31c9b211b2deb9df75d9a478f9L46-R57) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a54ff182c7e8acf56acfd6e4b9c3ff41e2c41a31c9b211b2deb9df75d9a478f9L92-R102) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L315-R324) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L337-R366) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L7-R32) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L65-R69) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L116-R126) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18R168-R262) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L228-R326).
* Troubleshooting sections and logs now reference the new engine-specific commands and clarify that Docker Desktop should not be started as a fallback [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L420-R453) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L240-R345).

**VS Code Integration Improvements:**

* New VS Code launch profiles are added for both Rancher and Podman Aspire full-stack runs (debug and no-debug), making it easy to select the desired engine directly from the editor [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bd5430ee7c51dc892a67b3f2829d1f5b6d223f0fd48b82322cfd45baf9f5e945R17-R50) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bd5430ee7c51dc892a67b3f2829d1f5b6d223f0fd48b82322cfd45baf9f5e945R59-R82).
* Corresponding VS Code tasks are introduced for Aspire runs with Podman and Rancher.

**Compose and Infrastructure Adjustments:**

* All Compose-based SQL Server containers now require the `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD` environment variable to be supplied externally, improving security and aligning with the updated documentation.
* Docker-specific configuration (such as Docker socket mounts and Docker provider settings in Traefik) is removed from Compose and Traefik config files, ensuring compatibility with Rancher and Podman [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-388f83f462bca32146131a5535ed3f96bd4945f2483bc518ebf6fae715d8fc85L34-L41) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7387e0f90ee86d3baaacf32c2c197a4c0f9cedc939ecbaf17a92e8d2fd14c769L12-L15).

**Security and Environment Variable Handling:**

* Documentation now emphasizes that sensitive environment variables (like `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD`) must only be set in the user’s shell/session and never committed to source control, `.env` files, or launch profiles [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L65-R69) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L116-R126).

**Summary of Most Important Changes:**

**Container engine migration and documentation:**
- All docs (`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `infra/Local/readme.md`) now require Rancher Desktop or Podman Desktop for local development; Docker Desktop is deprecated and unsupported. All CLI and troubleshooting examples are updated accordingly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a54ff182c7e8acf56acfd6e4b9c3ff41e2c41a31c9b211b2deb9df75d9a478f9L46-R57) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a54ff182c7e8acf56acfd6e4b9c3ff41e2c41a31c9b211b2deb9df75d9a478f9L92-R102) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L315-R324) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L337-R366) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L7-R32) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L65-R69) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L116-R126) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18R168-R262) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L228-R326) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L420-R453) [[11]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L240-R345)

**VS Code integration:**
- New launch and task profiles for Aspire full stack development with Rancher and Podman engines, supporting both debug and no-debug scenarios. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bd5430ee7c51dc892a67b3f2829d1f5b6d223f0fd48b82322cfd45baf9f5e945R17-R50) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bd5430ee7c51dc892a67b3f2829d1f5b6d223f0fd48b82322cfd45baf9f5e945R59-R82) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7d76d7533653c23b753fc7ce638cf64bdb5e419927d276af836d3a03fdf1745aR44-R55)

**Compose and infrastructure configuration:**
- Removal of Docker-specific Traefik provider and socket mounts from Compose files for Rancher/Podman compatibility. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-388f83f462bca32146131a5535ed3f96bd4945f2483bc518ebf6fae715d8fc85L34-L41) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7387e0f90ee86d3baaacf32c2c197a4c0f9cedc939ecbaf17a92e8d2fd14c769L12-L15)
- SQL Server Compose service now requires `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD` to be supplied via environment variable, not hardcoded.

**Security and environment variables:**
- Documentation clarifies that secrets like `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD` must not be committed and should only be set in the shell/session. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L65-R69) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-12c9f01b23127cb143120c0f568c5ebaf7f91237b1eba4405f2dd30146d79e18L116-R126)

These changes ensure a secure, engine-agnostic, and future-proof local development experience aligned with modern container tooling.

author: w-gitops
body:
## Self-hosted CI for `w-gitops/jinn` on pve21

Runs build + typecheck + test on a **dedicated self-hosted runner on our own hardware** (pve21) instead of `ubuntu-latest`, so the jinn suite (incl. the 329 command-gate tests on `feat/pretooluse-gate`) runs on infra we control.

### Runner
- CT **1120066** (`jinn-ci`, `192.168.200.66`) on pve21 — Debian 13.1, nasnfs rootfs, unprivileged + nesting=1, node v22.22.2.
- GitHub runner **v2.334.0**, name `jinn-ci-1120066`, labels `[self-hosted, linux, pve21]`, **`--ephemeral`** (fresh per job), runs as **non-root `runner`** via systemd. Registered repo-scoped with a single-use token from a fine-grained jinn-only PAT.

### Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- `build` / `typecheck` / `test` → `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, pve21]`, node 22, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm -r build && pnpm -r test`.
- Triggers: `push` + `pull_request` on `dev`, `main`, `feat/**`.
- `live-attack-demo` (PreToolUse gate E2E) = **deferred** `workflow_dispatch`-only job, **no creds wired** (separate secrets review).

### Security guardrails (Knox-reviewed & signed off)
1. **Environment `ci-self-hosted`** with required reviewer `w-gitops` gates every self-hosted job — nothing runs on the runner until approved (primary control; runner is on the trusted LAN with reach to prod).
2. **Same-repo head guard** on every job (`github.repository == 'w-gitops/jinn'` + `pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`) — fork / fork-PR heads never execute on the runner.
3. Repo Actions setting: fork-PR approval = **all external contributors**.
4. **No secrets** referenced; workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`.
5. **Ephemeral**, non-root runner.

**Residuals (recorded by Knox):** required reviewer `w-gitops` is also the pusher → can self-approve (accepted for this no-secrets bootstrap; an **independent approver is a hard gate once creds are wired** for the live-attack demo). Standard CI lifecycle-script exposure, contained to trusted same-repo code on an ephemeral non-root runner.

**Do not merge** — targets `dev`; for COO review.

author: timogilvie
body:
## Summary

- Adds a five-phase failure taxonomy (`artifact_load`, `mlflow_connectivity`, `predict_call`, `response_normalization`, `timeout`) for Model 30 inference so the ~11% 503 rate on `POST /api/v1/models/30/predict` can be classified instead of guessed at.
- Emits one structured `model_30_inference_failure` log record per failure with `request_id`, `model_uri`, `model_version`, `phase`, `path_type` (cold/warm/unknown), `exception_class`, `exception_message`, and `duration_ms`.
- Public response shapes are unchanged: 503 keeps the `"<entry.name> MLflow inference failed: <exc>"` body Strategy Explorer parses; 504 keeps `{error, request_id, run_id}`.
- Observability-first remediation — no retry/gating logic added, because the pre-change logs cannot identify the dominant phase. Acceptance-criteria classification is deferred to the next 24-hour window after deploy, when the new structured query can be run.

## Changes

- `src/api/endpoints/model_30_adapter.py` — add `Model30FailurePhase` enum, `Model30InferenceError`, `_is_connectivity_error()` classifier, `log_model_30_failure()` helper; wrap loader/predict/normalize failures with typed exceptions that carry the originating phase.
- `src/api/endpoints/model_serving.py` — import the new types; record `request_started_at`; route the timeout, cold-load-contention, and catch-all handlers through `log_model_30_failure()` with `path_type` derived from the trace.
- `tests/unit/test_model_30_adapter.py` — five new failure-classification tests, one per phase, plus cold-vs-warm cache discrimination.
- `tests/unit/test_model_serving.py` — endpoint-level assertions for the 503 catch-all, 503 response-normalization, and 504 timeout paths, each verifying the structured record fields.
- `docs/model-30-serving.md` — new "Failure Classes and Observability" section with the full field contract, an example log record, and CloudWatch Logs Insights queries (count-by-phase and recent samples).
- `features/fix-model-30-serving-reliability-failures/INVESTIGATION.md` — evidence window, why the pre-change logs cannot classify the four samples, and the observability-first remediation rationale.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_model_serving.py tests/unit/test_model_30_adapter.py` — 77 passed.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_model_serving.py::test_model_30_predict_mlflow_timeout_returns_504_without_alb_timeout` — verifies the new TIMEOUT phase structured record fires on the 504 path.
- [x] Pre-commit (ruff, ruff-format, auth-header checks) passes on both commits.
- [ ] Manual: after deploy, run the per-phase Logs Insights query in `docs/model-30-serving.md` against the next 24-hour window and update `features/fix-model-30-serving-reliability-failures/INVESTIGATION.md` with the dominant phase before filing the follow-up fix.

## Self-review

- Reviewer: `claude-sonnet-4-6` via `npx tsx /Users/timothyogilvie/Dropbox/wavemill/tools/review-changes.ts auto/integration --json --operating-mode normal`.
- Iterations: 2.
- Iteration 1: verdict `not_ready` — two blockers (missing docs section, INVESTIGATION.md not committed) plus two warnings (timeout-phase test assertion missing, auth.py scope concern). Fixed: added the docs section, created and committed INVESTIGATION.md, extended the timeout test to assert the structured `phase='timeout'` record.
- Iteration 2: verdict `ready` (exit 0). One residual warning re-raised the auth.py scope question — verified false positive: the auth.py edits live in commits `a04b726` / `26bdff5` (HOK-1934, PR #213) which are already on `origin/auto/integration`. The actual PR diff against `origin/auto/integration` is only the six Model 30 files listed above (`git log origin/auto/integration..HEAD` shows only the two HOK-1942 commits).

author: mistakenot
body:
## Summary
- Capture the JSONL `toolUseResult` envelope verbatim into a single new `tool_use_result_json` STRING column on the `messages` parquet, mirror it on the autosearch SQLite index, and surface it (parsed) via `autosearch message describe`.
- Bumps `model.SchemaVersion 2→3` and `indexdb.SchemaVersion 5→6` in lockstep; the autosearch bump auto-triggers a clean index rebuild.
- Makes AUQ picked/recommended-match **and** per-question annotation notes answerable from one SQL statement — no regex over prose, no `tool_input` schema change, no FTS change.

## Phases completed
- [x] Phase 1: auto-etl envelope capture (parser + transform + model + tests)
- [x] Phase 2: autosearch schema + plumbing + CLI (`message describe`)
- [x] Phase 3: E2E SQL test + live-corpus backfill (human acceptance)
- [x] Phase 4: documentation closeout

## Key finding (AC-7) — the structured column corrects the regex baseline
The plan referenced a research baseline of **34/61 = 55.7%** recommended-acceptance. The structured column yields **45/61 = 73.8%** corpus-wide. This is the task's premise validated, not a regression: the 55.7% baseline was a documented regex-over-prose **undercount** (single prose template + fragile adjacency join — reproducing it on the current corpus finds only 41 of 61 real calls). The verbatim envelope finds all 61. Track recommended-acceptance at ~74% going forward. Full detail in `docs/tasks/012-structured-tool-output/acceptance-results.md`.

## Live-corpus backfill results (Phase 3)
| Check | AC | Result |
|-------|----|--------|
| `autoetl run --full` | AC-3 | 809 sessions / 78,766 messages |
| `autosearch index` | — | full rebuild auto-triggered, 78,766 indexed |
| populated rows | AC-3 | 16,167 rows `tool_use_result_json != ''` (≥261) |
| column-set consistency | AC-4 | identical 32-col set across all 13 weeks; week=11 drift removed |
| SQLite parity | AC-5 | 16,167 populated in SQLite — exact parity with parquet |
| per-question notes | AC-8 | 63 rows with `annotations`, notes queryable by question text |

## Issues encountered
- **`autoetl run --full` exit code 1**: caused by the unrelated `github` ETL source hitting a 404 on a missing repo (`mistakenot/gtm-langchain-demo`). The in-scope `sessions` source completed cleanly. Not a task-012 defect.
- **SQLite JSON function**: the project SQLite driver (`modernc.org/sqlite`) lacks `json_extract_string` (a DuckDB-ism). The SQLite path uses plain `json_extract` over string paths; docs/tests updated accordingly.
- **Scope note**: a shared test helper `auto-search/internal/testutil/fixtures.go` was added (not in the original plan file list) to avoid fixture duplication between the two new tests — a scoped test-only addition.
- **Schema doc discrepancy**: `normalized-schema.md` documented schema version `1` (not `2`); corrected to `3`.

## How to test
- `cd auto-etl && go test ./...` — parser/transform envelope capture (AC-1, AC-11a/b)
- `cd auto-search && go test ./...` — SQLite round-trip (AC-5/11c), `message describe` JSON (AC-6/11d), `TestRecommendedAcceptanceFromFixture` (AC-7/8/11e)
- Regression: `content_truncated` golden snapshot unchanged for AUQ rows (AC-9/11f)
- Live (operator): `autoetl run --full && autosearch index`, then the DuckDB/SQLite queries in `acceptance-results.md`

- Acceptance results: docs/tasks/012-structured-tool-output/acceptance-results.md
