author: jamescfer
body:
## Problem

The Epic Destinies panel showed spending as `X / 24` per tree ("out of 24 spent"). **That's not how epic destinies work** — there is no 24-point per-tree cap. V3 had invented `DESTINY_AP_CAP = 24` (with a comment falsely attributing it to `stdafx.h`, which contains no such constant).

## How V2 actually works

Per `DDOBuilder/BreakdownItemDestinyAps.cpp` + `Build::AvailableActionPoints` (`TT_epicDestiny`), Destiny points are a **single shared pool** spent across all (up to 3) selected destiny trees:

```
pool = 4 × epicLevels        (character L20–30, capped at 10 → max 40)
     + 4 × legendaryLevels   (character L30–40, capped at 10 → max 40)
     + floor(fatePoints / 3)             ← FatePoint effects (Epic Past Lives)
     + Σ DestinyAPBonus effects          ← e.g. Epic Completionist
available = pool − totalSpentAcrossAllTrees
```

## Fix

- **`v2Formulas.ts`**: new `destinyPointPool(charLevel, fatePoints)` mirroring the V2 control flow exactly, including the `BUILD_START_LEVEL = 34` special case. (`Build::Level()` is 1-based, matching V3's `build.totalLevel`.)
- **`EpicDestiniesPanel.tsx`**:
  - Removed the fake `24` cap; uses the level-based pool and sums spend across **all** selected trees (previously it passed only the *viewed* tree's spend, so the shared pool wasn't enforced). `TreeGrid` already supported a shared pool via `totalAP`/`totalSpentAllTrees` — it was just being fed wrong values.
  - **Fate points + destiny-AP bonuses are now wired in.** The panel runs the shared `useStaticBundle` + `useBuildStats` pipeline (like the other panels) and folds `stats.total('fatePoint')` and `stats.total('destinyAP')` into the pool — so Epic Past Lives, Epic Completionist, and any gear/enhancement sources all count. The effect parser already maps `FatePoint → 'fatePoint'` and `DestinyAPBonus → 'destinyAP'`.
  - Display now reads `<spent in this tree> · <total>/<pool> destiny points`.
- **Tests**: `destinyPoints.test.ts` (pool at key levels 0/4/40/44/80, the L34 special case, fate-point bonus) and two `effectParser` tests locking the `FatePoint`/`DestinyAPBonus` → stat-key mappings.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors.
- Full webapp suite: **302/302 pass** (incl. the new tests).

author: drago1216
body:
## Summary

The latest sdk-update workflow run made it through composer install + generate + format + lint, then [died at \`make smoke-test\`](https://github.com/BambooHR/bhr-api-php/actions/runs/<run>):

\`\`\`
syntax error, unexpected integer "1", expecting identifier
syntax error, unexpected integer "3958585", expecting identifier
... (8 total)
\`\`\`

PHP identifiers cannot start with a digit, but the generator produced classes like:

\`\`\`php
class 1d64402ee192568adbd5e3179a91e6e2RequestInner extends ...
class 3958585c861325ea7a2cd30a8c74f042Request extends ...
\`\`\`

These are MD5 hashes of operation paths. \`openapi-generator-cli\` falls back to hashing when an inline schema has no \`title\` field AND the operation's \`operationId\` is itself non-identifier-shaped (which for our spec it is — a 32-char hex string).

## Why Python's SDK doesn't hit this

The Python target emits names like \`_3958585c861325ea7a2cd30a8c74f042_request\` (leading underscore + snake_case). Valid Python identifier. The PHP target strips the underscore convention and emits raw hex. Invalid PHP.

## Fix

Post-generation step \`scripts/fix_invalid_class_names.php\`:

1. Finds every \`lib/Model/<digit>*.php\`
2. Renames the class to \`_<original>\` (mirroring Python's convention) and the file to match
3. Rewrites every cross-reference in \`lib/\`, \`test/\`, \`docs/\` (\`use ...\\Model\\1d64...\`, bare \`::class\` refs, etc.)
4. Patches \`.openapi-generator/FILES\` so obsolete-files cleanup doesn't treat the renamed files as stale on the next run

Wired into the Makefile's \`generate\` target after \`cleanup_obsolete_files.sh\`. Re-running is a clean no-op (prefixed names don't start with a digit, scanner finds nothing).

## Verified locally

Built a synthetic fixture: a digit-prefixed model file plus an importing class referencing it. After the fix:
- File renamed
- Class declaration patched
- \`use\` statement + property type hint in importing file updated
- FILES manifest patched
- \`php -l\` reports no syntax errors on either file

## Long-term

The right fix is upstream — either openapi-generator's PHP target gets the same underscore convention the Python target uses, or the source spec gets \`title\` fields on inline schemas. Both are real but out of process for us. This script is the workaround until one of those happens; when it does, delete the script and the Makefile line.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger \`sdk-update.yml\` after merge and confirm \`make smoke-test\` passes against the latest spec.

> **Low Risk**
> Build-time-only rename of generated artifacts; no runtime API or auth changes, with guards against partial file corruption during rewrite.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **post-generation workaround** so the PHP SDK no longer ships **parse-invalid model classes** whose names start with a digit (hash-derived inline schemas from openapi-generator).
> 
> After `make generate`, **`scripts/fix_invalid_class_names.php`** runs: it finds digit-prefixed `lib/Model/*.php`, renames classes/files/docs/tests to a leading-underscore form (aligned with the Python SDK convention), rewrites references across `lib/`, `test/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, and **`.openapi-generator/FILES`**, and exits early if digit-prefixed names appear under `lib/Api/`. The step is **idempotent** on repeat generation.

author: willmurphyscode
body:
Previously, if a path under the root dir of a repo using this tool contained a ":", static-analysis would fail even if the path was gitignored or part of a submodule. The submodule case particularly comes up with repos that submodule anchore/vulnerability-match-labels, which has some weird paths, including paths with ":" in them.

Instead, use "git ls-files" to list files that are tracker or untracked but not ignored (and thus might be added and committed) so that this lint still protects the repo from accepting files with ":" in the path but doesn't fail on gitignored scratchwork or surprising decisions by submodules.

For example, in grype today `static-analysis` only passes if the vulnerability-match-labels submodule has not be initialized.

```
$ make static-analysis
... passes ...
$ git submodule update --init test/quality/vulnerability-match-labels
$ make static-analysis
... fails: ...
 ERROR:
error: unsupported filename characters found
```

author: davyreactiv
body:
### Motivation
- Users with the limited `ufsc_admin_limited` role (example: Hicham) could see a red notice "La page Paramètres UFSC LC n’a pas pu être enregistrée" because the settings page was registered against a parent menu slug that might not exist for limited-admin contexts. 
- The visible UFSC Licences menu and legacy slugs needed to point to a stable canonical licences table view while keeping legacy URLs working. 
- Several legacy capability names and admin-only controls were preventing expected access for canonical `ufsc_*` capabilities or were exposing admin-only pages and notices to non-admins. 

### Description
- Resolve missing-parent settings notice by changing `UFSC_LC_Settings_Page::register_admin_menu()` to pick a valid parent via `resolve_parent_slug()` (check `UFSC_LC_Plugin::PARENT_SLUG`, then `ufsc-licence-documents`, then `options.php`) and require `manage_options` for the settings submenu registration and rendering, and only show the missing-menu notice to actual admins. (file: `includes/admin/class-ufsc-lc-settings-page.php`).
- Make the visible UFSC Licences root menu use a canonical slug `ufsc-sql-licences` by updating `UFSC_LC_Plugin::PARENT_SLUG` and add a landing callback `render_licences_landing_page()` that delegates to `UFSC_LC_Licences_Admin::render_page()`; keep the old slugs (`ufsc-lc-licences`, `ufsc-licences`, `ufsc_lc_licences`) registered as hidden alias sub-pages so legacy direct URLs continue to work. (files: `includes/class-ufsc-lc-plugin.php`, `includes/class-ufsc-licence-documents.php`, `includes/admin/class-ufsc-licences-admin.php`).
- Extend and harmonize menu and page behavior for licences: add `UFSC_LC_Licences_Admin::PAGE_SLUG = 'ufsc-sql-licences'`, make list/table links and redirects use the canonical slug, and expose the requested table columns and non-mutating `Consulter` action; keep mutating actions and import/PDF/status pages protected by `ufsc_licences_manage`. (file: `includes/admin/class-ufsc-licences-list-table.php`, `includes/admin/class-ufsc-licences-admin.php`, `includes/class-ufsc-licence-documents.php`).
- Map legacy capability names to canonical ones and accept additional historical names so `ufsc_competitions_manage` / `ufsc_licences_read` behave as intended for users who have the canonical caps; add a few legacy aliases (`ufsc_licence_manage`, `ufsc_competition_manage`, `ufsc_manage_competitions`) to the capability map. (file: `includes/permissions/ufsc-licences-permissions.php`, `includes/competitions/Capabilities.php`).
- Restrict competition diagnostic and settings server-side checks to `manage_options` so the diagnostic page and its admin_post handler never expose admin-only failures or notices to limited users. (file: `includes/competitions/Admin/Pages/Access_Diagnostic_Page.php`).

### Testing
- Ran PHP lint over changed files with `php -l` and a full `find includes -name '*.php' -print0 | xargs -0 -n1 php -l`; all files reported `No syntax errors detected` (success).
- Searched for the settings-notice string and menu registrations with `rg` to verify the notice source and confirm the new parent/slug usage; the expected occurrences were found and adjusted (success).
- Ran `git diff --check` and repository status checks to ensure no trailing whitespace or index issues (success).
- Performed static checks (names/redirects in templates and code paths) by inspecting diffs of the modified files to confirm canonical slug, legacy aliases, capability mappings, and admin-only guards were applied (success).

Cuts **0.12.384** to PyPI. Carries two already-merged PRs:

- **#2437** — `clawmetry connect` auto-provisions `clawmetry-pro` for entitled cloud accounts (entitlement-gated, never-crashes-connect, idempotent, HTTPS-only) + hardened self-hosted `activate`.

### Why it is safe to ship now
- Cloud side already deployed: `/api/license/entitlement` (fail-closed) + `/api/license/download` (free→402) live; the 0.3.0 pro wheel (with governance) is already in the cloud's `wheels/` so entitled `connect` + licensed `activate` download a governance-capable wheel.

Publishing this OSS wheel to PyPI does not change what the cloud server runs, so paying cloud users keep governance via the existing `oss-passthrough` path. The cloud-pin bump to 0.12.384 needs a `cm-cloud-nemoclaw` interceptor first and is tracked separately.

body:
## Summary

- `useUpdateEvent` now refetches the canonical `events` row via `fetchEventById` instead of relying on the caller to reconstruct it from a `CalendarOccurrence`. Drops `master` from the hook's public API entirely.
- Extracts pure `updateEvent(vars, deps)` orchestrator — testable via DI without React or a real Supabase client.
- Removes the 27-line fake-master construction block from `EventEditScreen.onSave()` and the defensive runtime throw that papered over it.

## Why

The `forward`-scope edit on a recurring series needs the real master row (`family_id`, `type_id`, `rrule_*`) to call `insertSplitEvent`. `EventEditScreen` was hand-building a fake master from `CalendarOccurrence`, which only worked because a defensive `throw` in `mutations.ts` blocked the FK-violation in real usage. With auth live and real data flowing, the workaround needed to go.

The new shape makes the bad-input class **inexpressible at the type level** — `UpdateEventVars` no longer has a `master` field, so the defensive runtime guard is gone too.

## Net diff vs main

4 production files + 1 plan doc:

```
app-sections/event/EventEditScreen.tsx   |  27 ------
docs/TODO.md                             |   2 -
features/calendar/mutations.test.ts      |  89 +++++++++++++++  (NEW)
features/calendar/mutations.ts           |  57 +++++++----
docs/superpowers/plans/...md             | 374 ++++++++++++++++  (plan doc)
```

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test` — 57/57 pass across 10 files (added 2 tests for the orchestrator's unique behaviors: refetch-then-delegate + throw-on-missing)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `bun lint` — no new errors in changed files (pre-existing warnings in `app-sections/auth/`, `app-sections/settings/`, `app/+not-found.tsx` remain unchanged)

## Resolves

Removes both `docs/TODO.md` entries that were blocked on this fix:

- The `EventEditScreen rekonstruiert master-Row aus der CalendarOccurrence` bullet (Calendar section)
- The `Sobald Auth lebt: EventEditScreen-Master-Row-Fix oben` cross-reference (Auth/Onboarding section)

The `rrule_count`-aware forward-split bullet stays on TODO — it's a separate, independent concern in `insertSplitEvent`.

author: jan-ka
body:
## Summary

Resolves #166. The `Pings` module ([foundry-azzurite/pings](https://gitlab.com/foundry-azzurite/pings) v1.4.3, last release June 2025) installs a window-level `mousedown` listener gated by tracking whether the cursor is over `#interface`. In Foundry v14, `ApplicationV2._insertElement` (foundry.mjs ~30486) mounts windows to `document.body` directly — siblings of `#interface`, not descendants — so the module's "over interface" check stays `false` while the cursor is over a sheet. A long-press on a character sheet then triggers a canvas ping.

Upstream module appears unmaintained for v14 and exposes no API to suppress its listener.

## Fix

Opt-in client setting `block_sheet_pointer_bleed` (default **off**). When enabled, a `document.body` bubble-phase `mousedown` listener calls `stopPropagation` for events that originated inside any `.application` or `<dialog>` element. The window-level listener (Pings, or any module of similar shape) never sees those events. Clicks on the canvas (target outside any application) are untouched.

## Why opt-in

Globally blocking sheet→window event propagation could break other modules that legitimately need to see those events. Users only enable this when they're actually affected.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm run test` — 414/414 unit pass
- [x] `tests/smoke/tier-3-sheet-pointer-bleed.spec.ts` (new) — verifies a stand-in window-level mousedown listener fires when the setting is off, doesn't fire on sheet clicks when on, and still fires for clicks outside any sheet
- [x] Full Playwright smoke — **55/55** pass
- [ ] Manual: enable Pings module + the new setting, long-click on a character sheet, verify no ping. Disable the setting, verify ping returns.

Closes #166

author: noopurtrivedi
body:
## Why
`release.yml` runs `electron-builder --publish always`, and electron-builder's GitHub provider **defaults to `releaseType: draft`** — so every release is created as a **Draft** that needs a manual "Publish" click. That click was missed for **v0.1.14**, so it never reached users (0.1.13 stayed "Latest"). 

## What
Add a `publish-release` job that flips the draft → **published + Latest** automatically:
- `needs: build` → runs **only after all 3 platform builds succeed**, so a release is never published half-uploaded, and a failed platform leaves it safely as a draft.
- `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')` → tag pushes only (not `workflow_dispatch`).
- `gh release edit "$TAG" --draft=false --latest` (gh is preinstalled on the runner; `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: write`).

## Why keep electron-builder on draft upload (not publish-immediately)
The 3 matrix runners all append assets to **one** draft. Publishing immediately would let them race on release creation and could expose a release while assets are still uploading. Draft-then-publish is the safe, standard pattern — it's exactly the manual step we've been doing, now automated.

## Note on verification
This is a CI workflow change; it can't be exercised without pushing a tag. YAML validated locally (parses; `publish-release` job wired with correct `needs`/`if`/`run`). It takes effect on the **next** tagged release (v0.1.16+); v0.1.15 is already published.

## why Top-K acceptable-route reconstruction was using exact full-route identity. That undercounts planners that recover the reference route from the target downward but keep expanding below a reference leaf, which is a termination-choice artifact rather than a failure to reconstruct the reference route. ## what changed Scoring now treats the default acceptable-route match as target-rooted prefix identity: the predicted route must be at least as deep as the acceptable route, and its `Route.signature(depth=acceptable.depth())` must match the acceptable route signature. Exact full-route identity remains available through `--acceptable-route-match exact` and the library-level `AcceptableRouteMatch.EXACT`. The selected mode is persisted on `Evaluation` artifacts and score manifests so downstream analyses can distinguish prefix-scored and exact-scored runs. Reports use mode-neutral acceptable-route labeling, while the fixed-depth prefix diagnostics remain separate. ## risk The main behavior change is metric semantics for newly scored evaluations. Existing evaluation artifacts are not rewritten. `analyze` still reads `matches_acceptable` from the stored evaluation, so users must rescore to get prefix semantics. author: yiminnn
body:
## Summary
`Rollout._activate_step_skills` skips uploading scene skills when `skills_dir` is an absolute **str** host path, so deployed SkillsBench task skills never reach the agent — the with-skills arm silently becomes a no-op.

## Root cause
`src/benchflow/rollout.py::_activate_step_skills` gated the upload on the argument **type**:
```python
if isinstance(source_value, os.PathLike) and local_source.is_dir():
    ...upload...
elif source.startswith("/"):
    remote_source = source            # treated as already-in-sandbox, NO upload
elif local_source.is_dir():           # unreachable for absolute paths
    ...upload...
```
The SkillsBench entrypoint always passes an absolute **str** host path (`EvaluationConfig.skills_dir` is typed `str`; the YAML loaders and `_resolve_skills_dir` all `str(...)`). So `isinstance(str, os.PathLike)` is `False`, the host path falls into the `startswith("/")` "already in the sandbox" branch (no upload), and `_link_skill_paths` then `rm -rf`s the discovery dir and `ln -sfn`s it to a host path that does not exist inside the container → **dangling symlink** → the task skill is never discovered.

OpenHands' built-in/public skills load independently, so the catalog still shows those — the deployed **task** skill is the only thing missing.

## Evidence (raw leaderboard trajectories)
- OpenHands with-skills skill delta: **PR2 +13.1pp, PR3 +11.1pp → PR4 −1.1pp**.
- PR4 raw with-skills trajectories: task skill **absent** from `<available_skills>` (only the 42 generic built-ins; byte-identical to the no-skills catalog); `invoke_skill` called **0/10**. PR2/PR3: task skill is the first `<skill>` entry; `invoke_skill` 7/14.
- Bisected to the commit that introduced the `isinstance(..., os.PathLike)` gate.

## Fix
Key the upload on the directory existing on the **host** (the pre-regression behaviour) rather than the argument's type:
```python
if local_source.is_dir():            # real host dir -> upload (str or PathLike)
    ...upload...
elif source.startswith("/"):         # absolute path not on host -> sandbox path from an earlier scene
    remote_source = source
else:
    raise FileNotFoundError(...)
```

## Note on prior intent (please sanity-check)
The gate was meant to treat absolute **str** `skills_dir` values as in-sandbox paths produced by an earlier scene (self-gen flow). That intent is preserved: such sandbox paths (e.g. `/app/generated-skills`) don't exist on the orchestrator host, so `local_source.is_dir()` is `False` and they're still linked as-is with no upload. The only behaviour change is that an absolute str path that **does** exist as a host directory is now uploaded — exactly the SkillsBench case. Existing self-gen tests still pass.

## Test plan
- New regression test `test_scene_skills_upload_absolute_str_host_dir`: an absolute **str** host `skills_dir` is uploaded to `/skills/<scene>` and linked into the agent discovery path.
- `tests/test_scene_outbox_trial.py` — 12/12 pass (incl. existing self-gen tests).
- `tests/test_scene.py tests/test_rollout_config_path_coercion.py tests/test_rollout_branch.py tests/test_agent_setup.py` — 49/49 pass.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `ty check` clean.

---
Draft for maintainer review. Root cause + evidence derived from raw HF leaderboard trajectories (PR2/PR3/PR4) and a git bisect of the skill-deploy path.

## Milestone

M27 — ThreadSanitizer coverage (Phase III)

## Summary

Adds ThreadSanitizer (TSan) as a **data-race correctness gate** for the M24 SPSC ring and the M26
threaded pipeline. TSan instruments memory accesses and synchronization at run time and reports any
data race that ASan/UBSan cannot see — it dynamically validates the acquire/release reasoning in
`docs/memory_ordering.md`. **No engine or pipeline source changed**; this milestone is purely the
sanitizer build/CI/docs wiring.

## Definition of Done

- [x] TSan preset builds the threaded tests; CI runs a TSan job (a dedicated `thread-sanitizer` job).
- [x] Docs state TSan is for data-race detection, not performance; no benchmark numbers under TSan.
- [x] `make tsan` passes; `make check` passes; `PROGRESS.md` updated.

## What changed

- `cmake/Sanitizers.cmake` — `QSL_ENABLE_TSAN` (`-fsanitize=thread`), with a fatal error if combined
  with ASan (the two sanitizers are mutually exclusive — verified).
- `CMakePresets.json` — `tsan` configure/build/test presets.
- `Makefile` — `make tsan` → `ctest --preset tsan -L concurrency`.
- `tests/CMakeLists.txt` — labels the three `tests/concurrency/` executables `concurrency`, so TSan
  runs only the genuinely multithreaded tests (TSan over single-threaded tests adds nothing).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — a dedicated `thread-sanitizer` job.
- `docs/concurrency_model.md` — a ThreadSanitizer section (data-race detection only; honest that it
  is dynamic evidence over executed schedules, not an exhaustive proof of all interleavings).

## Verification

```text
make tsan     # builds -fsanitize=thread; 18 concurrency tests, 0 data races (~3.4s)
make check    # 182/182
# ASan+TSan guard: cmake -DQSL_ENABLE_ASAN=ON -DQSL_ENABLE_TSAN=ON  -> configure error, as intended
```

TSan is verified working on this Linux/clang toolchain; the CI `thread-sanitizer` job runs it on
ubuntu-latest. A green TSan run is dynamic evidence the SPSC ring + pipeline synchronization is
race-free on the exercised schedules — it strengthens, but does not replace, the static
happens-before proof.

## Notes

- Branch `claude/serene-fermi-rhuFJ` (reset to `main` after the M26 squash-merge) per the
  environment's branch rule; carries only M27. Please squash-merge — I don't merge my own PRs.

author: srid
body:
**`just ai::apm` hangs.** `apm compile` pegs one core near 100% CPU and climbs past 4 GB RSS without ever finishing on this repo. The cause is upstream in `apm-cli`: the placement optimizer resolves each instruction's `applyTo` pattern with `glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)`, whose `**` *follows directory symlinks* and ignores its own excluded-dir list — so it walks pnpm's `node_modules/.pnpm` symlink forest through exponentially many paths and never returns.

Kolu is the unlucky intersection that triggers it: we use **pnpm** (a `.pnpm` store with ~2,400 symlinks) **and** ship `**` `applyTo` patterns — notably `applyTo: "**"`. Either alone is fine; together they detonate.

This builds `apm-cli` from the open upstream fix via the **PR head ref** until it lands:

```diff
-apm_cmd := nix_shell + ' uvx --from apm-cli apm'
+apm_cmd := nix_shell + ' uvx --from git+https://github.com/microsoft/apm@refs/pull/1576/head apm'
```

`refs/pull/1576/head` is served from the base repo and resolves to the PR head, so this tracks the fix without referencing a personal fork. The fix filters the optimizer's cached, symlink-safe file walk through APM's existing `**`-aware matcher instead of re-globbing. On this repo the same compile drops from *never finishing* to **~2.5 s** with byte-identical AGENTS.md output. Verified `uvx` builds and runs it from that ref (`APM CLI 0.16.1`).

> **Revert when upstream merges.** Upstream PR: [microsoft/apm#1576](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/pull/1576). Once it merges and a release ships, restore `--from apm-cli`. The `ai.just` comment points back to it.

body:
## Root cause

`DocumentsPanel` fetch effect was keyed on `[user?.id]` only. Because `forms` is a subtab of `documents` via `PANEL_ALIASES.forms → {panel:'documents', subtab:'forms'}`, the panel never remounts when the user navigates Forms→Documents. After `handlePdfSave` called `setActivePanel('documents')`, the effect never re-fired — the just-saved document was invisible in the My Documents list even though it was confirmed in the database.

## Fix (1 line change)

`documents-panel.tsx` line 485: deps changed from `[user?.id]` to `[user?.id, viewMode]`.

When the user returns to the documents view, `viewMode` transitions from `'forms'` to `'documents'` (via the existing subtab-sync effect), triggering the fetch. `viewMode` is never mutated inside the fetch effect, so no render loop is possible.

## TDD proof (fail → pass)

**Hardened P5 assertion** added to `pdf-annotator.spec.ts`: DOM-only check, no page reload, no admin DB bypass — asserts `text=minimal-acroform.pdf` appears in rendered HTML after the forms→documents subtab switch without any navigation.

- **Pre-fix**: P5 fails — `locator('text=minimal-acroform.pdf')` element not found after 15s timeout. P4 (DB check) still passes, confirming the document is in the database — only the UI is broken.
- **Post-fix**: P5 passes — document visible in live DOM after subtab switch, no reload.

## Regression

| Spec | Pre-fix | Post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| pdf-annotator.spec.ts (P1/P2/P3/P4/P5) | P1-P4 pass, **P5 FAIL** | **All 5 pass** |
| forms-flow.spec.ts | 1 passed | 1 passed |
| auth.spec.ts | 4 passed, 1 pre-existing fail | 4 passed, 1 pre-existing fail |

author: opeolipe
body:
PDF and DOCX paths in extractCVText only enforced a 100-char floor after
extraction. Users bypassing the disabled upload button via DevTools or direct
API calls could submit arbitrarily short CVs and trigger unnecessary LLM work.

Add a universal post-extraction gate in handleAnalyze that rejects any CV
whose extracted text is under 1500 chars, regardless of file type. The txt
path already enforced this inside extractCVText; the new gate closes the gap
for PDF and DOCX without duplicating logic across all three branches.

Also extend the test fixture text so the happy-path mocks produce ≥1500 chars,
add a makeShortDOCXBase64 helper for structured-but-thin DOCX payloads, and
add a test that proves the new gate catches a DOCX in the 100–1499-char range.

The Qdrant backends implemented delete(ids=...) as a payload filter on metadata.id, but points are stored with the item id as the Qdrant point id (see _create_points), and not every point carries an id in its payload. Memory points store only {created_at} in metadata (KB metadata embeddings likewise), so deleting a single memory matched nothing and left an orphaned vector that kept being injected into RAG context.

Delete by point id instead: PointIdsList for the standard backend, and a tenant-scoped HasIdCondition for multitenancy (point ids are unique, so tenant isolation is preserved). Filter-based deletion is unchanged.

author: xuyushun441-sys
body:
## Summary

Unblocks `main` — the `apps/docs` Next.js (Turbopack + fumadocs-mdx) production build currently fails:

```
./content/docs/references/kernel/manifest.mdx
82:97: Unexpected character `5` (U+0035) before name, expected a character that can start a name
```

(This is a docs-build regression unrelated to the validation-rules work; it surfaced once the #1485 → #1490 platform-objects regression was cleared and the pipeline reached the docs build.)

## Root cause

`packages/spec/scripts/build-docs.ts` generates the reference MDX from the Zod schemas. Its `escapeMdxDescription` only backtick-wrapped **matched** `<…>` / `{…}` pairs. A **lone** `<` with no closing partner — e.g. the SemVer range in `manifest`'s `platform` field, `.describe('... ">=4.0 <5"')` — was emitted raw, and MDX read the `<5` as the start of a JSX tag.

## Fix

- An unmatched `<` / `{` is now emitted as its HTML entity (`<` / `{`) so it renders literally and never opens a JSX/expression node. Matched pairs keep their existing backtick-wrapping; fragments already inside inline-code spans are still left untouched.
- Union-variant descriptions (previously emitted raw) now also go through the escaper.

Only the generator changes — the committed generated `.mdx` is regenerated by the build (`gen:schema && gen:docs && next build`), so no generated content is included here.

## Verification

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/docs build` (full gen + `next build`) **completes successfully**. A sweep of all generated `content/docs/references/**` confirms no remaining unmatched `<` outside code spans (`>=2.0.0 <3.0.0` style ranges are inside backticks and unaffected).

author: akapug
body:
Right now `McpManager` only supports **stdio** and **headerless SSE**, so Odysseus cannot connect to any *authenticated remote* MCP server — but GitHub, Linear, Sentry, Cloudflare and most hosted/SaaS MCP servers speak **Streamable HTTP** with a `Bearer`/token header. This adds that transport.

### What this adds
- **`transport: "http"`** (aliases `streamable-http`/`streamable_http`) via the MCP SDK `streamablehttp_client`, correctly unpacking its **3-tuple** `(read, write, get_session_id)` (vs SSE/stdio 2-tuple).
- **Per-server `headers`** (e.g. `{"Authorization": "Bearer ..."}`) plumbed through `connect_server` → `_connect_http`, and into `_connect_sse` (SSE accepted no headers before).
- **`headers` column on `McpServer`** + a lightweight `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` migration (matches the existing `_migrate_add_*` pattern) so configs persist + reconnect on restart.
- **Admin add-server UI**: a "Streamable HTTP" transport option + a "Headers (JSON)" field (shown for sse/http), validated as JSON before submit.
- **Tests** (`tests/test_mcp_http_transport.py`, 8): transport routing (http/sse), header passthrough, default-`{}`, unknown-transport → False, and the 3-tuple/2-tuple unpack.

### Compatibility
Purely additive — stdio/SSE behaviour is unchanged; `headers` is nullable; the migration is idempotent.

### Testing
`pytest tests/test_mcp_http_transport.py` → 8 passed. Verified end-to-end against a live authed remote MCP server: it connects via Streamable HTTP with a Bearer header and lists its tools, no stdio bridge needed.

author: kevung
body:
Completes the **headless** chantier (`tasks/headless/`): blunderDB can now run as a network daemon and a multi-tenant engine over a pluggable storage layer, while the desktop GUI and the historical CLI keep working unchanged.

29 commits, ~120 files. All work lands behind the `Storage` interface; the `Database` wrapper (GUI binding) is preserved.

## Highlights

### `blunderdb serve` — HTTP+JSON daemon (P6)
- `internal/server`: RPC-style routes `POST /v1/<family>.<method>` over all 14 Storage families (100+ handlers), NDJSON streaming, frozen error envelope (closed code set), `/healthz` `/readyz` `/metrics`, tenant (`X-Tenant-ID`), logging, metrics, recover, CORS middlewares.
- Imports/exports over Storage (`pkg/blunderdb/ingest`): XG, GnuBG (SGF/MAT), BGBlitz (BGF), native `.db`, XGP + BGF-text positions — each parity-gated against the legacy `Database` importer; cross-format canonical-duplicate enrichment.

### PostgreSQL backend (P3)
- Full Storage implementation on `pgxpool` with per-tenant `tenant_id` scoping: positions/analyses/search, matches/games/moves, tournaments/collections, comments/anki, filters/history/metadata, **stats**, **session**.
- The backend-agnostic **contract suite is green on both SQLite and PostgreSQL with zero skips**.
- **Row-Level Security** (opt-in defence-in-depth): `serve --rls` installs fail-closed per-tenant policies and sets `app.tenant_id` per pooled connection.

### Storage-layer completion
- **Stats** ported to both backends (`StatsStore`), gated by JSON parity vs the legacy implementation (SQLite) and a cross-backend parity test (Postgres).
- **P2 PR6**: `Storage.Migrate` upgrades pre-existing older-version SQLite databases via the shared migration chain (registration hook, no import cycle) — `serve`/`migrate`/`call` now handle legacy `.db` files.
- **P4**: per-scope session state on both backends; SQLite `scope` columns on command/search history + filters (**schema 2.9.0**) so a multi-tenant SQLite-server isolates them.
- **P5 PR1**: per-connection PRAGMAs (busy_timeout) + pool sizing + `-race` concurrency tests.

### Tooling
- **CLI 100% coverage** (P7): `blunderdb call <family>.<method>` dispatches in-process through the live server handlers.
- **`blunderdb migrate`** (Phase B): SQLite → PostgreSQL copy over the Storage interface, per tenant.
- **Per-tenant rate limiting** (Phase C): opt-in token bucket, `serve --rate-limit-rps`.
- **Benchmarks** (P9): microbenchmarks (both backends), self-contained `cmd/blunderdb-loadtest`, and a measured `tasks/headless/perf-baseline.md`.

## Compatibility
- The desktop binary (`wails build`) and the historical CLI subcommands are unchanged. The GUI-bound `Database` wrapper is preserved and delegates to Storage.
- SQLite stays the default (GUI/CLI/desktop); PostgreSQL is the path to many tenants. The empty scope used by GUI/CLI is byte-identical, so existing desktop databases migrate transparently.

## Testing
- `go test ./...` and `go test -tags postgres ./...` (testcontainers Postgres) green; `-race` green on the storage layer.
- New: contract suite (both backends), tenant-isolation, RLS isolation (non-superuser role), import parity gates per format, cross-backend stats parity, legacy-DB migration over storage, concurrency tests.

See `tasks/headless/README.md` for the full phase map and per-phase notes.

author: tim-brooks
body:
The batch indexing path wrote one Translog.Index record per op. Write
the whole sub-batch as a single Translog.IndexBatch record instead:
SUCCESS ops become IndexOp entries carrying their row position in the
EIRF slice, and a seqNo-consuming failure becomes a NoOpOp so the
seqNo stream stays contiguous on replay.

Extract applyNoOpToLucene from innerNoOp so the no-op tombstone can be
folded into the batch record rather than emitting a standalone
Translog.NoOp; innerNoOp keeps its single-op behaviour.

Engine.indexBatch, IndexShard, and ShardBatchIndexer now take the
EirfBatch to slice each sub-batch and carry its row sources. Batched
docs store a null translog location, so realtime GET falls back to a
refresh + Lucene read.

author: jacksonweber
body:
# Description

Fixes the [MSRC 119493](https://portal.microsofticm.com/imp/v5/incidents/details/31000000623459/summary) defect family in the Node.js exporter, mirroring the Python fix in [Azure/azure-sdk-for-python#47265](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/pull/47265).

## Defect

`sdk/monitor/monitor-opentelemetry-exporter` disables `@azure/core-rest-pipeline`'s `redirectPolicy` (`httpSender.ts`) and handles 30x responses itself in `baseSender.ts`. On any 307/308 the previous `handlePermanentRedirect`:

- accepted **any** `Location` host with no origin allowlist;
- mutated `appInsightsClientOptions.host` and rebuilt the `ApplicationInsightsClient`, persisting the new host for the lifetime of the exporter; and
- on the recursive `exportEnvelopes` call, the rebuilt pipeline still contained `bearerTokenAuthenticationPolicy` (when a `credential` is configured), so a freshly-signed AAD token for `https://monitor.azure.com/.default` plus the telemetry envelope were POSTed to the redirect target.

This is the same code-shape MSRC paid out against the Python exporter (#119493), the .NET exporter (researcher Finding #12), and the Java exporter (researcher Finding #14).

## Fix

- New `ALLOWED_REDIRECT_DOMAIN_SUFFIXES` constant (`Declarations/Constants.ts`) listing the canonical Azure Monitor / Application Insights ingestion suffixes across public, US Gov, and China clouds (identical list to the Python PR).
- New `isSameRegisteredDomain(currentHost, redirectHost)` helper (`utils/redirectUtils.ts`) that returns `true` only when the redirect target is an **exact host match** for the configured ingestion host, or when **both** hosts live under the **same** trusted suffix. Customers with a custom ingestion host therefore still get the single-hop "remember the redirect" UX for an exact-host redirect, but server-issued cross-host redirects are refused.
- `HttpSender.handlePermanentRedirect` now returns a `boolean`: `false` (without mutating any state) when the redirect would cross the trust boundary, `true` otherwise. The abstract signature on `BaseSender` is updated to match.
- `BaseSender.exportEnvelopes` treats a `false` return as a non-retriable failure: it does **not** recurse into another `send`, surfaces an `ExportResultCode.FAILED` with a `Refused cross-origin redirect` error, and counts the exception via `networkStatsbeat.countException` / `customerSDKStatsMetrics.countDroppedItems(DropCode.CLIENT_EXCEPTION, ..., ExceptionType.CLIENT_EXCEPTION)`.
- Diag log added at `error` level when a refusal occurs so operators can identify the misbehaving server / proxy.

## Tests

- New `test/internal/redirectUtils.spec.ts` covering exact-match, same-suffix, cross-suffix, untrusted-parent (PoC scenario), trusted↔untrusted, empty inputs, user-info / port, and case / trailing-dot normalization.
- New `BaseSender` test: `should refuse cross-origin redirects without retrying` — asserts `send` is invoked exactly once, the result is `FAILED` with `Refused cross-origin redirect`, and `networkStatsbeat.countException` is called.
- New `HttpSender` test: `should refuse a cross-origin redirect and not leak telemetry to a foreign host` — uses `nock` to assert the exporter does **not** POST to the attacker host and that `appInsightsClient.host` remains the originally configured `DEFAULT_BREEZE_ENDPOINT` (no persistent host poisoning).
- Existing `HttpSender` redirect tests that redirected from `dc.services.visualstudio.com` to `ukwest-0.in.applicationinsights.azure.com` (which crosses trusted suffixes and would now be refused) are retargeted to `westus.services.visualstudio.com`, matching the Python PR's analogous test update.
- Existing `BaseSender` test mock returns `true` by default so legacy positive-path tests continue to exercise the success branch; the circular-redirect test is unaffected (refusal is gated by `numConsecutiveRedirects < 10`).

## Verification

- `pnpm turbo build --filter @azure/monitor-opentelemetry-exporter... --token 1` — green.
- `pnpm format` / `npm run lint` — green (only pre-existing warnings, none from new code).
- Full vitest suite: **20 files, 347 tests, all passing.**

## Version

Bumps `@azure/monitor-opentelemetry-exporter` from `1.0.0-beta.42` to `1.0.0-beta.43`.

## Checklist

- [x] **The pull request does not introduce [breaking changes]** — the only public surface change is `handlePermanentRedirect`'s return type on `BaseSender`, which is `@internal`.
- [x] CHANGELOG updated under `1.0.0-beta.43 (Unreleased)`.
- [x] Tests added for the security-relevant behavior.

## Summary

Surfaces the shadow-misfire correction on `TurnResult` and emits a full itemized interest breakdown so the UI can reconcile the net interest delta across all contributing sources.

## Changes

### New: `InterestBreakdownItem` type
```csharp
public sealed class InterestBreakdownItem
{
    public string Source { get; }  // stable key: base_roll | risk_tier | combo | shadow_misfire | horniness_trope_trap | delay_penalty
    public string Label  { get; }  // human-readable
    public int    Delta  { get; }  // signed
}
```

### `TurnResult` additions
- `ShadowInterestDelta` (int) — the shadow-misfire correction value; previously computed in `DeliveryStage` and applied to interest but never exposed. Wired from `deliveryStage.ShadowCorrection` in `TurnOrchestrator.Resolve.cs`.
- `InterestBreakdown` (IReadOnlyList\<InterestBreakdownItem\>) — itemized per-source list. Only non-zero components are included. **Sum invariant: `breakdown.Sum(x => x.Delta) == InterestDelta`.**

### Sources defined
| Key | Label | From |
|---|---|---|
| `base_roll` | Base roll | `BaseInterestDelta` (SuccessScale / FailureScale) |
| `risk_tier` | Risk tier bonus | `RiskBonusDelta` |
| `combo` | Combo bonus | `ComboBonusDelta` |
| `shadow_misfire` | Shadow misfire correction | `ShadowInterestDelta` ← DeliveryStage.ShadowCorrection |
| `horniness_trope_trap` | Horniness trope-trap | `HorninessInterestPenalty` |
| `delay_penalty` | Delay penalty | `delayPenalty` (defined, always 0 in current interest path) |

## Tests (Issue768_InterestBreakdownTests, 14 tests)
- Sum invariant: success-only, success+risk, combo, shadow_misfire, horniness variants
- Zero-delta filter

- **Live session 41cc7a50 regression**: roll 19 vs DC 17, Hard risk (+3), Dread Misfire shadow overlay (correction = −1 − 4 = −5), net delta −1 (interest 10→9). Asserts shadow_misfire line present with delta=−5, sum=−1.

body:
## Summary

- Badges can now reference [Simple Icons](https://simpleicons.org/) brand logos as `icon: si:<slug>` (e.g. `si:kubernetes`, `si:docker`, `si:grafana`), in addition to the existing `icon: mdi:<name>`.
- The icon pipeline is generalized into a small **set registry**: a `<set>:<name>` reference splits on the first `:` and dispatches to the right embedded table (`mdi` or `si`), erroring clearly at startup on an unknown set or name. The renderer was already set-agnostic, so icons render **white**, exactly like MDI.
- Simple Icons are built and embedded the same way as MDI — a gzipped `name\tpath` table generated from the `simple-icons` npm package by `cmd/genassets` at build time (not committed), decoded lazily on first use. `genMDI` was refactored into a reusable `genIconSet` helper.

## Details

- `cmd/genassets/main.go`: `genIconSet(label, dir)` helper + new `si.txt.gz` step reading `node_modules/simple-icons/icons`; `mdiPathRe` → `svgPathRe`.
- `internal/kromgo/icons.go`: shared `decodeIcons` helper; new `//go:embed assets/si.txt.gz` set with a lazy `siIcons` loader.
- `internal/kromgo/badge.go`: `iconSets` registry + generalized `resolveIcon`.
- `package.json`: add `simple-icons@16.22.0` (CC0-1.0); lockfile updated. `.gitignore`, `.mise.toml`, `Dockerfile` updated for the new generated asset.
- Docs: README Icons + Building-from-source sections, and the `Badge.Icon` struct comment.

Note: the Simple Icons set adds ~1.9 MB compressed to the binary (vs ~0.8 MB for MDI), since brand-logo paths are more detailed.

## Test plan

- [x] `go run ./cmd/genassets` builds both tables (7,447 MDI / 3,438 Simple Icons)
- [x] `go test ./...` passes (incl. new `si:` resolution, two-set embedded check, `/assets/si.txt.gz` 404)

body: ## Summary This branch lands two features against `main` (which has neither yet). They were built and reviewed as separate `/mission` runs but share this branch and can't be cleanly split — the trace work sits on top of the sandbox base. ### 1. Sandbox destinations (replaces the old `--fork`) Choose where the backtest branches + PR are created, decoupled from where the PR is read: - `--primary` — land in the PR's own repo (no prompt). - `--sandbox ` — land in a separate repo you control; the source PR is still only **read**, the original repo is never written to (commits come from a `source` remote). - `--create-sandbox` — with `--sandbox`, create the destination repo (always **private**) if missing. - Interactive prompt (TTY, no flag) can remember a default destination. `--primary`/`--sandbox` are mutually exclusive. ### 2. Live activity trace + `--verbose` Turn the safety guarantee into something you can watch: - **Default view:** each operation shows a friendly `✓` completion marker; on a TTY a slow clone/fetch/push shows an in-progress line replaced in place by its completion line. All trace on **stderr**; stdout stays exactly the PR URL. - **`--verbose`:** one dim line per GitHub API request (method, path+query, status, ms) and per git command (real argv, ms), in real time. Off by default; no `-v` collision. - **Trust enforcement:** every API request flows through one Octokit hook that **hard-errors on any host ≠ `api.github.com`**. Displayed git commands are the real ones and carry no token (token via `GIT_ASKPASS`, never in URL/argv); `redact()` is the final net on every line. ## How it was built & verified Both features were executed via the `/mission` multi-agent flow (written contract → workers in isolation → fresh `code-reviewer` validator). Live-activity-trace: **16/17 assertions passed, 1 blocked** (lint — no linter configured; tsc strict is the gate). Then this branch went through `/gstack-review` (clean, no criticals), `/gstack-cso` security audit (clean — token handling, redaction net, host assertion, no third-party egress all verified), and `/gstack-devex-review` (7.5/10; CHANGELOG correction applied here). - `npm run build` (tsc strict): clean - `npm test`: **141 pass / 1 skip** (the skip is the pre-existing network-gated integration test) - No new runtime dependency (still `@octokit/rest`, `chalk`, `commander`, `prompts`, `simple-git`) - No behavior/exit-code change from tracing (observation only) ## Notes - Mission artifacts live under `specs/*/mission/` (contracts, validation state, validator synthesis). - `main` currently predates both features, so the diff is large (~38 files); the implementation is well-scoped per the commit history. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) > [!NOTE] > ### Add `--verbose` live activity trace and sandbox destinations to `runBacktest` > - Adds a `--verbose` CLI flag that enables per-request and per-git-command trace output on stderr, including method, path, status, and elapsed time for all Octokit calls and equivalent git commands with timing. > - Implements a `traceOp`/`verboseLine` trace subsystem in [`src/log.ts`](https://github.com/govambam/pr-backtest/pull/4/files#diff-dafa5ebe0f463a0ac93f64787d8ca777a93d8b37aa8eaecde92c469b86430a06) that renders in-place on TTYs (carriage return) and as completion-only lines on non-TTYs; all output is redacted of secrets. > - Installs a request hook in [`src/github.ts`](https://github.com/govambam/pr-backtest/pull/4/files#diff-a248ff5ec76368168c745273fee0601b243545fdca37aa3bec76ef9e9365fdb7) `makeOctokit` that asserts all API calls target `api.github.com` and emits trace lines in verbose mode. > - Instruments git operations in [`src/git.ts`](https://github.com/govambam/pr-backtest/pull/4/files#diff-2ea4750851b34def3ddd617afa64e175a87064a29dbb9e6fd20eee6f1dd6dc93) (clone, addRemote, fetch, push) with trace markers and verbose command echoes; displayed commands never include tokens. > - Refactors [`src/index.ts`](https://github.com/govambam/pr-backtest/pull/4/files#diff-a2a171449d862fe29692ce031981047d7ab755ae7f84c707aef80701b3ea0c80) `runBacktest` to use a dependency-injection interface (`RunBacktestDeps`) for all external collaborators, with production defaults, enabling full-flow testing. > - Risk: `resolveToken` now routes through `makeOctokit` instead of `new Octokit` directly, applying the request hook (host assertion + tracing) to the initial `GET /user` validation call. > > > > Macroscope summarized a9e9463. > >

body:
## Summary
- `build_signal_data()` injected `_kestrel_producer_version` inside the signal `data` block — the object the runtime validates against the `external_scanner` `config.fields` allowlist. The undeclared key triggers `INVALID_REQUEST` ("received undeclared data field '_kestrel_producer_version'"), silently dropping **every** Kestrel signal. The helpers SDK catches the rejection so the daemon tick still reports `status:ok` — the failure only shows in the `signal_post … status:rejected` / `push_signal failed` log lines.
- Kestrel was the **only** fleet producer putting its version tag in the validated payload; cheetah/dire/etc. keep it in `cfg.output(...)` logs only. This is the same class of silent-producer bug as v3.0.2 (a malformed signal field rejected by the runtime), different field.
- Fix: removed the tag from `build_signal_data()`; retained in all six `cfg.output(...)` log sites so the running version stays visible in `/tmp/kestrel-producer.log`.
- **Do NOT** "fix" this by declaring the tag in `runtime.yaml` — that bakes a producer-internal debug field into the scanner contract, which no other agent does.

## Files
- `kestrel/scripts/kestrel-producer.py` — VERSION 3.0.2 → 3.0.3; remove tag from `build_signal_data()`; add in-code guard comment.
- `kestrel/SKILL.md` — metadata version 3.0.2 → 3.0.3.
- `kestrel/README.md` — v3.0.3 changelog entry.

author: fiberjw
body: > [!IMPORTANT] > **Superseded by a reviewable stack** (merge bottom-up): #50 deps/config → #51 GraphQL codegen restructure → #52 Apollo hardening → #53 UI cleanup → #54 mutations + react-doctor → #55 anime pagination. #56 (website) is independent. The stack tip is tree-identical to this branch except the stale chunk-pagination plan docs were dropped. Once the stack merges, this PR can be closed. ## Why React Doctor reported correctness, performance, and maintainability issues across the app. The highest-impact items were: - `.expo` was not fully ignored, which risks committing machine-specific simulator/device history and dev-server settings. This is repo hygiene rather than a user-facing bug, but it can create noisy or misleading diffs. - Several `FlatList` screens rebuilt `renderItem` callbacks on every screen render. On real devices that can make rows do extra work, which shows up as avoidable list jank on larger lists or slower phones. - Image-heavy screens used `Image` from `react-native`, which does not provide Expo Image's caching behavior. Users can see more reloads, flicker, and repeated image fetches while browsing anime, character, profile, and landing-page imagery. After fixing those, I continued through the remaining React Doctor output so the full scan is clean instead of leaving follow-up warnings in the same branch. ## How - Ignored the whole `.expo/` directory. - Installed and configured `expo-image`, then migrated app and website image usage from `react-native` image components to Expo Image where React Doctor flagged caching-sensitive usage. - Stabilized `FlatList` callbacks and key extractors in the related anime, character, profile, discover, and anime list flows. - Removed list item `key` props that were duplicating list-owned keys. - Cleaned up React correctness issues found by the full scan, including async effects, async `forEach`, prop-to-state sync effects, constructed context values, manual memoization that was no longer needed, index keys in skeleton lists, dynamic ScrollView padding, and unsupported React Native shadow styling. - Split the large details screen into smaller module-level components so it no longer trips the giant component rule. - Moved GraphQL operations/fragments from TS modules into `.graphql` documents, regenerated `graphql/generated.ts`, and added a small codegen postprocess step that keeps generated-only helpers module-private when the app does not import them. - Removed stale generated/source GraphQL files, unused constants/declarations, and no-longer-needed dependencies. ## Test Plan - `bun run gql` - `bun run lint` - `npx tsc --noEmit` - `git diff --check` - `npx react-doctor@latest --verbose` - Result: `No issues found!` - Score: `100 / 100` Manual simulator QA was not run in this pass; validation was focused on React Doctor plus local static checks. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes React Doctor findings and switches the Anime tab to server‑sorted, page‑based pagination for faster first load and stable scrolling. Improves networking, caching, startup resilience, and iOS EAS runtime fingerprinting; also unblocks EAS builds (Android SDK 36, `eas-cli` >=16). - **Performance** - Anime tab: page‑based `Page.mediaList` with cache‑layer page merge and infinite scroll; stable server sort; handles refetch/fetchMore races and partial merges; empty‑list skeleton no longer hangs; faster first paint. - Networking/startup: 30s fetch timeout; `RetryLink` avoids replaying aborted mutations and skips retries on network drops; dangling refetch rejections are caught; cache persistence falls back to memory so startup won’t hang; spinners no longer stick. - Images/UI/a11y: moved to `expo-image` with caching and `contentFit`; stable list keys; debounced search and mutations now await and surface errors; optimistic progress/score overrides clear correctly; favorites and “Add to list” stay in sync; trailers open via `expo-web-browser`; header uses safe‑area insets; 44pt hit targets and labels. - **Refactors** - GraphQL: operations moved to `.graphql`; regenerated `graphql/generated.ts` (enums‑as‑types, no refetch); `Page.mediaList` merges pages in the cache (dedupes, drops non‑contiguous deep pages on refetch races); next page derives from loaded count using ceil to avoid re‑request loops; helpers + tests. - Client/startup: `@apollo/client` persistence via `apollo3-cache-persist` falls back to memory; `Accept: application/json`; conditional Sentry/Vexo init; logout uses `client.clearStore`. - Dependencies/CI: synced Expo SDK 55 and added `expo-image` plugin; Android compile/target SDK 36 and buildTools 36.0.0; require `eas-cli` >=16.0.0; `.fingerprintignore` now ignores `node_modules/**/*.podspec.json` to fix iOS runtime fingerprint mismatches on EAS; ignore `.expo/`, `ios/`, and `android/`; README scripts renamed; React Doctor 100/100 and `expo-doctor` 19/19. Written for commit 1bf82eb440e24c2e19723c029e85d949cf4a9c77. Summary will update on new commits.

author: kdeyarmin
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two genuine code gaps surfaced by the communications audit (calls / texts / chat / email). The other audit findings were intentional product/physics boundaries (free-text inbound-email AI classification deferred per ADR 013; no typed reply on a live phone call) and are not code changes.

### 1. Account assistant goes Claude-first (`POST /shop/me/chat`)
Previously this route read `OPENAI_API_KEY` directly, so a deployment configured exactly as the docs recommend — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` only — left the **signed-in** account assistant silently offline while the storefront chatbot and sleep coach worked. It now routes through `selectLlmProvider()` like the other two surfaces: Claude Sonnet 4.6 first, gpt-4o-mini fallback, then a static offline reply. Adds an Anthropic JSON + SSE-streaming path that reuses the existing async, customer-scoped tool dispatcher (the four `get_my_*` DB tools behave identically whichever vendor answered). System prompt is wrapped in a `cache_control` block.

### 2. ElevenLabs is now the agent's voice on the live phone path
When `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` is set, ElevenLabs becomes the voice:
- The OpenAI Realtime session runs in **text-output mode** (`generateAudio: false`) — the model emits `response.output_text.*` instead of audio.
- `VoiceBridge` gains a `TtsSynthesizer`: each finalised agent turn is synthesised through ElevenLabs (`ulaw_8000`), re-framed to 160-byte µ-law frames, and streamed to Twilio.
- Caller **barge-in** (`input_audio_buffer.speech_started`) aborts the in-flight synthesis (real `AbortSignal` → cancels the ElevenLabs fetch) and flushes the Twilio sink.
- Utterances are synthesised one at a time so frames reach the sink in order.

**Graceful degradation (preserved):** when `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` is unset the bridge forwards OpenAI's built-in **cedar** audio unchanged — a missing vendor key never breaks a call. A mid-call ElevenLabs error drops just that utterance's audio (logged as a `tts` session error) and the call continues.

> ⚠️ **PHI / BAA:** synthesised agent speech is patient-facing PHI. The ElevenLabs BAA (Enterprise tier) must be in place before enabling against real patients. There's also a small per-turn TTS latency vs. cedar's native speech-to-speech. Both are called out in `CLAUDE.md` and `.env.example`.

## Files
- `lib/resupply-ai`: `realtime-client.ts` (text-output mode + `input.speech_started` + text-output event mapping), `bridge.ts` (`TtsSynthesizer`, synthesis queue, barge-in), `elevenlabs-client.ts` (`AbortSignal` support), `index.ts` (re-export ElevenLabs + `TtsSynthesizer`).
- `artifacts/resupply-api`: `voice-config.ts` (read `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`/`_VOICE_ID`/`_MODEL_ID`), `ws-handler.ts` (synthesizer adapter + `generateAudio`/`tts` wiring), `routes/shop/me-chat.ts` (Claude path).
- Docs: `CLAUDE.md`, `.env.example`.

## New env vars (all optional)
`ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID`, `ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID`.

## Testing
- `@workspace/resupply-ai`: 146 passed — new tests for Realtime text-output session config, text-output/`speech_started` event mappings, and bridge TTS (audio.delta suppression, synthesis on output turns, no synthesis of caller turns, in-order queueing, barge-in abort + late-frame drop + sink flush, synthesis-failure → `tts` session error without closing the call).
- `@workspace/resupply-api`: full suite passing (4013) — added a Claude-path test for `/shop/me/chat`; offline tests updated to clear both keys.
- `tsc --build`, ESLint (0 warnings), Prettier, and `check-resupply-architecture.sh` all green.

body:
Fixes a `NameError` in the unsupported-modality error path.

### Evidence
`core/app/infra/generation/execute.py:327` — the "Unsupported modality pair" error emit passed a bare `artifact_type` as a kwarg to `emit_modality_event`:

).model_dump(), artifact_type=artifact_type,   # L327 — bare, undefined here

### Fix

# Based on PR #1126

## Chain of upstream PRs as of 2026-06-03

* PR #1166:
  `master` ← `lsierant/devcontainer`

  * PR #1048:
    `lsierant/devcontainer` ← `search/ga-base`

    * PR #1126:
      `search/ga-base` ← `search/simulated-mc`

      * **PR #1177 (THIS ONE)**:
        `search/simulated-mc` ← `search/simulated-mc-comprehensive-tests`

<!-- end git-machete generated -->

## Summary

Stacked on top of #1126 (`search/simulated-mc`). Elevates the simulated-multi-cluster MongoDBSearch tests from basic/scaffold to **comprehensive**, and fixes a startup-timing race in the sharded path that the new coverage exposes.

Three reviewable commits:

1. **`test(search)`: comprehensive Go unit tests** — full-`Reconcile()` coverage for the Envoy reconciler in simulated-MC mode (no-match silent no-op; missing-`clusterIndex` Invalid with message pin; renders at the *resolved* pinned index, not spec-array position); a Failed-first multi-cluster worst-of-phase aggregation test (mutation-verified); message pin on the main-controller enforcement subtest; `AssignClusterIndices` last-write-wins row.
2. **`test(search)`: comprehensive simulated-MC e2e** — RS now proves the **per-cluster data plane** end to end (per-process automation-config `mongotHost` → each cluster's LOCAL Envoy, on-disk locality read-back, `$search` index on the source, real `$search` through each cluster's own mongod). Cross-cluster resource-isolation (absence) assertions, state-ConfigMap mapping persistence, and `len`-guards against vacuous-green loops. Sharded: corrected the per-cluster `$search` docstring (mongos share one `additionalMongodConfig` → only cluster-0's data path is exercised) + a `getParameter` read-back making that explicit; isolation + state-CM + guards. Shared helpers extracted to `conftest.py`.
3. **`fix(search)`: retry mongot bootstrap on simulated-MC sharded source** — on the sharded path mongot dials mongos over TLS at startup; when the cross-cluster Istio mTLS mesh hasn't converged, the handshake is terminated far-side, mongot exits 1, and Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOffs it (5-min backoff), consuming the readiness window. Wraps the existing mongot command in a bounded shell retry loop so a transient bootstrap failure no longer trips the crashloop trap. **Gated to simulated-MC + sharded only** — central-MC and single-cluster StatefulSets are byte-identical; no ga-base-owned file touched.

## Notes for review

- No assertions were weakened to make anything pass. Three Go cases that are unreachable through `Reconcile()` (the `-1`→Pending sentinel + Pending-aggregation legs — `resolveClusterMapping` persists the mapping before `buildClusterWorkList`, so every entry is always mapped) were **not faked**; that branch looks vestigial and is flagged for a possible follow-up cleanup.
- The sharded `$search` single-path limitation is structural (MC sharded mongos share one config), documented rather than worked around.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` clean; `go test ./controllers/operator/ ./controllers/searchcontroller/ ./api/mongodb/v1/search/` all `ok` (uncached).
- `py_compile` clean on all touched test files.
- E2E validated in CI (this patch).

### Motivation
- Improve audio quality, stability, and diagnostics for Continuous Mouth Motion rendering and make it easier to isolate issues such as pitch instability, clipping, and distortion.

Wrapped the `apptDays` Set creation logic in a `useMemo` hook in `app/appointments.tsx`.

The `apptDays` calculation involves filtering and mapping the entire `appointments` array to extract active dates for the current month. author: hankhsu1996
body:
## Summary

Adds the first cut of user-defined SystemVerilog functions (tracked as F1 in `docs/progress/functions.md`): value-returning and void functions with `input` by-value arguments, a `return` statement, function-local variables, and calls used both as expression operands and as statements. The work spans every layer from AST lowering to C++ emission and lands single-instance, scalar (integral / packed) functions end to end; output / inout / ref arguments, return-by-name, recursion, managed-type boundaries, and cross-instance access remain tracked as later items.

## Design

A subroutine body is the same shape as a process body, so the two now share a single HIR `ProceduralBody` (statement tree plus its expr / stmt / local arenas). In MIR a subroutine is a callable peer of a process whose body is a `ProceduralScope`; MIR carries only the semantic argument direction and leaves the C++ passing mode to the backend. The cpp backend emits each function as a by-value member function with a native `return`, so C++ value semantics and return-by-value cover argument copy-in and result conveyance with no return-slot or hand-rolled lifecycle. Peer and mutual references resolve by mapping every subroutine's identity before any body is lowered, then composing each lowered decl and adding it once.

## Testing

`bazel test //...` passes, including eight new `function_*` cases covering simple return, parameters, locals, void calls, nested calls, calls in expressions, and early return.

author: vivek7405
body:
Closes #183

## Summary

"Progressive enhancement by default" is webjs's foundational claim, but it was never continuously verified. This adds an e2e layer that loads the blog with JavaScript DISABLED and asserts the no-JS baseline: content reads, an `<a>` link navigates, a `<form>` submits and the server renders the response, and a display-only component renders. A counterfactual proves the harness genuinely disabled JS.

## What changed

1. **A progressive (no-JS) search form on the blog** (`examples/blog/app/search/page.ts` + a `/search` nav link). The blog's existing forms (auth, comments, chat, new-post) are all JS-driven (`@submit` + `fetch`), so the app had no native `<form action method>` to exercise the framework's promise that forms submit with JS off. `/search` is a plain GET form over post titles: with JS the client router fragment-swaps it, with JS off the browser does a full navigation to `/search?q=...` and the server renders the results. This is the canonical no-JS form the test asserts on, and a genuinely useful blog feature.

2. **The JS-disabled e2e layer** (`progressive enhancement (JS disabled) (#183)` in `test/e2e/e2e.test.mjs`). A nested describe runs a second page with `setJavaScriptEnabled(false)`. Because that also disables `page.evaluate`, the block reads the DOM via `page.content()` (HTML serialization, no page JS) and interacts via CDP-level `type`/`click` (real browser input/mouse events). It asserts:
   * Content reads (seeded posts render) AND a display-only component renders its SSR markup (`zero JS shipped for this badge`).
   * An `<a>` nav link performs a full native navigation to `/about`.
   * The `/search` GET form submits (type + click) and the server renders `Found 2 results for "web"`.
   * **Counterfactual**: clicking the interactive counter does NOT increment it with JS off, proving JS is genuinely disabled (so a feature whose first paint or behaviour needed JS would render broken and fail the assertions above rather than passing on a secretly-live page).

## Acceptance criteria

* JS-disabled e2e asserts content reads, links navigate, and a server-rendered form submits on the blog: done (4 tests).
* At least one display-only component renders correct markup with JS off: done (the build-stamp badge).
* Counterfactual: a feature whose first paint depends on JS fails the test: the counter counterfactual proves the harness fails JS-dependent behaviour.

## Test plan

* JS-disabled describe: 4/4 green.
* Full blog e2e suite: **61/61** (the 4 new tests plus the pre-existing 57; the added `/search` nav link in the shared layout does not disturb any other test).

## Summary

- **Root cause**: `str(Path("bandcamp://x"))` on POSIX collapses `//` to `/`, so SQL `WHERE file_path = ?` matched 0 rows for remote tracks — silently breaking favorites, play count, and last-played for all Bandcamp streaming tracks.
- **Fix 1** (`server.py`): `TrackOut.from_track` now uses `_canonical_track_key(t.file_path)` instead of `str(t.file_path)`, so the client always receives and round-trips the correct `bandcamp://` URI.
- **Fix 2 + 3** (`library.py`): `record_track_started` and `record_played` use `_canonical_track_key(file_path)` in their SQL bindings.
- **Fix 4** (`library.py`): New `LibraryIndex.inherit_remote_favorites()` method — called by `LibraryScanner.scan()` after upserting newly-added local files — copies the `favorite` flag from any matching `bandcamp://` row (matched by album + track_number + disc_number), so favorites set on streaming tracks survive an album download.

author: resitch-source
body:
## Root causes

**Bug 1 — Wrong callback signature (primary cause)**
All `panelCallbacks` were calling `onUpdate(entry.id, updatedEntry)` with two arguments, but `onUpdateEntry(updatedEntry)` only accepts one. The string `entry.id` was treated as the updated entry object, so every attachment save was silently discarded.

**Bug 2 — Stale closure in async Drive upload**
After Drive upload completes, `onUpdate` was reading `entry.attachments` captured at render time (before `onAdd` added the new file), so the Drive-updated attachment would overwrite with the old empty array.

## Fix
- Callbacks now call `onUpdate(updatedEntry)` with a single argument
- `entryRef = useRef(entry)` updated every render; async callbacks read `entryRef.current.attachments`
- Both `attached_record` and `examination_record` share `makeAttCallbacks()`

author: raymondjacobson
body:
## Summary

The `claimable_reward` backfill query in `EngagementNotificationsJob` was running ~49 minutes per tick on prod, overrunning its 10-minute schedule ~5x and pinning a DB connection + CPU continuously.

**Root cause.** The Go port collapsed the original Python task's [two-stage dedup](https://github.com/AudiusProject/apps/blob/main/packages/discovery-provider/src/tasks/create_engagement_notifications.py) into a single statement with one correlated `NOT EXISTS`. The planner underestimated the `user_ids` overlap anti-join's selectivity, materialized a full `notification` scan, and nested-loop-anti-joined **every** undisbursed candidate across the ~2-year `completed_at >= '2024-06-06'` window — a ~22-billion-cost plan.

**Fix.** Restore Python's staging explicitly via a `WITH candidates AS MATERIALIZED (...)` CTE:
- **Stage 1** (`candidates`) selects the ≤500 rows via the `uq_notification` index — this mirrors Python's `Notification.id IS NULL` anti-join + `.limit(BATCH_SIZE)`, which the first port dropped in favor of `ON CONFLICT` alone.
- `AS MATERIALIZED` is an optimization fence: it forces those ≤500 rows to be computed **before** the 1-hour overlap debounce runs, instead of the planner re-fusing both anti-joins.
- **Stage 2** runs the debounce against only the materialized candidates.

No schema or behavior change — same rows inserted, same `ON CONFLICT` safety net.

## Measured on prod (read-only EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the SELECT equivalent)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Planner cost | ~21.9 billion | ~18 million |
| Wall time | ~49 min | **~40 s** |

Stage 1 fills in ~1.7s via `Index Only Scan using uq_notification`; the ~38s tail is stage 2 scanning the claimable_reward notifications once for the 500 candidates.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Stage 2 still scans all `claimable_reward` rows because `ix_notification gin(user_ids)` is not type-selective. A partial GIN index `(user_ids) WHERE type = 'claimable_reward'` would turn the debounce into per-user probes (~sub-second), but that's a separate migration with its own index-build/locking considerations.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./jobs/...`
- [x] `go vet ./jobs/`
- [x] `go test ./jobs/ -run TestEngagementNotifications -count=1` (FullPipeline + Exclusions pass)
- [x] Verified improved plan via read-only `EXPLAIN` against the prod write primary

### Motivation
- Provide a way to export and import WaLTER data (roles, users, tournaments, matches, decks, leagues) between instances or for restore purposes. 
- Allow optional password-protected backups to keep sensitive data safe during transfer.
- Surface backup functionality in the admin UI for convenient access.

### Description
- Added backup/export/import backend logic including payload serialization (`export_backup_payload`), optional encryption (`encrypt_backup_payload` / `decrypt_backup_payload`) using `PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256` and `AES-256-GCM`, helpers for encoding/decoding and ISO date parsing, and database apply logic (`apply_backup_payload`).
- Added new admin routes `GET/POST /admin/backup` and `GET/POST /admin/backup/export` and integrated file sending with `send_file` for downloads.
- Added templates and UI changes: new `admin/backup.html`, link in the admin panel (`admin/panel.html`) and navigation (`base.html`) to access the backup tools.
- Included `tests/test_backup.py` to validate export/import flows for both unencrypted and encrypted backups and wired up cryptography imports and constants for iteration counts and formats.

### Testing
- Added and ran the unit tests in `tests/test_backup.py` which exercise export and import for unencrypted backups and for encrypted backups with the correct and missing password cases, and they passed. 
- Verified that exported payloads use the `walter-admin-backup` and `walter-admin-backup-encrypted` formats and include roles, users, tournaments, and matches as expected. 
- Confirmed the encrypted export contains the expected encryption metadata (`AES-256-GCM` + `PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256`) and cannot be imported without the backup password. 
- All new tests executed with `pytest` succeeded.

author: duanbing
body:
## What

Splits the overloaded `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` constant in the Novita provider:

- `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (300s) — stays the **per-HTTP-request** timeout (create-task submit, single poll fetch).
- `ASYNC_TASK_TIMEOUT` (**3600s / 1h**) — new constant, the **total poll-loop deadline** for one async media generation.

## Why

Heavy models (e.g. `sora_2_pro_i2v`) routinely render past the old 300s budget, producing spurious `Novita async task … did not complete within 300s` failures even though the upstream render eventually succeeds.

On the RouterBase side this generation is now **single-attempt, no-retry** (`video_submitter` `MAX_ATTEMPTS=1`), so this is the one and only budget for a request — one upstream Novita task, no throwaway re-submissions spawning fresh task ids.

## Paired change

Requires the RouterBase parent PR that:
- pins this submodule commit,
- sets `MAX_ATTEMPTS=1` and raises the worker reaper above 1h (`STUCK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=70`),
- adds 60s TCP keepalive on the backend→gateway client (the connection sits idle for up to 1h while the gateway polls Novita),
- surfaces in-flight generations in `/logs`.

## Risk

A single submission now holds an **idle** connection to the gateway open for up to 1h. Backend-side keepalive mitigates conntrack/idle drops; worth watching connection counts at high concurrency on first real 1h render.

author: tongqqiu
body:
## Summary

The Snowflake connector (0.5.0) supported **password auth only** — but Snowflake disables single-factor password sign-in on many accounts, so a real programmatic loader at a fintech shop typically **can't connect** without key-pair auth. This adds it as the preferred method, making the connector actually usable for the Target User.

## How it works

Credentials resolve from the environment, key-pair first:

| Env var | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` | PEM private-key file — key-pair auth (recommended) |
| `SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSPHRASE` | passphrase if the key is encrypted (optional) |
| `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD` | password auth — fallback, used only when no key path is set |

The connector passes `private_key_file` / `private_key_file_pwd` to `snowflake.connector.connect` (the driver loads/parses the key — we don't handle key bytes ourselves). Key-pair takes precedence when both a key path and a password are present. Nothing secret is read from `pipeline.yaml`.

## Testing

Unit tests against the fake `snowflake.connector` cover: key-pair precedence over password, passphrase passthrough, password fallback when no key, and the "no credential" error — connector stays at **100% line coverage**. The gated integration test now accepts **either** credential, and the `Snowflake Integration` workflow materializes the PEM key from a `SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY` secret when present.

## Also
Registry descriptor lists both credential env vars; the connectors reference documents key-pair as the recommended method (with the `RSA_PUBLIC_KEY` registration note); CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`.

## Verification
`986 passed, 36 skipped`; lint clean; strict docs build clean.
