author: gwarmstrong
body:
# Add compute_eval benchmark and resource server

Migrates the [`compute-eval`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/compute-eval) benchmark from NeMo Skills into Gym. Uses execution-based verification: model-generated CUDA / C / C++ / Python kernel solutions are compiled with `nvcc` and run against the benchmark's hidden test suite via `compute_eval.execution.evaluate_solutions(eval_mode="local")`.

## Includes

- `resources_servers/compute_eval/` — `nvcc`-compile + hidden-test execution server
  - Wraps the third-party `compute-eval` PyPI package; pins to upstream commit `e01a5d2` (Release 2026.1) for reproducibility
  - `verify()` parses fenced code blocks from the model output via `compute_eval.generate_completions._parse_solution`, validates them as `FileSolution`, then dispatches `evaluate_solutions(problem, [solution], eval_mode="local")` to a single-worker `ThreadPoolExecutor`. The single-thread pin is required because `compute_eval.utils.parsing.find_matching_subtrees` uses a `tree-sitter` Parser that's marked `unsendable` — concurrent calls from rotating asyncio worker threads panic at runtime.
  - `setup_cuda_nvcc.py` auto-installs `cuda-nvcc=12.9 + cuda-cudart-dev=12.9 + cuda-cccl=12.9 + cuda-nvtx-dev=12.9` via `micromamba` into a local prefix at server startup. Two paths only: reuse if `prefix/env/bin/nvcc` exists, otherwise install. To share a single install across consumers (or persist across SLURM jobs via a lustre-mounted prefix), each consumer sets `$COMPUTE_EVAL_CUDA_NVCC_PREFIX` to the same path.
  - `compute_metrics()` exposes `pass@k/accuracy`, `pass@1[avg-of-k]/accuracy`, and `majority@k/accuracy` via `compute_pass_majority_metrics()`; `_score_fn` returns `{"accuracy": passed}` so a single `_score_fn` covers all three.

- `benchmarks/compute_eval/` — benchmark config + dataset preparation
  - Data source: `nvidia/compute-eval` (566 CUDA / C / C++ / Python kernel problems, Release 2026.1)
  - `prepare.py` fetches the per-release problems tarball directly from `https://github.com/NVIDIA/compute-eval` at commit `eede5ce` and emits Gym-shaped JSONL with `problem_prompt`, `build_command`, `context_files_block` substituted into the prompt at rollout time, plus `verifier_metadata.problem` carrying the full discriminated `CudaCppProblem | CudaPythonProblem` record. Sidesteps a `Json`-feature type mismatch between the HF dataset metadata and `datasets >= 4.0`.
  - Prompt: lives at the consolidated `benchmarks/prompts/compute-eval/baseline.yaml`, identical to NeMo Skills' `nemo_skills/prompt/config/compute-eval/baseline.yaml`.
  - Verification: delegates to the `compute_eval` resources server above.

## Validated against NeMo Skills

Validated with `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16`, N=4 rollouts per task × 566 problems = 2264 rollouts per side, temperature=1.0 / top_p=0.95 / max_output_tokens=16384, reasoning parser `deepseek_r1`. Both sides used the same `cuda-nvcc=12.9` toolchain.

```
========================================================================
NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 | N=4 | T=1.0 top_p=0.95
========================================================================
Metric                       Skills        Gym         Delta
-------------------------------------------------------------
pass@1[avg-of-4]            12.77 %     12.90 %       +0.13 pp
pass@4                      19.43 %     19.43 %       +0.00 pp
majority@4                  10.78 %     11.13 %       +0.35 pp
```

Per-task pass@4 agreement on 566 tasks: 544 / 566 = **96.1 %**. The 22 disagreements split **perfectly symmetric** (11 Skills-only, 11 Gym-only) — pure rollout-level sampling noise at temperature 1.0, no directional bias.

`pass@4` is identical to two decimal places. The +0.13 pp `pass@1` delta is well within the ~3–5 pp MoE non-determinism floor typical for these models.

NeMo Skills' `ComputeEvalEvaluator` at HEAD has a bug that silently returned `passed=False` for every problem (PR #1315 renamed `evaluate_solution` → `evaluate_solutions` but kept accessing `.passed` on the now-list return). A small Skills patch (`graded_list[0].passed`, plus a single-thread executor for the same `tree-sitter` reason as Gym) was applied locally to get a usable baseline — without it the comparison would be against `0.0 %` everywhere.

author: kris-anderson
body:
# Fix build on Apple Clang / C23 by pinning to `-std=gnu17`

## Problem

`brew install kris-anderson/netperf/netperf-enable-demo` started failing during `make` with a wall of errors like:

```
nettest_bsd.c:5197:36: error: too many arguments to function call, expected 0, have 4
./netlib.h:679:26: note: 'allocate_buffer_ring' declared here
  679 | extern  struct ring_elt *allocate_buffer_ring();
./hist.h:135:6: error: conflicting types for 'HIST_purge'
```

Nothing in this repo changed — the host toolchain did.

## Root cause

The formula runs `./autogen.sh`, which regenerates `configure` with the current `autoconf`. Modern `autoconf` (2.73) paired with **Apple Clang 21** (Command Line Tools 26) probes for the newest C standard the compiler supports and selects **`-std=gnu23`**, baking it into `CC`.

In **C23, an empty parameter list `()` means `(void)`** — *takes no arguments* — instead of the old K&R "unspecified arguments". Netperf 2.7's headers are full of K&R declarations:

```c
extern struct ring_elt *allocate_buffer_ring();
extern void HIST_purge();
extern void HIST_get_stats();
extern int  HIST_get_percentile();
```

So every call with arguments becomes a hard error (`too many arguments to function call`), and `()` vs `(HIST h)` declarations now "conflict". These are **semantic errors under C23, not warnings** — they can't be silenced with `-Wno-*`. The only fix is to build on a pre-C23 standard.

## Fix

Pass `CFLAGS=-std=gnu17` to `./configure`:

```ruby
system "./configure", "--disable-dependency-tracking",
                      "--enable-demo",
                      "--prefix=#{prefix}",
                      "CFLAGS=-std=gnu17"
```

`gnu17` is the last pre-C23 dialect, so empty-paren K&R declarations compile again (just a benign `-Wdeprecated-non-prototype` warning). Pinning explicitly via `CFLAGS` keeps the build on `gnu17` regardless of which standard the compiler defaults to now or in the future.

## Why this approach

A few options were tested end-to-end through Homebrew; all worked, but this one is the most robust and idiomatic:

| Approach | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ac_cv_prog_cc_c23=no` (configure cache var) | ✅ builds | Relies on clang's *default* staying pre-C23 — would break if a future clang defaults to C23 |
| `CFLAGS=-std=gnu17` to `./configure` **(chosen)** | ✅ builds | Explicitly pins gnu17; survives a future C23 default |
| `make … CFLAGS=-std=gnu17` (make-time) | ✅ builds | Works (wins as the last `-std`), but less conventional |

## Testing

Built and verified from source on macOS (Apple Clang 21, CLT 26, Apple Silicon):

- `brew reinstall --build-from-source kris-anderson/netperf/netperf-enable-demo` → builds in ~17s
- `brew test …` → passes
- `netperf -V` → `Netperf version 2.7.1`
- `netperf -D 0.5 …` → the demo-mode flag is accepted, confirming `--enable-demo` is still compiled in

## Also

- README updated with a note explaining the `-std=gnu17` pin.

author: mann-joshi
body:
### 💡 What
Two targeted micro-optimizations inside `src/game/mahjongLogic.ts`:
1. Switched `computeFreeTiles` from using `Array.prototype.map()` to using a pre-allocated `new Array(length)` with a standard `for` loop.
2. In `getHintPair`, replaced the O(N) array scan occurring inside an O(P) pairs loop with a single O(N) precomputed `Record<string, Tile>` map.

### 🎯 Why
- `computeFreeTiles` is an extremely highly executed hot path (re-run constantly as the board state updates). The `map` implementation forces V8 to allocate closures and dynamically resize arrays. The standard `for` loop mitigates this GC churn.
- `getHintPair` previously exhibited $O(N \times P)$ worst-case complexity by doing a linear array scan to find two tiles per candidate pair. Precomputing a fast look-up dictionary cuts this down to $O(N + P)$.

### 📊 Impact
Measurable reductions in synchronous main thread blocking during hint requests, tile clicks, and automated level clears, reducing overall GC spikes.

### 🔬 Measurement
Tests were verified with `npx jest` and static type checks via `npm run ts-check` all pass. You can measure the improvement by placing timers around `getHintPair` before and after this PR on a complex, fully populated boss level board layout.

body:
## Summary

Clicking a recent-agent row in the Studio/Rovo sidebar nav no longer reorders it to the top of the list.

The recent-agents list is sorted by `lastTouchedAt` descending — there is no explicit "pinned" flag, so "highest" is purely emergent from that timestamp. Selecting an agent ran `selectAgent()` → `touchSessionAgent()`, which wrote `lastTouchedAt: Date.now()` and re-sorted the clicked agent to the top.

This removes the `touchSessionAgent` call from `selectAgent` (in `app/contexts/context-rovo-chat.tsx`). Selection identity is still tracked via `selectedAgentId` (the highlighted row), so the selected styling is unchanged — only list order stays stable.
